title: Nick Bosa breaks extended Twitter silence to express agreement with Ryan Clark's ouster
summary: The story of the week came from ESPN, where a supposed exercise in removing red ink became, for NFL analyst Ryan Clark, more like a Red Wedding. 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has chosen to chime in.
full_text: '' The story of the week came from ESPN, where a supposed exercise in removing red ink became, for NFL analyst Ryan Clark, more like a Red Wedding. 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa has chosen to chime in. In his first actual tweet since November 2022 (he's had a handful of retweets since then without comment), Bosa reposted the original article from The Athletic about Clark's ouster with an “OK” emoji . It's an odd postscript to the (relatively speaking) old news. And while those in the media accept that the public nature of the job will include a public reaction to the job ending, Bosa's tweet is another example of the notion that someone's firing is something to be celebrated on social media. Of course, it happens to players. And while it's usually fans and not media members who pop a cork publicly when the player is cut from his team, it's easy to blur the lines. Especially if the media member in question has a reputation for the kind of candor that will ruffle feathers. There are two general ways to handle these jobs. One, kiss everyone's ass and say everything is great. Two, consistently share honestly-held opinions and beliefs, even if those opinions and beliefs may at times piss people off. The consumers have to ask themselves what they want. If it's incessant, superficial cheerleading, plenty of outlets, shows, and personalities will provide it. There are multiple sports utopias where the approach is to constantly glorify everything (including gambling) and never to directly criticize anyone or anything. There are also platforms where those who spend the bulk of their time focusing on one specific sport share the views they've developed without pulling punches or pretending to believe something they don't. It's not as if Clark took a sudden turn in the way he did the job. He's always been exactly who he is. And that was fine and dandy for ESPN, for more than a decade. Clark didn't change; ESPN's attitude toward him did. And now that ESPN has decided to move on (with the bush-league move of pulling the plug while he was on the air), many are doing a victory lap. It just feels different when a big-name player with no habit of expressing his views on Twitter chooses to fuel the ticker-tape parade. It feels personal. (It may be political.) And while Bosa has every right to do it, it's worth pointing out that he did — and wondering why he chose to do it.
author: Mike Florio

title: George Kittle links lingering Brandon Aiyuk issues to his 2024 contract negotiations
summary: When 49ers tight end George Kittle last addressed receiver Brandon Aiyuk, during a visit with Pardon My Take, he told Commanders fan PFT Commenter, "Have fun with that."
full_text: ''' When 49ers tight end George Kittle last addressed receiver Brandon Aiyuk, during a visit with Pardon My Take , he told Commanders fan PFT Commenter, " Have fun with that ." In a Thursday visit with Chris Simms , Kittle opted not to get into the details about the things that have happened between Aiyuk and the 49ers. However, Kittle strongly hinted that the problems trace to the protracted and difficult contract negotiations between Aiyuk and the 49ers from 2024. "I feel like I know basically everything that's happened and what's gone on, and I can't share all of that, because it's not my business to share or tell," Kittle said. "But . . . I feel like the Niners have done a very good job throughout the entire process and have tried. [Coach] Kyle [Shanahan] has tried. [G.M.] John [Lynch] has tried. Teammates have tried. And this is where we are. And so I think the organization itself has done a really good job. And like I said, I know plenty of things. . . . I don't want to point a finger at anybody, but I've been here for 10 years, and I've been treated with nothing but respect and love my entire career. I feel like I've done it the right way as long as I can." That's the right approach. Kittle and Aiyuk have been teammates for six years. Technically, they still are — even if Aiyuk undoubtedly will never play for the 49ers again (barring a dramatic and unexpected change of heart). Kittle pivoted during his response to the contract issue that bogged down the relationship between Aiyuk and the 49ers. And Kittle's comments make clear his belief that, for Aiyuk, the situation left a wound that never healed. "Contract negotiations are also — those are always hard for everybody," Kittle said. "And you just try your best to not be sensitive about it. But I will say, you know, Richard Sherman gave me advice back in the day when I was going through my first contract negotiation. It was, 'Contracts are like braces. They hurt and they suck the entire time, and then once you get your braces off and you get paid, you don't even remember having them. And it's a great time.' Like, that's kind of the mindset you have to have, and, you know, if you get offended by something, you hold onto it, that's kind of on you, because everybody goes through contract negotiations, and they're all difficult." Regardless of how much sense that makes, something happened that pushed Aiyuk past the point of no return. For him, it was the first real contract negotiation of his pro career. The 49ers do them all the time and, frankly, this creates an obligation to not treat all of them the same. For someone like Kittle, the discomfort of the braces was forgotten immediately. For someone like Aiyuk, the pain and discomfort can't be. Successful coaches have a different approach to coaching different players. Front offices should do the same. Hardball can't be the only game played; for some players, the echoes of chin music never fade away. Whether or not the 49ers had reason to believe Aiyuk would hold a grudge over contentious contract talks is a different issue. As the situation was unfolding two summers ago, however, there was plenty of evidence to support the conclusion that the time had come to move on. And the 49ers had a chance to do it, with a trade to the Steelers teed up before Aiyuk suddenly decided to accept the team's offer. Surely, the 49ers wish they'd gone through with the trade. Even more surely, they've learned from the experience a better way to resolve the next negotiations that turn extra ugly. Or maybe they've learned how to keep the negotiations from getting extra ugly. Especially from the players who won't forget the ugliness.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams unveil their two new alternate uniforms
summary: The Nikefication of the NFL continues.
full_text: ' The Nikefication of the NFL continues. For some teams, it's becoming impossible to keep up with the various helmet, jersey, and pants combinations . For the Rams, who unveiled new base uniforms in April (the drain plug was thankfully pulled on the dirty dishwater option), two alternate uniforms were added on Thursday. They include a look dubbed "Classic Sol," consisting of a yellow jersey and white pants. The uniform honors the team's 1951 NFL Championship team. The other alternate uniform is called "Fearsome White," a nod to the "Fearsome Foursome" of Rosey Grier, Deacon Jones, Lamar Lundy, and Merlin Olsen. The jersey is white, the pants are white, and the helmet logo is white. Then there's the " Midnight Mode " uniform added last year as part of the largely nonsensical "Rivalries" line, a semi-plausible strategy for giving fans another jersey to buy . When Nike assumed the apparel contract in 2012 from Reebook, some (including me) feared that NFL teams eventually would look like Oregon, with a different uniform every week. I'm now starting to wonder when Nike will talk the league into one-upping the Ducks by letting a team change uniforms at halftime.
author: Mike Florio

title: What's next for Diego Pavia?
summary: After failing to win a chance at training camp to secure a spot as one of Lamar Jackson's backups, former Ravens quarterback Diego Pavia has entered the NFL's waiver system.
full_text: After failing to win a chance at training camp to secure a spot as one of Lamar Jackson's backups, former Ravens quarterback Diego Pavia has entered the NFL's waiver system. If unclaimed, what's next? He could choose to wait for another NFL opportunity. Injuries could open a door for Pavia to participate in a training camp as an extra arm, which would in turn give him an opportunity to earn a 53-man roster spot or a position on a practice squad. If there's no NFL interest, Pavia could go to the CFL. The Winnipeg Blue Bombers hold his negotiating rights, and they've made it clear that they are interested . The UFL apparently has interest, too — if the social-media team has its finger on the pulse of the league's priorities. The league retweeted the announcement of Pavia's waiver by the Ravens with the eyes emoji . Then there's college football. While he doesn't fit within the NCAA’s new eligibility rule (he turned 20 the year before his four-year college career began), Pavia could try to sue for another season. He played two years of junior-college football before commencing a four-season NCAA career in four years. With every NCAA rule currently subject to an antitrust challenge, Pavia could give it a shot. Of course, the fact that he signed a contract with the Ravens would make it harder. But he didn't get a signing bonus or a game check; at most, he received the standard per diem for his offseason work. It doesn't hurt to try, and it wouldn't be ridiculously expensive (in theory) to hire a lawyer to file the paperwork and roll the dice. Surely, someone would be interested. Pavia finished second in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting. It's a path to getting more game experience — and to getting paid more than he'd receive in the CFL or the UFL.
author: Mike Florio

title: Quinshon Judkins will have no limitations in Browns' training camp
summary: Judkins had surgery in December for a fractured fibula and dislocated ankle.
full_text: Browns running back Quinshon Judkins' rookie season ended with an ugly injury in December, but it won't affect him in training camp. Judkins is full-go for camp, seven months after surgery to repair his fractured fibula and dislocated ankle, according to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. That's no surprise, as Judkins participated in the offseason program, but clearance for full contact practices was the last step. The Browns took Judkins in the second round of last year's draft, but he didn't sign his rookie contract until September as he faced a misdemeanor battery charge that was eventually dismissed. After missing Week One, Judkins started Week Two and started every game until his injury ended his season in Week 16. Judkins finished his rookie season with 230 carries for 827 yards and seven touchdowns, and he projects to be the Browns' top running back this season.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Texas lineman wins preliminary right return to college football after attending rookie minicamps
summary: The crowd that crows about college football chaos compelling Congressional intervention will love this one, even if it's not much of a surprise.
full_text: The crowd that crows about college football chaos compelling Congressional intervention will love this one, even if it's not much of a surprise. Earlier this week, former Texas offensive lineman Cole Hutson secured a temporary restraining order allowing him to return to college football despite entering the draft, not being picked, participating in the Browns' and Cowboys' rookie minicamps, and not being signed by either team. Via Pete Nakos of On3.com, a Texas judge granted the request for extra-extraordinary relief — one that often is presented and decided without the defendant having a chance to be heard. The next step will be a hearing on a motion for a preliminary injunction, which would extend the TRO through the resolution of the case. It's very hard to secure a TRO. Hutson's success suggests that he'll also get a preliminary injunction at the hearing set for August 3. Hutson's case follows a recent ruling by an Ohio judge granting a preliminary injunction to 24 athletes based on an age-based eligibility model for a fifth year. Hutson has played four years of college football, appearing in 48 games and making 23 starts. While Hutson has yet to rejoin a college program, it appears that Texas would be willing to bring him back. “If it ultimately all goes through, we’re getting a veteran player , right?” Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian said, via Ralph D. Russo of The Athletic . “At the end of the day, there’s nothing like having an experienced player on your team, in your locker room, in the offensive line room. What does the future hold? I don’t know. I haven’t seen Cole. It’s been seven months since the last time we played. So there’s a lot that we have to kind of sort through and unpack. But if we’re fortunate enough to have him back, it’d be great.” The naysayers will claim that the sky is falling, given that Hutson donned an NFL uniform. But he never signed an NFL contract. He was never paid to play pro football. In the recent past, basketball players who had been drafted by the NBA had been permitted to return to college. It's a narrow ruling, applying only to players who fit within the new NCAA eligibility rule. The new standard provides players with five years of eligibility " if they enroll in college no later than the academic year after their 19th birthday ."
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals OL Isaiah Adams practices despite his recent arrest
summary: Cardinals offensive lineman Isaiah Adams, who faces four weapons charges after his recent arrest in Canada, took part in the team's first training camp practice.
full_text: Cardinals offensive lineman Isaiah Adams, who faces four weapons charges after his recent arrest in Canada, took part in the team's first training camp practice. Coach Mike LaFleur would not comment on Adams' legal trouble. "I'm not going to comment too much on that," LaFleur said, via video from Bo Brack of PHNX_Cardinals. "Obviously, I'd appreciate you guys not really asking the questions with that. But he’s doing good , and it was good to see him." Adams was charged with possession of a firearm obtained in a crime, possession of a restricted/prohibited firearm, no license while in possession of a loaded firearm and possessing a prohibited device. His attorney, Adam Weisberg, said in a statement last week that Adams is "completely innocent in this matter." Police concluded an investigation on Friday into a male believed to have a firearm and involved in drug trafficking. Three other people were arrested, including two who were charged with possession of fentanyl with intent to distribute. Adams, who was born in Ajax, Ontario, was a third-round pick of the Cardinals out of Illinois in 2024. He started 11 games last season after starting five as a rookie.
author: Charean Williams

title: Broncos OLB Nik Bonitto: I still have a lot of room to grow in my game
summary: Broncos outside linebacker Nik Bonitto made 13.5 sacks in 2024 and finished ninth in Defensive Player of the Year voting.
full_text: Broncos outside linebacker Nik Bonitto made 13.5 sacks in 2024 and finished ninth in Defensive Player of the Year voting. In 2025, he had 14 sacks and was fourth in Defensive Player of the Year voting. He expects a similar jump from 2025 to 2026 but likely sees even more attention from the opponent. He spent the offseason studying other top pass rushers to see how they dealt with double teams. Bonitto said Thursday he hopes to improve in "all facets" of his game this season. "I still have a lot of room to grow in my game — in the run and in the pass," Bonitto said, via Aric DiLalla of the team website. "Just keep trying to fine-tune these things, keep looking at other guys around the league that are doing it at a high level and seeing how I can put it into my game to continue to be the best player I know I can be." Bonitto might have been even better in two postseason games, forcing two fumbles, including a strip-sack, along with three tackles, a quarterback hit and a tackle for loss. Bonitto's two forced fumbles led to six points in Denver's 33-30 overtime win over the Bills. "It's obviously great when you can do it in the regular season," Bonitto said, "but doing it in the postseason in those big type of moments, it gives you that confidence to know you're supposed to be there, and you can make those types of plays on big stages."
author: Charean Williams

title: Myles Garrett's Cleveland home is on the market for $2.1 million
summary: Usually, news of a player's home being put on the market is the spark for speculation that he may be looking for a new city in which to play.
full_text: ' Usually, news of a player's home being put on the market is the spark for speculation that he may be looking for a new city in which to play. For former Browns defensive end Myles Garrett, the "For Sale" sign has come nearly two months after he was traded to the Rams. Via Kalan Hooks of ESPN, Garrett's home in Wadsworth, Ohio, is available for $2.1 million . Sitting on two acres, the house has five bedrooms, six bathrooms, and 4,300 square feet of living space. (There's no mention of whether it comes with his quarterback graveyard .) The house was built in 2018, a year after Garrett arrived in Ohio as the first overall pick in the draft. To get a similar home in L.A., Garrett will probably need to move the decimal point one space to the right.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike LaFleur: Paris Johnson, Josh Sweat landing on PUP list is "just maintenance"
summary: The Cardinals placed left tackle Paris Johnson and linebacker Josh Sweat on the physically unable to perform list on Thursday, but head coach Mike LaFleur didn't make it sound like either player is going to miss much time during training camp.
full_text: ' The Cardinals placed left tackle Paris Johnson and linebacker Josh Sweat on the physically unable to perform list on Thursday, but head coach Mike LaFleur didn't make it sound like either player is going to miss much time during training camp. LaFleur told reporters that both players are dealing with knee issues and that the Cardinals will "be smart" with them at this point in the calendar. The Cardinals will practice the next four days before taking Monday off and neither player will practice before that rest day, but LaFleur suggested they won't be out much longer. "The Paris thing, that is honestly nothing ," LaFleur said, via the team's website. "It's really just maintenance. He'll be back before you know it. Same thing with Josh. Seeing him, he's fired up to be here. He's in great spirits and feeling good." The Cardinals also placed cornerback Garrett Williams (Achilles) and tight end Tip Reiman (ankle) on the PUP list to open camp.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots agree to terms with TE Jeremiah Franklin
summary: The Patriots agreed to terms with tight end Jeremiah Franklin, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
full_text: The Patriots agreed to terms with tight end Jeremiah Franklin, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports. Franklin worked out for the team on Thursday. The Patriots were thin at the position with Julian Hill out for the season with a knee injury and C.J. Dippre on the active/physically unable to perform list. The team signed tight end Mitch Van Vooren earlier this week. The team will have to make a corresponding move to get Franklin on the roster. Franklin started all 12 games as a senior at Boston College, catching 49 passes for 506 yards and two touchdowns. He appeared in 44 games during his college career, including 30 starts, finishing with 93 receptions for 1,010 yards and six touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jacoby Brissett will practice on Thursday
summary: The Cardinals QB did not take part in the team's offseason program.
full_text: Jacoby Brissett is at Cardinals training camp and the quarterback is not staging a hold-in for the team's first practice. Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters that Brissett will participate in the team's first workout of the summer on Thursday. Brissett skipped the voluntary portion of the team's offseason program and did not participate after reporting to the team's mandatory minicamp last month. Brissett is looking for a revised contract that better reflects his position as the team's likely starter at quarterback to kick off the season. There has been no agreement on a new deal at this point, but LaFleur said at his press conference that talks on that front have been "productive." As long as things remain unresolved on the contract front, there would be a chance that Brissett makes a different decision regarding his practice plans but camp will open with the veteran taking reps along with his fellow quarterbacks Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants put Roy Robertson-Harris, two others on PUP list
summary: Wide receiver Malik Nabers avoided the physically unable to perform list to open Giants training camp, but three of his teammates were less fortunate.
full_text: Wide receiver Malik Nabers avoided the physically unable to perform list to open Giants training camp, but three of his teammates were less fortunate. The team announced that defensive lineman Roy Robertson-Harris, tight end Thomas Fidone, and defensive lineman Sam Roberts were all placed on the list. All three players can be activated at any point during camp, but it will be some time before Robertson-Harris is ready to play. He tore his Achilles during the team's offseason program, so the move to PUP as opposed to injured reserve keeps some hope alive that he can return during the season. Giants rookies reported to training camp on Thursday. The full squad is due to report to the Greenbrier in West Virginia on July 28.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Sweat, Paris Johnson among Cardinals placed on PUP list
summary: The Cardinals added four players to their physically unable to perform list on their first day of training camp.
full_text: The Cardinals added four players to their physically unable to perform list on their first day of training camp. The NFL's daily transaction report shows that left tackle Paris Johnson, linebacker Josh Sweat, cornerback Garrett Williams, and tight end Tip Reiman landed on the list. None of the players will be able to practice as long as they remain on it, but they count against the 90-man roster and can be activated at any point. Sweat was the subject of trade chatter this offseason and he skipped the voluntary portion of the team's offseason work. He returned for mandatory minicamp, but did not participate in any on-field work. The Cardinals picked up their option on Johnson's contract for 2027, but he is eligible for an extension. There's been no word about specific injuries for either player. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur is scheduled to speak with reporters on Thursday afternoon and questions about the outlook for all those will likely be part of the discussion.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper has a court hearing Friday
summary: Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is scheduled for a court hearing on Friday before a Douglas County (Colorado) judge, Mike Klis of 9News reports.
full_text: '' Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper is scheduled for a court hearing on Friday before a Douglas County (Colorado) judge, Mike Klis of 9News reports. Cooper will appear virtually along with his attorney, Harvey Steinberg. The expectation is Cooper’s case will be continued to a later date, which would leave it unresolved before the Broncos report to training camp Tuesday. Cooper was arrested twice in June and faces multiple charges arising from the June 4 incident involving his then-girlfriend. He is charged with second-degree assault, third-degree assault, criminal mischief, violating a protective order and harassment via repeated telephone calls. He sat out minicamp last month in a mutual decision with the team to focus on his personal health and well-being. Klis reports that Cooper recently completed an inpatient counseling, therapy, mental health and overall wellness program that lasted more than a month. Cooper, 28, has 31.5 sacks through the first five seasons of his career, with 27 coming in the past three seasons.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens waive QB Diego Pavia
summary: Undrafted rookie will be available to be claimed by another team.
full_text: '' With training camp approaching, the Ravens had five quarterbacks on the 90-man roster. They now have four. Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Ravens have waived rookie quarterback Diego Pavia. Undrafted in April, Pavia signed with the Ravens. The contract contained no signing bonus or guarantees . Pavia finished the offseason program with the Ravens. He'll now be subject to the waivers system. If not claimed, he'll become a free agent again. Remaining on the roster for the Ravens are quarterbacks Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley, Skylar Thompson, and Joe Fagnano.
author: Mike Florio

title: Browns place DT Maliek Collins on PUP list
summary: The Browns have made a roster move with training camp set to begin soon.
full_text: The Browns have made a roster move with training camp set to begin soon. Cleveland announced defensive tackle Maliek Collins has been placed on the active/physically unable to perform list. Collins suffered a season-ending quad injury in Week 13 of last season. He was placed on injured reserve in early December. The Browns will be able to take Collins off of the PUP list whenever he is medically cleared if he’s healthy during training camp. Collins signed a two-year deal with Cleveland during the 2025 offseason. In his first year with the club, the veteran defensive tackle tallied 6.5 sacks with seven tackles for loss and 13 quarterback hits in his 12 games.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panthers sign TE Caden Prieskorn
summary: The Panthers agreed to terms with outside linebacker Cam Gill earlier Thursday.
full_text: '' The Panthers agreed to terms with outside linebacker Cam Gill earlier Thursday. They filled an open roster spot later in the day by signing free agent tight end Caden Prieskorn. Prieskorn, 26, spent time with the Lions and Broncos during training camp in 2025. He was briefly on the practice squad of the Bucs and then the Browns. Cleveland signed Prieskorn to a futures contract but cut him May 19. He played college ball at Ole Miss and Memphis and was offensive MVP of the 2023 Peach Bowl after catching 10 passes for 136 yards and two touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins place CBs Darrell Baker Jr., Storm Duck on active/PUP
summary: The Dolphins placed cornerbacks Darrell Baker Jr. and Storm Duck on the active/physically unable to perform list, the team announced Thursday.
full_text: The Dolphins placed cornerbacks Darrell Baker Jr. and Storm Duck on the active/physically unable to perform list, the team announced Thursday. Baker's injury is unknown, while Duck is recovering from a season-ending knee injury in an Oct. 26 game against the Falcons. Baker signed with the Dolphins in March after playing all 17 games with the Titans the past two seasons. He played 724 defensive snaps and 115 on special teams in 2025 and totaled 55 tackles and seven passes defensed. In his career, which includes two seasons with the Colts, Baker has appeared in 51 career games, with 25 starts. He has recorded 123 tackles, 19 passes defensed and one fumble recovery. Duck has appeared in 16 games with four starts in two seasons with Miami (2024-25), recording 34 tackles and five passes defensed. He entered the NFL as an undrafted college free agent with Miami in 2024 out of Louisville.
author: Charean Williams

title: Titans place JC Latham, Amani Hooker on PUP list
summary: The Titans have made a series of roster moves on Thursday as they get set to begin training camp.
full_text: '' The Titans have made a series of roster moves on Thursday as they get set to begin training camp. Tennessee announced offensive tackle JC Latham and safety Amani Hooker have been placed on the physically unable to perform list. Reporter Paul Kuharsky noted both Latham and Hooker have short-term injuries and are expected to be on the field soon. During training camp, players on PUP can be taken off the list at any time. Additionally, the Titans signed offensive tackle Zachary Thomas and waived offensive tackle Ryan Hayes. Rookies reported to Tennessee’s training camp on Thursday with veterans slated to be in next Tuesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Panthers LB Nic Scourton diagnosed with torn ACL after practice injury
summary: Scourton will get a second opinion but is expected to miss the entire 2026 season.
full_text: Panthers linebacker Nic Scourton is expected to miss the entire season after injuring his knee on the practice field today. Scourton has been diagnosed with a torn ACL, according to NFL Network. The report says Scourton will seek a second opinion, but barring something surprising, he'll have surgery and begin a long rehab process to get ready to play in 2027. Reporters on the scene said Scourton and teammates were emotional as he was carted off the practice field, and it was clear that he had suffered a serious injury. The 21-year-old Scourton was a second-round draft pick last year and had a promising rookie season for the Panthers, starting eight games in 2025.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon will present Adam Vinatieri at Hall of Fame induction
summary: Adam Vinatieri began his career with the Patriots and played 10 seasons in New England, but he left and went to the Colts for 14 more.
full_text: Adam Vinatieri began his career with the Patriots and played 10 seasons in New England, but he left and went to the Colts for 14 more. Not surprisingly, Vinatieri has chosen someone from the Colts to present him at the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Vinatieri would have asked late owner Jim Irsay if the former kicker had gone in as a first-ballot Hall of Famer in 2025. Instead, Irsay's daughter, Colts principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, will get the honors at the Aug. 8 enshrinement. "It means a lot to me, but also potentially means a lot for her being the fact she's the new owner. This is the right thing to do," Vinatieri told Mike Chappell of Fox 59. Jim Irsay died May 21, 2025, at 65. Vinatieri will join Jan Stenerud and Morten Andersen as the only exclusive kickers to have a bust in Canton. He was clutch in the playoffs for the Patriots and the Colts, winning four Super Bowls while going 56-of-69.
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers agree to terms with OLB Cam Gill after Nic Scourton's injury
summary: The Panthers lost outside linebacker Nic Scourton to a right knee injury in the team's first training camp practice on Thursday.
full_text: The Panthers lost outside linebacker Nic Scourton to a right knee injury in the team's first training camp practice on Thursday. They didn't waste any time bringing in a replacement on the roster. The Panthers have agreed to terms with Cam Gill, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports. Gill, 28, played for the Panthers in 2024, totaling 22 tackles and four quarterback hits in 10 games. Gill most recently played for the United Football League's Louisville Kings. He recorded a league-best 11 sacks in 10 games and won the league's 2026 Defensive Player of the Year. He has played 50 regular-season games in his career with the Bucs and Panthers, totaling 51 tackles and 2.5 sacks.
author: Charean Williams

title: Giants WR Malik Nabers is expected to avoid PUP list
summary: The question remains about when Malik Nabers will return from rehab on his right knee, with the Giants hopeful he can play the season opener against the Cowboys.
full_text: '' The question remains about when Malik Nabers will return from rehab on his right knee, with the Giants hopeful he can play the season opener against the Cowboys. The Giants wide receiver, though, is expected to avoid the active/physically unable to perform list to start camp, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports. The Giants surely will be deliberate in Nabers' return, but all eyes will be on him during training camp. Nabers tore the ACL in his right knee in Week 4 against the Chargers and underwent surgery Oct. 28. He required a second surgery this offseason to remove scar tissue after Nabers experienced stiffness. Coach John Harbaugh has said that Nabers' knee injury was "not simple." The 2024 first-round pick totaled 18 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns last season.
author: Charean Williams

title: UFL MVP Jack Plummer to work out for 49ers, Dolphins
summary: The 49ers and Dolphins will be taking a look at the UFL's best player in 2026.
full_text: The 49ers and Dolphins will be taking a look at the UFL's best player in 2026. Per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, Jack Plummer will work out for San Francisco on Friday and Miami next week. Plummer is the UFL's reigning MVP, having won it for his season with the Orlando Storm. He led the UFL with 2,188 passing yards while tossing 17 touchdowns with just one interception in 10 games. Plummer previously spent time with the Panthers after going undrafted in 2024. He was waived by the team during roster cuts last year.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jonathan Jones leaves CBS to become "senior writer" at The Athletic
summary: The "advanced talks" have advanced all the way to a done deal.
full_text: The " advanced talks " have advanced all the way to a done deal. Jonathan Jones announced on Thursday that he has left CBS . The Athletic separately announced that Jones will become a " senior writer " covering the NFL. Per the item posted by The Athletic , "Jonathan will focus on bringing behind-the-scenes stories to the forefront, breaking news and capturing game moments with deeply reported articles and video analysis." Jones had worked for CBS since 2019. The Athletic has not yet filled its "NFL Insider" role following the abrupt resignation of Dianna Russini in April, a week after photos emerged of Russini with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel at a resort in Arizona. ( The Athletic also has not yet concluded its internal investigation regarding Russini's reporting.) It's possible, if not likely, that The Athletic will not have an "NFL Insider" in the sense that the job has evolved. Frankly, it would be difficult if not impossible for an "NFL Insider" to do the job competitively while also complying with the high journalistic standards of the New York Times , which apply by extension to The Athletic . Throw in the lingering newsroom tensions regarding the perception that The Athletic is held to a lower bar, and it arguably makes no sense to have an employee in a role that necessitates the kind of relationships that the Times would regard as actual or apparent conflicts of interest.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dave Canales: Jonathon Brooks looks like "guy that I remember"
summary: The first day of Panthers training camp saw running back Jonathon Brooks on the practice field.
full_text: ''' The first day of Panthers training camp saw running back Jonathon Brooks on the practice field. That's a significant development for the 2024 second-round pick. Brooks made a late debut as a rookie because he was recovering from a torn ACL and his run ended when he tore the same ACL again in his third game. Brooks missed all of last season while recovering and said in April that he was feeling close to 100 percent after an extended rehab period. On Thursday, head coach Dave Canales said Brooks resembled the player that the team was so high on when he came out of Texas. "Really looking forward to, just the hard work that JB has had to do over the last couple of years to get him to this point ," Canales said, via the team's website. "He feels great. He feels strong. He looks fast; he looks like the guy that I remember, and I'm really excited for that. But more so just, for a guy to go through things and to be able to have the emotional and mental resiliency to go through that training twice, to get himself back, this is a celebration, and you can feel the gratitude in him; you can feel the focus and how important this opportunity is for him." The Panthers have Chuba Hubbard and Trevor Etienne back from last year's team, but Rico Dowdle moved on to Pittsburgh after leading the team in rushing and that should leave the door open for Brooks to grab a share of the backfield work if he continues to impress the coaching staff.
author: Josh Alper

title: Fernando Mendoza signs rookie contract
summary: Mendoza is now officially a Raider with his fully guaranteed, four-year rookie deal.
full_text: ' With rookies reporting to training camp on Thursday, the Raiders have taken care of an important piece of business. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza has signed his rookie contract, the team announced. " Let’s get this thing rolling ," Mendoza said in a video released by the team on social media. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network notes Mendoza's deal is worth $57.27 million, fully guaranteed. The Raiders also hold a fifth-year option on the first-round pick. Mendoza's signing should clear the way for Rams quarterback Ty Simpson and Steelers quarterback Drew Allar to also sign their rookie deals. Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck agreed to terms on his four-year rookie contract earlier this week.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Dave Canales confirms Nic Scourton suffered knee injury, will undergo MRI
summary: Panthers outside linebacker Nic Scourton did suffer a right knee injury during the club’s first training camp practice on Thursday, head coach Dave Canales confirmed in his press conference after the session.
full_text: Panthers outside linebacker Nic Scourton did suffer a right knee injury during the club’s first training camp practice on Thursday, head coach Dave Canales confirmed in his press conference after the session. “ They’re going to look at that and get some imaging , and we’ll let you know once we have more [information],” Canales said. While the nature of the injury appeared serious given that Scourton was emotional as he was carted off the field, Canales did not want to speculate on its severity. “I’m hoping for the best,” Canales said. “So, we’ll just get the full imaging before we make any announcements that way.” If it turns out that Scourton will be out for a lengthy period, Canales noted he has confidence in the club’s group of edge rushers. “We’ve got guys,” Canales said. “That’s why we keep bringing in depth, and talent, and different guys. You know, Jaelen Phillips is in that room, Pat Jones is back, Princely Umanmielen is coming along. “We’ve got a whole group of guys that we’re counting on. So, if it comes to that, we have guys that we trust and are going to ask to do different things. But let’s hold off on that until we know what’s going on.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: ESPN, NFL Network announce plans for "Back Together Weekend"
summary: ESPN, if you haven't heard, is making plenty of changes in the aftermath of the April 1 takeover of NFL Network.
full_text: ''' ESPN, if you haven't heard, is making plenty of changes in the aftermath of the April 1 takeover of NFL Network. One thing has remained the same. The two networks are partnering on a continuation of "Back Together Weekend." Of course, it wasn't an NFL Network initiative. The league tried to make it into a thing several years ago. It hasn't really established the full-fledged footing that had been envisioned. But they're still doing it. This year, it's the weekend of August 1 and 2. All camps will be open, and the Hall of Fame game will happen the following Thursday. It starts at 9:00 a.m. ET on August 1, with a three-hour edition of NFL Live on ESPN. Which means that NFL Live won the internal rock-paper-scissors competition with NFL Network's Good Morning Football . At noon ET, coverage of "Back Together Weekend" shifts to NFL Network until 5:00 p.m. ET. On Sunday, it's NFLN only from 10 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. ET. The announcement comes two days after ESPN implemented massive layoffs impacting numerous recognizable on-air names. And the timing of the press release underscores the reality that the date for the implementation of the belt tightening was carefully and strategically selected to fall between ESPYs week and the official disclosure of the various assignments for "Back Together Weekend." Which becomes an ironic label, to say the least, given recent events.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals' Jacoby Brissett to participate in training camp amid contract talks, ends offseason hold-in
summary: Brissett did not practice during the mandatory minicamp while seeking an extension
full_text:
There will be no training camp hold-in or holdout for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett as he continues to negotiate with the team on a new contract. Coach Mike LaFleur said Thursday that Brissett will practice on the first day of camp even though the sides have yet to reach a potential agreement on an extension.
Brissett's attendance is significant considering he sat out of most of the Cardinals' offseason program . It was not until the mandatory minicamp that the veteran reported to the team facility , but even then, he conducted a hold-in as a non-participant in practices.
When the Cardinals released Kyler Murray and elected not to replace their longtime starter with a free agent, Brissett became the de facto No. 1 option in the group. He started 12 games in 2025 when Murray sat due to a severe mid-foot sprain, making him the incumbent starter in a group that also includes journeyman backup Gardner Minshew and rookie third-round pick Carson Beck .
That role promotion from a No. 2 to the projected full-time starter is the crux of Brissett's demand for an extension. He is in the second year of a two-year, $12.5 million contract, which gives him just the 32nd-largest average annual value at the quarterback position and places him behind multiple backups in scheduled earnings.
As the presumptive leader of a team that will rely heavily on him to avoid finishing with one of the NFL's worst records, Brissett seeks to be valued more in line with fellow starters across the league.
"Still ongoing," LaFleur said of the contract talks. "It's been productive between us and his team."
Limiting Brissett's leverage in the negotiations is that the Cardinals have not officially named him the starter. When given the opportunity to do so on Thursday, LaFleur declined to say whether he is conducting an open competition or if the job belongs to Brissett.
"I'd describe it as Practice 1 on July 23," LaFleur said.
Arizona could instead turn to Minshew, given that he holds 47 career starts and has been serviceable in stretches throughout his seven-year run with five different teams. The franchise also made a notable investment in Beck in selecting him in the third round, and it may want to see what the rookie can make of playing time. That the Cardinals figure to be well outside the playoff hunt gives them the latitude to hand the keys to Beck and determine whether he is a worthy building block for the future.
Still, Brissett likely gives the Cardinals the best chance to be competitive. Even though he went 1-11 as a starter last year, most of the team's woes fell on the defense's shoulders. Brissett himself ranked first in the NFL in completions, tied for third in passing touchdowns and third in total passing yards over the final nine weeks of the regular season.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Ravens cut Diego Pavia from Lamar Jackson's QB room before start of training camp
summary: Pavia already lost his shot at being the Ravens' QB3 behind Jackson and former Pro Bowler Tyler Huntley
full_text:
Diego Pavia's stay with the Baltimore Ravens didn't last long. After signing the 2025 Heisman Trophy runner-up as an undrafted free agent out of Vanderbilt on May 1, the Ravens waived him 83 days later on Thursday, just one day before rookies were set to report to Baltimore's training camp.
We have waived QB Diego Pavia. https://t.co/Q1wbCbkwLe
Pavia was in the mix to compete for the third spot on Baltimore's quarterback depth chart behind two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson and former Pro Bowler Tyler Huntley . Pavia's competition for that spot was 2022 seventh-round pick Skylar Thompson and 2026 undrafted free agent Joe Fagnano out of Connecticut. There's a good chance the Ravens won't carry more than Jackson and Huntley on the 53-man roster during the 2026 season, with the third quarterback spending most of their time on the team's practice squad. Baltimore will likely divide up the majority of their preseason game reps between those two quarterbacks.
The 2025 Heisman runner-up led the Commodores to their first 10-win season in school history while setting single-season school records for wins, passing yards (3,539) and passing touchdowns (29). He ranked second in college football in total yards per game (338.5) and tied for third in the sport in total touchdowns (39). Pavia's 119 career total touchdowns and 88 career passing touchdowns both led college football since 2022. At his size (5-foot-10, 203 pounds), sticking around the NFL will be an uphill battle for the 24-year-old rookie. That's especially true for NFL teams that could view him as not worth the time, given the potential distraction factor he brings. Pavia posted an expletive-filled image about the Heisman voters after he lost out on the award to Fernando Mendoza before eventually apologizing for doing so .
So where could Pavia's next landing spots be? Here are a few potential options.
The New York Jets have one of the worst quarterback rooms in the entire NFL. Geno Smith , who will turn 36-years-old during the 2026 season, is likely to be the team's Week 1 starter just a year removed from becoming the sixth quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to lead the league in both interceptions and sacks taken in the same season. Behind Smith are 2026 fourth-round pick Cade Klubnik and two veterans: Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe .
The Jets are playing for the future in 2026, aiming to snag a franchise quarterback in the loaded 2027 NFL Draft . Why not give Pavia a turn to see if he can hang at the NFL level? There's a good chance he can be a solid co-captain of New York's tank brigade in 2026.
Winnipeg has owned Pavia's Canadian Football League negotiating rights since 2024, and they may be in a position to make good on those rights with the popular 2025 SEC Offensive Player of the Year this offseason. Regardless of physical stature, Pavia would immediately become one of the CFL's most talented quarterbacks.
Obviously, Pavia will look to secure some form of football employment for the fall, whether that's an NFL practice squad or a spot in the CFL. However, the UFL in the spring of 2027 would make plenty of sense for him. It's a chance to receive immediate playing time while suiting up alongside other players just on the fringe of making the NFL. This is where he'll likely find the most talented teammates outside of the NFL itself. Plus, he's a big name who could juice the UFL's TV ratings.
If Pavia is unable to find a football landing spot for the fall, he could quickly navigate into the world of podcasting and social media. He has both a big personality and a sizable Instagram following of 112,000. Plus, he has relationships with comedian Theo Von and others in the entertainment industry. That could add up to a comfortable post-football life if Pavia feels his playing days are over.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Panthers' Nic Scourton suffers torn ACL on first day of NFL training camp
summary: The Panthers' pass rush takes a massive hit on Day 1 of training camp as a promising second-year defender is carted off with an ACL tear
full_text:
The reigning NFC South champion Carolina Panthers opened up training camp on Thursday, but the excitement was quickly halted when an expected starter suffered a serious injury.
Pass rusher Nic Scourton suffered a torn ACL, and will miss the entire 2026 season, per ESPN. Scourton went down with a knee injury team drills, and was carted off the field. Cameron Wolfe reported it appeared to be a significant injury, and that teammates around him were emotional with their frustration. The Charlotte Observer reported that Scourton was not putting pressure on his right knee.
Panthers head coach Dave Canales confirmed to reporters after practice that Scourton suffered a right knee injury and that he had to undergo additional testing before they discuss the severity of the issue.
No details on Nic Scourton’s injury (other than the fact that it’s a right knee injury). He will go for imaging this afternoon, per HC Dave Canales. #Panthers pic.twitter.com/HhnYGHFH62
Scourton was slated to be the starting pass rusher opposite free-agent addition Jaelan Phillips . The former No. 51 overall pick out of Texas A&M in the 2025 NFL Draft tied Derrick Brown for the team lead in sacks as a rookie with five despite making just eight official starts. Scourton also recorded 47 tackles, seven tackles for loss, nine QB hits, one pass defensed and a forced fumble in 17 total games played.
Princely Umanmielen and Patrick Jones II are two names that could step up in Scourton's place. Umanmielen was a third-round pick of Carolina out of Ole Miss last year. He didn't make any official starts in 2025, but recorded 24 tackles and 1.5 sacks in 16 games played as a rookie. Jones signed with the Panthers last offseason following four years with the Minnesota Vikings , but played in just four games before he was shut down for the year with a back injury. In those four outings, Jones recorded nine tackles and one sack.
Despite an 8-9 final record that resulted in a division title, there was optimism surrounding the Panthers this year. The front office spent big money on the defensive side of the ball, signing Phillips to a four-year, $120 million deal -- which was the largest free-agent contract handed out by any team this offseason. The Panthers also added one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL in Devin Lloyd , who agreed to a three-year, $42 million contract after a career year with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Still, Scourton is a major loss.
The Panthers' pass-rush room is not the deepest, and with training camp just beginning, general manager Dan Morgan could look outside the building for some help.
There's a former Panther on the market looking for a new home right now, as Jadeveon Clowney remains one of the top free-agent pass rushers available. In 13 games with six starts for the Dallas Cowboys last year, Clowney recorded 41 tackles, 8.5 sacks and 10 QB hits. CBS Sports' Zachary Pereles has called him " the perfect training camp signing ," as Pro Football Focus rated the former No. 1 overall pick as a top-20 EDGE last year with the 16th-best pass rush grade. Among nearly 200 players with at least 200 snaps as a pass rusher, Clowney ranked fourth in pressure rate (19.1%) behind stars like Micah Parsons , Nik Bonitto and Will Anderson Jr . Current Panther Jaelan Philips ranked fifth.
Clowney, a Rock Hill native and former South Carolina star, spent 2024 with the Panthers. In 14 starts, he recorded 46 tackles, 5.5 sacks, 11 QB hits and four passes defended.
We'll keep the former Panther train going here with Haason Reddick . He spent one season with Carolina back in 2021 and racked up 68 tackles, 11 sacks and 18 QB hits. The 31-year-old two-time Pro Bowler is coming off a disappointing season with the rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers , in which he got to the quarterback just 2.5 times in 13 games played. Obviously, the Matt Rhule connection is now gone, but the Panthers could entice him to Charlotte with an opportunity to start immediately.
There are some other big names still available worth mentioning, but they are older and/or on the verge of retirement.
Joey Bosa , who led the NFL in forced fumbles with five last season during his one year with the Buffalo Bills , is said to have " more likely than not " played his last NFL snap, per Adam Schefter. The former No. 3 overall pick and Defensive Rookie of the Year has made five Pro Bowls, and turned 31-years-old earlier this month.
Former Super Bowl MVP Von Miller is now 37-years-old. He played 17 games with three starts for the Washington Commanders last year and recorded nine sacks. He's more of a rotational player at this stage of his career, but can still provide some juice off the edge.
Kyle Van Noy enjoyed three solid seasons with the Baltimore Ravens , including a Pro Bowl campaign in 2024 in which he racked up 12.5 sacks. Now 35, he's a free agent looking for a new contract.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Agent's Take: How high can Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson take a resurgent RB market?
summary: After years of depressed salaries, the running back market has rebounded with deals for Christian McCaffrey, Saquon Barkley and others
full_text:
The running back market had taken an economic downturn until Christian McCaffrey signed a two-year, $38 million contract extension averaging $19 million per year with the San Francisco 49ers during the 2024 offseason. McCaffrey was already the NFL's highest-paid running back with a four-year extension, averaging $16 million per year, which he received from the Carolina Panthers in 2020. He remained the only running back legitimately averaging more than $14 million per year under the 2024 extension.
Saquon Barkley became the league's first $20 million running back in 2025 when he signed a two-year, $41.2 million extension with the Philadelphia Eagles . The deal had a then-record-high $36 million in fully guaranteed compensation at signing.
Derrick Henry subsequently signed a two-year, $30 million extension averaging $15 million per year with the Baltimore Ravens despite his high mileage and being 31 years old. Barring an injury, it was a certainty that Henry would easily eclipse the 2,500-career-carry mark during the 2025 season.
Three running backs landed deals for more than $14 million per year this offseason. Kenneth Walker III signed a three-year, $43 million contract worth up to $45 million through incentives with the Kansas City Chiefs as an unrestricted free agent. Breece Hall , who was kept off the open market by a $14.3 million franchise tag, signed a three-year, $43.5 million deal worth a maximum of $45.75 million through incentives to stay with the New York Jets .
De'Von Achane received a four-year, $64 million extension with $32 million in guarantees from the Miami Dolphins . Incentives make the deal worth up to $68 million. At $16 million per year, Achane is the NFL's third-highest-paid running back.
Six running backs make more than $14 million per year. There could be as many as nine by the time the regular season starts in early September.
Jonathan Taylor has entered the final year of a three-year, $42 million extension with the Indianapolis Colts , signed early in the 2023 regular season after acrimonious negotiations in which he requested a trade. He is likely looking for a new deal near the top of the running back market.
Taylor probably thinks his place in the running back salary hierarchy shouldn't be any lower in a new deal than in 2023. For all practical purposes, Taylor was the NFL's second-highest-paid running back. Alvin Kamara's $15 million-per-year extension with the New Orleans Saints included a fifth new contract year worth $25 million for cosmetic purposes, artificially inflating his average yearly salary. The deal averaged $12.5 million per year through the first four new years. Doing the same thing would mean Taylor getting more than McCaffrey's $19 million per year.
Taylor was coming off an injury-plagued 2022 season in which he rushed for a then-career-low 861 rushing yards while dealing with a terrible economic climate for running backs, when he got the $14 million-per-year deal. That isn't the case this time around.
Taylor was selected to the Pro Bowl for the third time in his six NFL seasons in 2025. He was also named first-team All-Pro by The Sporting News, one of the three media outlets approved by the NFL collective bargaining agreement for honors incentives. Taylor was third in the NFL with 1,585 rushing yards last season. He led the league with 20 total touchdowns (18 rushing and two receiving).
Taylor will be a prime candidate for a franchise tag if he doesn't sign a new deal. It will cost the Colts $18.7 million, given how the prior year's salary provisions work with franchise tags. That's 120% of Taylor's $15.562 million 2026 cap number.
Jahmyr Gibbs and/or Bijan Robinson should reset the running market when signing new deals. Both are dual-threat, former first-round running backs.
Robinson led the NFL with 2,298 yards from scrimmage (combined rushing and receiving yards) last season. It was the 12th-best single-season mark in NFL history. He also earned first-team All-Pro honors for the first time. Gibbs recorded the league's fifth-most yards from scrimmage (1,839) in 2025. He earned Pro Bowl honors on the original ballot for the second straight year.
Since the Detroit Lions are more proactive than the Atlanta Falcons with contract extensions for first-round picks, Gibbs seems more likely to get a new deal this year. The Lions have a recent track record of signing first-round picks to early contract extensions. Offensive tackle Penei Sewell and wide receiver Jameson Williams got new deals after their third NFL seasons in 2024 and 2025, respectively. Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson's extension came during the middle of his fourth year last season.
Typically, the Falcons give first-round picks new deals after their fourth NFL season. That's what happened in recent seasons with guard Chris Lindstrom , cornerback A.J. Terrell and wide receiver Drake London . Kyle Pitts , 2021's fifth overall pick, played out his five-year rookie contract and was designated a franchise player in February before signing a deal making him the NFL's third-highest-paid tight end at $17.7 million per year in June.
Gibbs and Robinson should be looking to become the NFL's first $25 million-per-year running backs, which would represent a dramatic market increase. Getting to that mark would be 21.36% more than Barkley's $20.6 million per year.
Coach Dan Campbell hasn't done the Lions any favors with his public comments about Gibbs. He said Gibbs is just scratching the surface of his talent and is an offensive weapon rather than just a runner at the NFL's annual owners meeting in late March. Gibbs should be poised for a career year with the Lions. Campbell acknowledged in June that Gibbs will be the bell cow running back with David Montgomery's trade to the Houston Texans in March. Gibbs' camp will surely try to use Campbell's comments to their advantage in contract talks.
Something Gibbs and Robinson could focus on is how first-round running backs who got new deals after three years were treated in their respective negotiations. Todd Gurley , Ezekiel Elliott and McCaffrey became the league's highest-paid running backs in 2018, 2019 and 2020.
Elliott's $15 million-per-year extension equates to just over $24 million per year in the current $301.2 million salary cap environment. McCaffrey's 2020 deal, adjusted for salary cap inflation, is little more than $24.3 million per year. Gurley's $14.4 million per year, when factoring in the 69.98% increase in the salary cap since 2018, is nearly $24.5 million per year.
Gurley, in particular, can be viewed as a cautionary tale for big-money extensions with first-round running backs. The Rams released Gurley in 2020 following a lackluster 2019 campaign in which he rushed for 857 yards, his career low at that time, while being slowed by left knee troubles. Gurley didn't play any of his new-contract years, since his four-year extension ran from 2020 through 2023. He made out like a bandit from the deal. Gurley was $20 million better off from the extension than playing out his rookie contract.
Another reference point is the running back market moving by an average of 11.2% the last three times a new salary benchmark was set. Barkley's deal was 8.42% more than McCaffrey's. McCaffrey bettered his 2020 extension by 18.63% in 2024. The 2020 extension was 6.77% more than Elliott's contract. Applying this 11.2% increase to Barkley's $20.6 million per year would be almost $23 million per year.
Regardless of how much Gibbs and Robinson ultimately raise the financial bar for running backs, expect the deals to have significantly more than Barkley's $36 million fully guaranteed at signing. There's a quirk with running back salary guarantees because of the Arizona Cardinals selecting Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft .
Since first-round rookie contracts are fully guaranteed and strictly determined by draft position, Love's $53 million is the most guaranteed money ever in a running…
author: Joel Corry

title: 2026 NFL Draft first-round pick contract tracker: Fernando Mendoza signs deal with Raiders
summary: A rundown of the rookie contracts for the first-round picks of the 2026 class
full_text:
The 2026 NFL Draft is a thing of the past, and now it's time for the 257 selected players to join their teams by signing rookie contracts. Rookies can participate in minicamps and other offseason activities while not under contract, but once training camp rolls around, they need to be under contract to avoid complications.
Complications do indeed happen. Signing a rookie deal is usually a formality, with the rookie wage scale from the 2011 NFL Collective Bargaining Agreement laying out non-negotiable salary slots for the rookie wage scale. Still, there are a few instances in which things get sticky -- Shemar Stewart last offseason stands out as one such example -- and as such, it's worth keeping track of who has officially signed and who hasn't.
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza became the penultimate first-rounder to ink his deal, leaving Los Angeles Rams signal-caller Ty Simpson as the only unsigned player of the bunch. The Rams open training camp on July 25, so the clock is ticking on the Alabama product.
Below is the contract status for all 32 first-round picks, with all salary numbers via Spotrac .
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL's most overrated quarterbacks revealed, plus ranking every first-round draft pick since 2020
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for July 23
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Thursday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
I hope you enjoy the next four days of your life, because starting Tuesday, football will be everywhere. That's July 28, and it's a magic date in the NFL this year because it's when 26 of the 32 teams report to training camp. The other six teams have either already started training camp ( Cardinals , Panthers ) or will be starting this weekend ( Rams , 49ers , Seahawks , Patriots ). That means all 32 teams will be in camp by Tuesday.
This is the weekend to tell your family you love them and that you'll see them in February, but before you do, make sure you sign them up for this newsletter . Anyway, we've got a lot to get to today, so let's get to the rundown.
If you're a Bears or Broncos fan who needs something to get mad about this weekend, Garrett Podell has you covered. Garrett put together a list of the most overrated quarterbacks in the NFL right now, and let's just say, there's a good chance that Garrett is going to be getting a lot of angry messages from fans in Denver and Chicago over the next few days.
Let's check out the top two names on Garrett's list of overrated quarterbacks.
If you want to see Podell's full list of overrated quarterbacks, you can do so here (in that same story, he also listed a few underrated quarterbacks, so be sure to check it out).
There have been 191 first-round picks made so far this decade, and the only reason I know that is that Mike Renner decided to rank EVERY SINGLE ONE OF THEM this week.
This ranking starts with the 2020 NFL Draft and goes through the 2025 draft (Renner didn't include the 2026 draft since we haven't seen those players on the field yet).
Let's take a look at the top five first-rounders since 2020:
1. Bengals QB Joe Burrow (No. 1 overall in 2020) 2. Patriots QB Drake Maye (Third overall in 2024) 3. Vikings WR Justin Jefferson (22nd overall in 2020) 4. Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba (20th overall in 2023) 5. Packers QB Jordan Love (26th overall in 2020)
Six of the top 10 players came from the 2020 draft, so it's pretty clear that the first class of the decade was pretty strong.
Now that you know the top first-rounders, let's check out the bottom five.
187. Colts QB Anthony Richardson (Fourth overall in 2023) 188. Titans OT Isaiah Wilson (29th overall in 2020) 189. Lions CB Jeff Okudah (Third overall in 2020) 190. Jets QB Zach Wilson (Second overall in 2021) 191. 49ers QB Trey Lance (Third overall in 2021)
Wilson and Lance are likely going to go down as two of the biggest busts of all time. If you have some time to burn today, then I highly suggest you read Renner's full list of all 191 players here .
With training camps kicking off around the NFL, Deebo Samuel still doesn't have a team to play for. The former Pro Bowler spent last season with the Commanders , but he's now a free agent. Samuel has hit the age (30) where most receivers start to slow down, but he doesn't think that's going to happen to him.
As a matter of fact, Samuel seems to think he has a few years left in the tank.
"I'm going on Year 8 … I still feel like I got a lot, at least like three, four good years left," Samuel said.
With that in mind, Jordan Dajani decided to come up with a few potential landing spots for Samuel and here are two of his more intriguing options:
Dajani came up with five landing spots, and you can see his full list here .
With the reigning NFL MVP (Matthew Stafford) and the reigning defensive player of the year ( Myles Garrett ) on their team, the Rams are currently the overwhelming favorite to win Super Bowl LXI.
As a matter of fact, the Rams are an unprecedented favorite to win the Super Bowl this year. Let's check out the top five favorites along with their odds:
1. Rams (+550) 2. Bills (+1000) 3. Ravens (+1100) 4. Seahawks (+1200) T-5. Chiefs (+1600) T-5. Chargers (+1600)
As you'll notice, the Rams are the only team this year with odds under +1000. Since the NFL expanded to 32 teams in 2002, this marks just the fifth time that we've seen an overwhelming Super Bowl favorite like this.
Here are the previous four instances where there was only one team with odds under +1000:
As you can see, the Rams are the first NFC team in 23 years to be an overwhelming Super Bowl favorite. And it's worth noting that in the four other instances where we had a heavily favored team, all four teams fell short of expectations during the regular season. (Three of the four teams finished under their projected win total while the 2018 Patriots pushed, so none of them hit the over).
When you're the Super Bowl favorite, you have high expectations, but when you're an overwhelming favorite, the expectations that come with that can crush you, as history has shown.
This could be the final NFL season for two major stars. Aaron Rodgers has already said that he's likely going to call it quits after 2026 , and then there's Travis Kelce , who could also end up retiring after the season. With that in mind, Bryan DeArdo decided to dig deep through the annals of NFL history so he could rank the 10 best farewell seasons that have ever happened.
Some guys get to ride off into the sunset, while others see their careers end on a low note. Let's check out the top three farewell seasons on DeArdo's list:
1. Jerome Bettis (2005). The Steelers running back had the perfect storybook finish to his Hall of Fame career, winning a Super Bowl in his hometown of Detroit and retiring on the podium with the Lombardi Trophy in hand.
2. John Elway (1997). After winning his first Super Bowl in his 15th season, Elway contemplated his future for most of the offseason before deciding to return to help the Broncos win back-to-back Super Bowls. In Denver's Super Bowl win over the Falcons , Elway let loose, throwing for 336 yards, including an 80-yard touchdown pass that gave the Broncos a double-digit lead they wouldn't relinquish. Elway capped his MVP performance with a short touchdown run early in the fourth quarter.
3. Peyton Manning (2015). Manning's final season was downright bizarre. Injuries limited him to 10 games during the regular season. And when he did play, it was clear that he was no longer capable of playing at a high level. It got so bad that Manning was in jeopardy of finishing the season and his career on the bench. But when the opportunity presented itself, Manning took full advantage. He replaced an ineffective Brock Osweiler in Week 17 and helped lead the Broncos to a come-from-behind win over the Chargers. Manning remained Denver's starter through the playoffs and helped the Broncos win their third Super Bowl title.
Kelce and Rodgers will both be hoping to end their career with a Super Bowl title just like the top three guys on DeArdo's list. If you want to see Bryan's full top-10 ranking, we've got it here .
It's been a busy few days in the NFL, and since it's nearly impossible to keep track of everything, I put together a quick roundup for you.
author: John Breech

title: Why Tyreek Hill's NFL career could be in jeopardy: Eight-time Pro Bowler offers update on injured knee
summary: Hill is trying to work his way back from a dislocated kneecap and multiple torn ligaments, but his timeline remains unclear
full_text:
It doesn't look like Tyreek Hill is very close to returning to the field. The eight-time Pro Bowler gave an update this week on his left knee, which he injured back in September.
Hill missed the final 13 games of the 2025 season after suffering the gruesome injury in a Week 4 game against the Jets . Not only did Hill suffer a dislocated kneecap, but he also tore multiple ligaments in his knee, including his ACL. In the 10 months since the injury, Hill has undergone two surgeries.
In his latest video on social media, the free agent receiver, who was cut by the Dolphins in February, admitted that he's nowhere near 100%.
"So it's about 10 months after doing two surgeries," Hill said. "My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg at all, so I'm trying to regain all the power back in my left leg, but it's one day at a time."
In the video, Hill showed a few clips of himself jogging, but it's clear he's still got a long way to go before he can hit the cheetah speed he's been known for throughout his NFL career.
If Hill makes a comeback, it would be an impressive story, but that's not going to be easy. Over the course of his 10-year career, Hill has been one of the best receivers in the NFL, and the one big thing that set him apart from everyone else was his speed. And now, the problem for Hill is that it's not clear if he's going to have the explosiveness that he once had when he returns from the injury.
At this point in his recovery, Hill says he feels good, but he knows there's still a long way to go.
"That's it, my first step is just kind of rusty," Hill said.
If Hill ends up losing a step following his injury, he might have to reinvent himself, but that's not going to be easy to do at his age. The five-time All-Pro is 32 years old, which is ancient for a receiver. Receivers tend to fall off a steep cliff after hitting age 30, as CBS Sports researcher Doug Clawson pointed out back in February .
"I looked at every wide receiver with 10,000 career receiving yards to debut since 2000. They average 89.8 receiving yards per game from ages 25-29, and it falls off a cliff to 64.3 yards per game from ages 30-34," Clawson wrote.
Hill is a rare talent, but even he slowed down after hitting age 30. From his rookie year until he turned 29, Hill played eight seasons -- six with the Chiefs and two with the Dolphins -- and he averaged 81.8 receiving yards per game. During his age 30 season in 2024, that average dropped dramatically to 56.4. Hill bumped that average up to 66.4 yards per game last season, but that came over just four games, so it may not have been sustainable.
Even if he's not the same player he once was, just returning to the NFL would be remarkable, considering where he was 10 months ago.
"You know, they told me I might not be able to walk again," Hill said of his injury. "And the doctor was like, 'Bro, we don't know what's going to happen with your future.' And now, look at me."
If Hill's speed isn't what it used to be, he may have limited suitors in free agency. At this point, it's hard to say where Hill might end up, but we did look at some potential landing spots, and a reunion with the Chiefs is at the top of the list. For now, most teams will probably wait until Hill is closer to 100% before showing any interest, so it could be a month or two (or even longer) before he gets any offers.
