title: A monster season was just the beginning for Nik Bonitto
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Nik Bonitto is coming off a career season. The Denver Broncos edge totaled 14 sacks, finished fourth in the NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting, and went to his first Pro Bowl. It’s Bonitto’s second straight season of double-digit sacks. In the win over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 25: Nik Bonitto #15 of the Denver Broncos lines up before the snap during the AFC Championship NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Nik Bonitto is coming off a career season. The Denver Broncos edge totaled 14 sacks, finished fourth in the NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting, and went to his first Pro Bowl. It’s Bonitto’s second straight season of double-digit sacks. In the win over the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoffs, he was a game-wrecker, tallying two forced fumbles, including a strip sack of Josh Allen. Bonitto is now in the discussion as one of the top pass rushers in the NFL. Now, he wants to get even better. As Bonitto said to the Broncos website on Thursday: “All facets. I still have a lot of room to grow in my game — in the run and in the pass. Just keep trying to fine-tune these things, keep looking at other guys around the league that are doing it at a high level and seeing how I can put it into my game to continue to be the best player I know I can be.” What gives Bonitto the confidence is the success he had in the win over the Bills. How could it not? He was a huge reason Denver recorded one of the best wins in franchise history. “It’s obviously great when you can do it in the regular season,” Bonitto said Thursday to the Broncos website. But doing it in the postseason in those big type of moments, it gives you that confidence to know you’re supposed to be there and you can make those types of plays on big stages.” "I still have a lot of room to grow in my game. Just keep trying to fine-tune these things." OLB Nik Bonitto eyes improvement in 'all facets' in Year 5 » https://t.co/6vN2y2cm08 pic.twitter.com/kz4hlxPAx8 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) July 23, 2026 As Bonitto and Denver look to take the next step after finishing one game away from the Super Bowl, Bonitto will play a key role in making that come to life. He’s one of the leaders on defense and has put himself in the discussion as one of the best edge rushers in the NFL. If Bonitto is able to take his game to another level this season, that makes the Broncos defense better and the team. His mindset will force his teammates to match his commitment and desire. It’s exactly what a team needs looking to build off a season like Denver just had. “I’m really excited,” Bonitto said to the team website. “Especially how the season ended, I know everybody’s champing at the bit to get the pads back on and compete against each other these next couple months. It’s going to be real fun for sure.”
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Ranking the Denver Broncos’ offensive position groups prior to training camp
summary: The Denver Broncos showed some amazing flashes on offense during the 2025 season, but their overall efforts landed them in the middle of the pack in almost every offensive category. This offseason, the Broncos made a big splash by adding wide receiver Jaylen Waddle into the mix, as well as drafting players to shore up […]
full_text: Sep 29, 2025; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos offensive tackle Garett Bolles (72) celebrates after the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images | Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images The Denver Broncos showed some amazing flashes on offense during the 2025 season, but their overall efforts landed them in the middle of the pack in almost every offensive category. This offseason, the Broncos made a big splash by adding wide receiver Jaylen Waddle into the mix, as well as drafting players to shore up their backfield, tight end group, and offensive line. In order to compete at a high level and make their Super Bowl dreams come true, Denver needs to find a way to be more consistent offensively. The aforementioned moves should help accomplish that. Moreover, I’m optimistic Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb will find a way to help them be more efficient. Nevertheless, they still have to prove themselves on the field. That means executing better on third downs, drastically improving their three-and-out woes, and finding a way to consistently run the ball and take some weight off Bo Nix’s shoulders. Without further ado, here are my offensive position group rankings for the upcoming season. Feel free to give yours in the comments section. #1: The Offensive Line Football games are won in the trenches. Thankfully, the Broncos boast one of the best offensive lines in the National Football League and have good depth. With multiple All-Pro and Pro-Bowl players, Denver’s linemen up front have done a fantastic job protecting Bo Nix and paving ample rushing lanes for Denver’s running backs. Garett Bolles, the elder statesman of the franchise, continues to play at a high level as his Ring of Fame career rolls along. Mike McGlinchey, a key free agent signing from a few years ago, has finally ended Denver’s longstanding revolving door at the right tackle position. They have proven themselves to be one of the top tackle duos in the NFL. A road grader and bully at right guard, Quinn Meinerz continues his ascent as one of the league’s best offensive linemen. Center Luke Wattenberg impressed last year with healthy and took a major jump as a player. Whether Ben Powers or Alex Palcezwski win the left guard job, I feel comfortable with their ability to play well on a weekly basis. This is a well-rounded group and one that deserves a lot of credit for the franchise’s quick turnaround the past few seasons. I have no doubts they will perform well as a group this season and help pave the way for another double-digit win season. #2: The Wide Receivers Ranking Denver’s wide receiver corps as the second-best position group on offense will certainly raise a few eyebrows. Last season, the group made a lot of big plays in big moments. Alas, they struggled with drops and game-to-game consistency which resulted in a lot of stalled drives and missed scoring opportunities. Even so, I believe Waddle’s addition will help unleash the potential of this group in ‘26. He’s a threat down the field and is extremely effective creating yards after the catch. It’s been a long time since Denver has had two receivers top the 1,000-yard mark, but Jaylen and Courtland Sutton appear poised to do that for the Broncos in ‘26. If all goes as planned, they could be one of the most productive wide receiver duos in the NFL. Marvin Mims Jr., Troy Franklin, and Pat Bryant are all talented wideouts with very different playing styles. It’s hard to theorize the trio’s potential target share given Waddle’s presence. However, the best we can hope for is that we see increased explosive plays and that they take advantage of the opportunities and looks they are given. I’m confident that at least one of them will play a significant role in helping Denver’s offense become a Top 10 unit this season. #3: The Quarterbacks Entering his third year leading the Broncos on the gridiron, Bo Nix has arguably been the most productive rookie from the 2024 NFL Draft class. Nix touts a penchant for game-winning drives and fourth quarter heroics. His Houdini-like ability to evade pressure and avoid sacks has been a welcomed sight for sore eyes after seeing Russell Wilson take too many bad sacks in his time in Denver. By all accounts, Nix has surpassed almost any expectation I had of him once he was drafted. He hasn’t been perfect, but the production and wins speak for themselves. That being said, my biggest concern for the team in ’26 is how he will recover and perform after his devastating ankle injury against the Buffalo Bills in the AFC Divisional Playoff game. So much of his game is predicated on his ability to roll out of the pocket and make plays on the move. Will his ankle injury inhibit or limit that? Potentially. Which means he has to take a big leap as a pocket passer, especially operating over the middle of the field. For as much as I’ve been thrilled with Nix, that is an area he has struggled at since his collegiate days at Auburn and Oregon. If he can improve demonstrably in that regard, the offense will be much more efficient. At that point in time, he will certainly merit consideration as one of the league’s best signal callers. #4: The Running Backs The Broncos had one of the better rushing attacks for about half of last season. Unfortunately, things spiraled downward when J.K. Dobbins suffered a season ending Lisfranc injury in Week 10 versus the Las Vegas Raiders. RJ Harvey was a dual-threat player last season and led all rookies in total touchdowns and amassed nearly 1,000 all-purpose yards. Though his vision and consistency as a runner was a struggle throughout the year. In order to help their ground game in ‘26, Denver drafted Washington standout Jonah Coleman in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. He is a touchdown scoring machine, a tough runner with a low center of gravity, and has great vision in patience. In the event Dobbins were to have any setbacks with injury, I’m confident Coleman could step in immediately and be an asset for the team. With Coleman’s addition to the squad, that likely means one of Tyler Badie and Jaleel McLaughlin, will be suiting up in a different uniform for the upcoming season. Regardless of how that shakes out, I believe Denver’s top trio of running backs will be more productive this year compared to ‘25. #5: The Tight Ends For quite some time now, the Broncos have been without a top-flight player at the tight end position. I’m not “down” on this group as a whole, but it’s certainly the one that has the most room for improvement. All of Broncos Country was hopeful Evan Engram would prove to be the ‘Joker’ Head Coach Sean Payton touted him as all of last offseason. Alas, that never came to fruition and Engram’s first year in the Mile High City wound up being quite forgettable. Instead of pursuing an outside addition to the squad, the team opted for continuity at the position. Well-versed in Payton’s system, veteran tight end Adam Trautman to be their main man at the ‘Y’ for the season. Additionally, every other player that saw snaps last year is set to compete for a spot during training camp and the preseason. Denver also added NC State standout Justin Joly and Utah’s Dallen Bentley on Day 3 of this year’s draft. I’m not sure how much to expect from either as rookies. However, I do believe Joly has the talent to be consistent contributor at the position in time. He seems like a viable replacement for Engram, with Bentley offering a skillset more similar to Trautman’s, but with a little bit more receiving potential.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Denver Broncos 2026 Training Camp: 5 storylines to keep an eye on
summary: When the Broncos officially hit the practice field for training camp next week (Yes, it is almost here), there will be several storylines that we will be following. Despite making it to the AFC Championship Game last season, being the number one seed, and winning the AFC West, the Broncos made some major changes to […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - DECEMBER 21: Quarterbacks coach Davis Webb of the Denver Broncos speaks to Bo Nix (10) during the first quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, December 21, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images When the Broncos officially hit the practice field for training camp next week (Yes, it is almost here), there will be several storylines that we will be following. Despite making it to the AFC Championship Game last season, being the number one seed, and winning the AFC West, the Broncos made some major changes to their team this offseason, and this will be our first real look at these changes. On top of that, they have some key players coming back from injury and some roster battles to keep an eye on. Here are the storylines I believe we should be keeping track of during the Denver Broncos’ 2026 training camp practices. Bo Nix is back After suffering a broken ankle during the final plays of the Broncos’ thrilling overtime comeback victory vs. the Buffalo Bills in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, quarterback Bo Nix missed the vast majority of the offseason program. He was absent during OTA’s but did come back in a limited fashion during the team’s minicamp practices last month. However, Nix is expected to be 100% and ready to go for the start of camp, and this will be our first look at Nix since that bittersweet victory in January. BO NIX IS BACK! 🎥 via @Broncos pic.twitter.com/OSVEDV6fzF — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) June 16, 2026 Nix spoke to the media last month after returning to the practice field and told reporters that his doctors told him his ankle, which he had multiple surgeries on, looks good as new. I felt really good, just a little bit of soreness. Just wanted to go ahead and get it out of the way for good. Now they tell me—I didn’t get in there and look at it—but the doctors told me that the ankle looks good as new. We’re right back to normal. So once the progression of the rehab comes and goes after you wait your due diligence and wait patiently and get through it, it should feel great.” He was later asked if he would be able to go full go by the start of training camp, and Nix told reporters, “Yes, I could go full go right now if they wanted me to”. So, the Broncos franchise quarterback should not have any limitations when camp opens up next week. However, all eyes will be on Nix to see how he does. The expectations are Super Bowl or bust; he has a new play caller, a new number one receiver in Jaylen Waddle, and a bunch of critics ready to pounce if he struggles. The pressure will be on Nix, but thankfully for the Broncos, Nix thrives when the pressure is on, and I believe he is on the verge of a great season in 2026. Davis Webb, the OC and play-caller One of the bigger storylines surrounding the Broncos this offseason was the return of Davis Webb and his promotion to offensive coordinator, where he would take the play-calling duties away from head coach Sean Payton. Webb had multiple head coaching opportunities as well as some offensive coordinator/play-calling offers from other teams. However, Webb ultimately decided to stay with the Broncos and, somewhat surprisingly, was handed the keys to the offense by Head Coach and veteran play-caller Sean Payton. While Payton will very much be involved in the offense and in the play-calling, Webb will be the one running the offense and working directly with Bo Nix and the rest of the Broncos’ offensive players. Nix spoke to the media about Webb and told reporters that Webb is ready for the job and believes it will allow Payton to manage the other aspects of the team, which will be a “good weapon for us to have”. “He had several chances to go be straight up a head coach, so I think we were fortunate to keep him as an organization. [I’m] just excited to see his growth and maturity as a play caller. Obviously it’ll be his first time, but he’s prepped and has been waiting for this day for a long time. This is his first opportunity, so he has to make the most of it, and he knows that and he’s working really hard. He’s had a really successful grind this offseason, just really taking what we have [and asking], ‘How can we grow it, how can we make it a little bit more suitable for where we are now?’ How can we make it so he enjoys calling it and comfortable for him? Then at the end of the day, how can he teach me to go out there and execute it and perform? We think similarly, so that’s going to be the fun part as we go. I’m really excited to have him. It allows [Head] Coach [Sean] Payton to be relieved of those duties, be able to go and do other things, like really critique the defense, really critique special teams, really look at offensive line and defensive line, really look at the trenches, look at the skill and evaluate a little bit more because his time’s not filled having to game plan or all that kind of stuff. So I think it’s just a good weapon for us to have, and I think it’s going to help us.” While we may not see noticeable changes during camp, this will be our first real look at what a Davis Webb-run offense will look like. Some changes that have been rumored are getting the play call in fast, maybe more up-tempo, and some more aggressive plays that fall into Bo Nix’s wheelhouse. Broncos OC and primary play-caller Davis Webb, when asked last month about calling plays with Sean Payton potentially leaning over his shoulder, metaphorically speaking: "I would say just two things about that. No. 1, that was one reason why I wanted to be here — was with Sean… pic.twitter.com/eEa8tT61Ns — Andrew Mason (@MaseDenver) July 21, 2026 With that said, Webb himself said that the offense will be the same for the most part, just with some tweaks here and there. He continued by saying this is a Sean Payton-coached football team and Sean Payton offensive philosophy, so Payton’s influence will still be heavily involved in this offense, as it should be. “I would say there’s two things about that. title: Denver Broncos roster review: Edge Jonathon Cooper
summary: One of the key questions heading into 2026: What happens to Jonathon Cooper? The Denver Broncos edge finds himself in limbo heading into the season due to off-the-field legal issues. Will George Paton and Sean Payton keep Cooper on the roster? Or will they move on from the sixth-year linebacker? At this point, no one […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 25: Jonathon Cooper #0 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the AFC Championship Playoff game between the New England Patriots and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the key questions heading into 2026: What happens to Jonathon Cooper? The Denver Broncos edge finds himself in limbo heading into the season due to off-the-field legal issues. Will George Paton and Sean Payton keep Cooper on the roster? Or will they move on from the sixth-year linebacker? At this point, no one outside the franchise knows, and Denver isn’t saying. That’s before possible discipline from the NFL comes down for the personal conduct policy. Player Profile Age: 28 | Experience: Sixth Year | College: Ohio State | Height: 6’4” | Weight: 257 pounds Until a decision is made on Cooper’s status, let’s assume he’s in the equation in 2026. At least in some capacity. Of course, we all know what they say about those who assume, but we don’t have much of a choice at this point. Jonathon Cooper’s 2026 outlook with the Broncos Before we get into what Cooper could bring to the Denver defense, let’s quickly circle back to what happened in early June. It was on June 5 that the news broke that Cooper had been arrested and was being held on two counts of domestic violence and one count of criminal mischief. The incident appears to have occurred on the night of June 4. Then, the news broke that Cooper was arrested again , a week later, on charges of domestic violence and misdemeanor charges of harassment and violation of a protection order. As a result, the Broncos excused Cooper from minicamp practices. Will that be the play for Denver heading into training camp? Or will he be allowed to get on the field? When Cooper is on the field, his ability to get after the quarterback has helped make the Broncos defense so vaunted over the last few seasons. His pairing with Nik Bonitto has made them one of the pass-rushing duos in the league. In 2025, Cooper finished with 8 sacks, 50 tackles (23 solo), and four passes defended. His best season in the NFL came in 2024 when he had 10.5 sacks. What adds to the dilemma is Cooper’s salary. In 2026, he carries a cap hit of $5.7 millon but a dead cap of $18.3 million. In 2027, the cap hit jumps to $17.5 million, and the dead cap drops slightly to $13 million. Final thoughts What Denver decides to do with Cooper is one of the biggest questions heading into training camp. Of course, it’s possible the Broncos do nothing and let all the legal issues play out in court, then decide afterward. It’s possible Denver does with Cooper what it did in minicamp and excuses Cooper from training camp. If that happens, it falls on the guys lower on the depth chart to step up and find a way to replace him. If Cooper is on the field in 2026, the Broncos know what to expect: a guy who can get after the quarterback and make life more difficult for opposing quarterbacks. How this plays out is one of the franchise’s looming issues.

title: Expectations for RJ Harvey in Year 2
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos finished their 2025 season as a middle of the pack offense in most statistical categories. While they had a penchant for fourth quarter comebacks and miraculous victories, the down-to-down consistency for the unit was an issue for them throughout the ’25 gridiron campaign. In order to compete at […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 04: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball in the second half against the Los Angeles Chargers at Empower Field At Mile High on January 04, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by C. Morgan Engel/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos finished their 2025 season as a middle of the pack offense in most statistical categories. While they had a penchant for fourth quarter comebacks and miraculous victories, the down-to-down consistency for the unit was an issue for them throughout the ’25 gridiron campaign. In order to compete at a high level in 2026 and secure the franchise’s fourth Lombardi Trophy, being more efficient on offense is an absolute must and one of the top priorities for them. With the addition of Jaylen Waddle, the Broncos made an all-in move to bolster their offensive output. I have no doubt that his presence will pay big dividends for them this season and beyond. Boasting tremendous deep ball ability and the talent to accrue yards after the catch, Waddle’s talents will unleash a dynamic on that side of the ball that was missing last year. However, a key recipe to Denver’s offensive endeavors this year will be the continued development of second year running back RJ Harvey. As a rookie, Harvey made quite the impact in his first season donning orange and blue. Amassing 896 yards from scrimmage (540 rushing, 356 receiving), the former UCF standout was one of Denver’s most impactful offensive players. His twelve touchdowns were the most of any rookie in the National Football League and the most since Ja’Marr Chase posted thirteen back in 2021. When the Broncos needed a big play on the ground or through the air, Harvey often answered the call and was a key reason why the team was able to string along 14 hard-fought victories during the regular season and their first AFC West crown in a decade. When asked about his development entering his second season with the Broncos in June, Head Coach Sean Payton had glowing praise for Denver’s second-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft. “He’s doing well. We saw the early passing game traits. He just goes to work. He’s really smart. He’s instinctual. I think we’re pleased with how he’s progressing.” Whether or not Harvey can become a ‘Joker’ player for the Broncos in ‘26 remains to be seen. Nevertheless, he has all the traits and ability to do so. As Payton mentioned, his impact as a receiver last season was undeniable. His 80-percent catch-rate was one of the best in the league. Even better? 23 of his 48 catches resulted in first downs or touchdowns. However, one area for significant improvement would be with respect to yards per carry. He finished the season at 3.7 YPC. That’s just a shade under the desired 4.0 YPC threshold, but he is certainly capable of more. In the final stretch of the season including their AFC Divisional Playoff win over the Buffalo Bills, Harvey averaged just 3 yards per carry. If the Broncos want to have one a Top 10 offense in the NFL this season, Harvey will need to be more consistent as a runner. The splash and impact plays are great but being able to hit the right lane and get-tough yardage will be crucial for Denver to buck their trend of three-and-outs and stalled drives. If he can accomplish that, Harvey could very well be a 1,250 all-purpose yard player and a potential Pro-Bowler and could be the dynamic player that helps the offense reach new heights. title: Detroit Lions 2026 training camp preview: 4 big questions at EDGE
summary: In this installment of our Detroit Lions 2026 training camp preview series, we continue our exploration of the defensive trenches by examining the Lions’ edge rushers, speculating on current and future roles, and discussing how many players from this group could make the 53-man roster. Previous training camp previews: Roster construction Under the Brad Holmes […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive end Derrick Moore (9) practices during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images In this installment of our Detroit Lions 2026 training camp preview series, we continue our exploration of the defensive trenches by examining the Lions’ edge rushers, speculating on current and future roles, and discussing how many players from this group could make the 53-man roster. Previous training camp previews: Quarterback: Can Luke Altmyer force a QB3 role? Running back: How RB roles could shift in 2026 Wide receiver: WR depth roles up for grabs Tight end: How many TEs will make the roster? Offensive tackle: Can Blake Miller win the starting RT job? Interior OL: How quickly will Cade Mays adapt to scheme? Defensive tackles: DT has upgraded starters, questionable depth Roster construction Under the Brad Holmes and Dan Campbell regime, the Lions have kept at least five pure edge rushers on the roster, but have consistently needed to tweak numbers as they’ve dealt with injuries. Let’s take a look at what they’ve done at edge rusher in the previous five seasons: 2021 : Opened the season with five and ended with six. 2022 : Repeated the process of starting with five and ending with six. 2023 : Opened and closed the season with seven edge rushers, as they looked for a dedicated pass-rushing linebacker option. 2024 : Opened and closed with five on the roster, despite working through a plethora of injuries. 2025 : Opened with six, but quickly reduced to five; kept five active on game days for the first half of the season, but reduced to four on game days soon after the bye week. Altering their approach on the edge Impactful pass rushers can be difficult to find in the NFL, but the Lions have been incredibly fortunate to have All-Pro Aidan Hutchinson locking down one side of their defensive line. Because Hutchinson almost never leaves the field, the Lions can focus solely on deploying their remaining pass rushers on the opposite edge, as well as using them in creative situations, like kicking them inside, stacking them, and introducing a pass-rushing linebacker role. Unfortunately, the Lions have struggled to find a reliable solution opposite Hutchinson. For the last several seasons, the Lions have preferred their edge rushers to have a balanced run-stop/pass-rush skill set, and most starters checked in at over 265-280 pounds, as Detroit prioritized size to set a firm edge. Last season, the Lions rostered five edge rushers to fight for time opposite Hutchinson, but due to injuries, lack of production, or opportunities elsewhere, none of them remain in Detroit for 2026. Starter Marcus Davenport failed to stay healthy, was not re-signed, and is still a free agent. Josh Paschal stayed on NFI the entire 2025 season and was eventually released. Tyrus Wheat returned to Dallas (the team that drafted him) after minimal opportunities, and Pat O’Connor retired this offseason . Al-Quadin Muhammad was by far the most productive pass rusher to play opposite Hutchinson, registering 11 sacks in 2025, but the Lions mainly deployed him in pass rushing situations because, at only 250 pounds, he struggled to set an edge in the run game. The Lions would have loved for Muhammad to return in a pass-rushing role in 2026, but he opted to sign with the Buccaneers on a more lucrative contract . With only Hutchinson and Ahmed Hassanein (who spent half the season recovering from injury and the other half on the practice squad) returning to Detroit in 2026, the Lions were forced to rebuild their edge rusher room this offseason. The Lions made five additions, signing DJ Wonnum and Payton Turner in free agency , then drafting Derrick Moore in the second round of the NFL Draft, as well as signing rookies Anthony Lucas and Eric O’Neill as undrafted free agents. This group of players still possesses a balanced skill set as pass rushers/run defenders, but only Turner tips the scales over 265 pounds. Whether conscious or not, the Lions invested in multiple edge rushers who are a bit lighter than they traditionally prefer, but they also bring more juice as pass rushers. Setting the edge is still something each of these edge players does well, but there appears to be a greater emphasis on pass rush than we have seen in previous seasons. The battleground Who starts opposite Hutchinson: DJ Wonnum or Derrick Moore? While Wonnum will surely begin training camp as the starter—Lions coaching staff tends to favor veterans, especially early, in these circumstances—the reality is he’ll likely end up splitting time with Moore in a rotation. How even those rotational snaps are split will depend on how quickly Moore gets up to NFL speed. Once things slow down for Moore, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the snaps even out, and potentially favor the rookie, who could end up starting by season’s end. With four years of starting experience (54 games), Wonnum is a steady presence that the Lions can trust. He can set a strong edge, has positional range to move around, and has two eight-sack seasons (30 sacks in his career) under his belt. On a defensive front that features Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, and Tyleik Williams, Wonnum won’t need to be a superstar, and his steady presence can still help upgrade the defensive line as a whole. The presence of Wonnum will allow the Lions to take their time with developing Moore, but he comes out of Michigan with plenty of experience in a pro-style scheme, and it wouldn’t be surprising to see him make an early impact on the field. Moore’s an exciting addition to the Lions’ edge rusher room, and the Lions should feel confident they can trust him to set an edge against the run, while also offering more developable pass rush than they have had on the roster in several years. A starting role appears to be in Moore’s future, but he’ll have to work to earn snaps because of Wonnum’s steadiness. This duo should be a noticeable upgrade from seasons past. Can Payton Turner overcome his injury history? Turner matches the profile of an edge rusher the Lions have typically preferred. At 6-foot-6, 270 pounds with elite athleticism, Turner was a former first-round pick who has failed to reach his developmental ceiling due to an injury-plagued career. In the last five seasons, Turner has played in just 31 games, has never started a game, and has produced only 50 tackles and five sacks. While Turner will remind some fans of Davenport, there are stark contrasts worth noting. Turner’s contract is worth just over a million dollars and contains no guarantees, so they’re not tied to him if he struggles. He also isn’t expected to challenge for more than an EDGE4 position, meaning he’d likely hold a depth/pass-rushing-only role, closer to how the Lions used Wheat last season. If Turner stays healthy, his upside could be worth the gamble. If not, there’s very little keeping the Lions from parting ways. Can Ahmed Hassanein settle into a new role? With the offseason additions on the edge, the Lions have elected to alter Hassanein’s role for 2026, shifting him away from the rush end position and over to a “Big” end role. The key difference between the roles is that the “Big” end is asked to occupy blockers first, then pursue the ball, as opposed to simply attacking. It’ll be a shift that will require discipline from the young edge rusher, but will also allow him a simpler learning path to find the field. Hassanein has bulked up to 275 pounds for the transition, but is still a bit undersized for the position by previous standards—Levi Onwuzurike, Tyler Lacy, and Tyre West all check in between 290 and 305 pounds—which could give him anchoring problems early. However, if Hassanein can show the ability to hold an edge and provide the discipline to make his reads before attacking, there’s a chance for him to be molded into an impact player. Will a UDFA emerge as a contributor? Anthony Lucas was a draftable…

full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 2: Penei Sewell #58 of the Detroit Lions looks on during the singing of the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 2, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. The other, who was ranked in the 20-11 range last year, is replacing Brian Branch, who fell from five to eight this year largely because of his injury. So let’s jump into the final installment of this countdown, and if you need some catching up, you can find the previous editions below: Previously: Players ranked 90-81 Players ranked 80-71 Players ranked 70-61 Players ranked 60-51 Players ranked 50-41 Players ranked 40-31 Players ranked 30-21 Players ranked 20-11 Players ranked 10-6 5. Jack Campbell (Highest: 4; Lowest: 10) Last year’s ranking: 15 2024 ranking: 20 2023 ranking: 28 Campbell vaults into the top-five after an All-Pro breakout season. Now considered among the best linebackers in the NFL, Campbell will have even more put on his plate following the departure of Alex Anzalone. But Detroit showed full confidence in the former first-round pick by giving him a four-year, $81 million extension that will keep him in Detroit throughout the prime of his career. 4. EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (Highest 3; Lowest: 4) Last year’s ranking: 3 2024 ranking: 4 2023 ranking: 4 2022 ranking: 5 Hutchinson slides a spot in this year’s ranking, but that has more to do with the player he traded spots with. In 2025, Hutchinson proved that his gruesome leg injury from 2024 was not going to slow down his career. The defensive end set career highs in sacks (14.5), forced fumbles (four), tackles (54), and even added yet another interception to his resume. Oh, and he also led the NFL in pressures (100), according to PFF. Four seems awfully low for an elite pass rusher, but it speaks to the incredible high-end talent the Lions have on the roster. 3. RB Jahmyr Gibbs (Highest: 2; Lowest: 5) Last year’s ranking: 4 2024 ranking: 6 2023 ranking: 12 Gibbs continues his ascent up our list after yet another strong season. While the overall running game took a step back in 2025, Gibbs proved he doesn’t need perfect conditions to be an explosive player. For the second straight season, he posted over 1,200 rushing yards, 13 rushing TDs, and at least 5.0 yards per carry. He also had more 40-yard rushes (six) than every other player in the NFL. In fact, no one else had five. With a reformed offensive line and a new offensive coordinator who is committed to running the football, expectations are for Gibbs to build upon an already outstanding career. 2. Amon-Ra St. Brown (Highest: 2; Lowest: 5) Last year’s ranking: 2 2024 ranking: 3 2023 ranking: t-1 2022 ranking: 4 2021 ranking: 22 St. Brown is the model of consistency with the Lions. He has now produced four straight seasons of at least 100 catches and 1,100 receiving yards, and three straight seasons of at least 10 touchdowns. Just five years into his NFL career, St. Brown already ranks fourth in franchise history in receiving yards (6,252), third in receptions (547), and third in receiving touchdowns (44). There’s a very good chance he finishes his Lions career with a statline that matches or surpasses that of Calvin Johnson. First 5 years of Calvin Johnson's career Vs. First 5 years of Amon-Ra St. Brown's career pic.twitter.com/RgZ5KnTTby — Nick Brandel (@MotorCityBanter) July 19, 2026 1. LT Penei Sewell (Highest: 1; Lowest: 1) Last year’s ranking: 1 2024 ranking: 1 2023 ranking: t-1 2022 ranking: 2 2021 ranking: 8 For the third straight year, Penei Sewell is the unanimous choice for the No. 1 player on the Lions roster. Even coming off a year that wasn’t his best, Sewell is highly deserving of the top spot. He’s such a dominant force in the run game that Detroit designs play that center around his mobility and versatility. He’s so sound as a pass protector that there is virtually no concern that he’s making the move from right tackle to left tackle this offseason. In short, Sewell is the most reliable player on the entire team, is considered the best offensive tackle in football , and is one hell of a leader, too.

full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 13: Mekhi Wingo #94 of the Detroit Lions walks off of the field after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 13, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Generally speaking, we have a pretty good idea of what the Detroit Lions’ starting offensive and defensive lines are going to look like for the 2026 season. While there will likely be a few training camp battles to weed out (left guard, EDGE2, and maybe right tackle), the key players have already been identified. However, the depth at each position is very much up for grabs. This offseason, the Lions devoted a lot of resources to their offensive line reserves. They added Juice Scruggs, Ben Bartch, Larry Borom, and Seth McLaughlin to compete with the likes of Miles Frazier, Giovanni Manu, Michael Niese, and Colby Sorsdal, among others. Things are even more convoluted on the defensive side. With so many different roles on the line—nose tackle, 3-tech, “big” end, “rush” end, etc.—Detroit has several different archetypes who can fill one or multiple roles. Players like Ahmed Hassanein are switching positions from rush to big end, but is the competition there too competitive for the 2025 draft pick to make the roster? What does the drafting of Skyler Gill-Howard mean for the future of Mekhi Wingo? Is Levi Onwuzurike on the roster bubble given his injury history, or is he Detroit’s best option as a versatile backup to pretty much every position? Who will win the backup nose tackle job? And can Payton Turner turn his career around? On this week’s episode of the Midweek Mailbag, Erik Schlitt and I break down a lot of the roster bubble, which players are in competition for the same roster spot, and identify the different roles that Detroit needs to fill on both sides of the ball. Other topics on this week’s episode include (in chronological order): Will Kerby Joseph start training camp on the PUP list? Could Luke Altmyer realistically win the QB2 job or is he simply trying to make a case to keep a QB3? title: Packers News: Green Bay betting on internal improvement again. History suggests that’s smart
summary: The Green Bay Packers have heard the criticism all offseason — and I’ve written about them a bit already. After a relatively quiet free agency period, some national analysts have questioned whether Brian Gutekunst did enough to elevate the roster.  Inside Green Bay, however, the approach appears unchanged. ESPN’s training camp preview recently identified several […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - SEPTEMBER 15: Green Bay Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd (32) heads up field after the catch chased by Indianapolis Colts linebacker Zaire Franklin (44) during an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and the Green Bay Packers on September 15, 2024 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have heard the criticism all offseason — and I’ve written about them a bit already. After a relatively quiet free agency period, some national analysts have questioned whether Brian Gutekunst did enough to elevate the roster. Inside Green Bay, however, the approach appears unchanged. ESPN’s training camp preview recently identified several of the Packers’ biggest storylines as players poised for larger roles rather than newcomers expected to transform the team. Jordan Love is looking to bounce back from a slightly inconsistent 2025 season, Jordan Morgan is expected to seize the left tackle job, Lukas Van Ness faces heightened expectations off the edge, and running back MarShawn Lloyd could finally carve out a meaningful role after an injury-shortened rookie year. Those player-development storylines have been the Packers’ blueprint under Gutekunst for years. Rather than chasing veteran solutions, Green Bay has consistently invested in drafting and developing talent, trusting that young players will improve with experience and eventually replace departing veterans. This isn’t news to readers here, but it’s worth level setting during the offseason as we all tend to become at least a little detached from reality in the summer months. This strategy has already produced foundational contributors across the roster, and the next wave of development could determine whether the Packers become legitimate contenders in 2026. Our Jon Meerdink wrote about some of that development just yesterday . Training camp will offer the first real glimpse into whether the team’s bets are paying off. If Love returns to form, Morgan solidifies the offensive line, Van Ness becomes a more disruptive pass rusher, and Lloyd provides another explosive option in the backfield, Green Bay’s roster could look significantly stronger than many outside observers currently believe. 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp preview – ESPN previews the Packers’ 2026 training camp, which runs from July 29 to Aug. 26 at Ray Nitschke Field near Lambeau Field. ICYMI: Packers’ ‘young’ talent is starting to grow up – The Packers don’t rank highly in talent under 25 on the roster, but a lot of key players just aged out of that bracket. Xavier McKinney is key to Packers success in 2026 – Coming off an all-pro season, McKinney is a vital leader and a foundational player for the Packers’ defense moving forward. WATCH: Isaiah McDuffie previews the Packers defense in ’26 – Green Bay Packers linebacker Isaiah McDuffie joins “The Insiders” for an interview. Previewing Packers 3 largest projected cap hits in 2026 season – The Green Bay Packers have managed their cap space incredibly well and have more than enough space to make another impact move if needed.

title: Outlook for Houston’s productive 2023 draft picks amid contract extensions
summary: The 2023 Texans draft class moves into the final year of their rookie deals, a natural inflection point for evaluating each player’s future with the team. With extensions already in place for C.J. Stroud and Will Anderson Jr., the remaining players now face a season that will determine whether they fit into the Texans’ long‑term […]
full_text: Apr 28, 2023; Houston, TX, USA; From left to right, Houston Texans quarterback CJ Stroud (left), second overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, and Texans linebacker Will Anderson Jr., third overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft, pose for a photo at a press conference at NRG Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images The 2023 Texans draft class moves into the final year of their rookie deals, a natural inflection point for evaluating each player’s future with the team. With extensions already in place for C.J. Stroud and Will Anderson Jr., the remaining players now face a season that will determine whether they fit into the Texans’ long‑term roster construction. Houston Texans 2023 NFL Draft Class Round 1, Pick 2: C.J. Stroud – Quarterback (Ohio State) – EXTENDED via fifth-year option Round 1, Pick 3: Will Anderson Jr. – Defensive End / Linebacker (Alabama) – EXTENDED through 2030 Round 2, Pick 62: Juice Scruggs – Center / Offensive Lineman (Penn State) – CUT Round 3, Pick 69: Tank Dell – Wide Receiver (Houston) Round 4, Pick 109: Dylan Horton – Defensive End / Defensive Lineman (TCU) Round 5, Pick 167: Henry To’oTo’o – Linebacker (Alabama) Round 6, Pick 201: Jarrett Patterson – Center / Offensive Lineman (Notre Dame) Round 6, Pick 205: Xavier Hutchinson – Wide Receiver (Iowa State) Round 7, Pick 248: Brandon Hill – Safety / Defensive Back (Pittsburgh) – CUT This class has become the backbone of the Texans’ return to prominence in the AFC. Outside of the massive bust of Juice Scruggs, this class has produced both elite talent and consistent role players. They’ve started 231 of 459 possible games, a 50.3% start rate, by far the highest of any Texans draft class in the past decade. What’s made this class stand out are the Day Three contributors. Henry To’oTo’o has developed into a starting linebacker and a great counterpart to Azeez Al-Shaair. Jarrett Patterson has started 21 games; one more than former second-rounder Juice Scruggs. Xavier Hutchinson has proven to be a capable rotational receiver who can block and contribute on special teams. With their rookie deals coming to a close, they have one final season to earn a second contract. But first, they have to earn their spot on this 2026 team. That quest is most prevalent for center/guard Jarrett Patterson. He’s been the answer to the Texans all-too-often break glass scenario on the offensive line. He watched the Texans trade for, re‑sign, sign, and draft interior offensive linemen this offseason. Houston pursued every possible means to acquire talent at the expense of Patterson. According to the latest Rosterology , Patterson is expected to miss the cut. That would be a major letdown for a player who started five games last year. Unfortunately, he wouldn’t be in this position if he had made the most of his opportunities. By far the most intriguing situation in this class is WR Tank Dell. A dynamic and promising rookie season was cut short by injury. His slow ascent back in his second year ended suddenly with a gruesome leg injury that took him out all of 2025. Now, he enters the final year of his contract with much to prove. The Texans have done equally as much to replace and mitigate the loss of Dell by drafting three WRs the last two classes. What’s more, the offensive coordinator and scheme have changed while Dell has been sidelined, favoring two tight end sets that would limit Dell’s opportunities to get on the field . Even if Dell does return to health and contribute in 2026, will the organization reward him with a new contract after the injuries he’s suffered? It’s an extremely murky situation and will be intriguing to see how much he could get on the open market if the parties do decide to part ways. For now, Dell remains the single biggest X-factor on this offense. Dylan Horton remains one of the most unheralded players on the entire team. The backup DE has never started a game and only a half sack to his resume, but he has steadily increased his contribution each season . He’s now the clear third defensive end on the roster and plans to rotate in heavily to relieve the expensive and aging Danielle Hunter. He is in store for a bigger role this season and has the opportunity to earn a sizable second contract here. For Hutchinson, he’s been the backup for Nico Collins allows the offense to maintain its physicality at the position when their WR1 is out. His frame and toughness have kept him in the lineup and made him valuable as an option in the middle of the field. As illustrated by PFF’s reception depth chart, Hutch’ is employed between the numbers to gain tough yardage on slant and dig routes. His two touchdown day against Baltimore helped solidify him in the offense as a great option in spread offense packages with four or five receivers. However, he faces challenges to his role on the team and potentially his roster spot as a whole. Veteran Justin Watson remains a factor in this position group and could shake up the competition if he can wedge his way into the offense. Both Watson and Hutchinson contribute on special teams and are great run blockers. While Hutchinson is penciled in as a foregone conclusion, it’s hard to count out the former Super Bowl champion. If Hutchinson can win the spot and produce another consistent season, he should earn a team-friendly contract to stay as a depth piece. C.J. Stroud’s upcoming season towers over every other storyline. It may be the most consequential year any Texans player has ever faced, because the team’s future and financial strategy hinge entirely on his performance. Stroud is currently the twenty‑fifth‑highest‑paid quarterback, earning a fraction of what top passers make. If he delivers at the level he showed as a rookie, he’ll belong in the fifty‑million‑per‑year tier. If his results remain opaque, Houston will delay the commitment and use the franchise tag. The direction of the franchise sits squarely with him, and everyone would prefer he cements himself as the answer rather than force the team into another reset. Only thing we can do is watch this season play out.

title: Nico Collins is the star of the show
summary: About 6 years ago, I detailed the Five Best Wide Receivers in Houston Texans History. That list included Corey Bradford, Will Fuller V, Kevin Walter, DeAndre Hopkins and, of course, Andre Johnson. Based on receiving yardage alone, Nico Collins is already the 3rd place WR all-time for the Texans with 4,347 yards heading into the […]
full_text: About 6 years ago, I detailed the Five Best Wide Receivers in Houston Texans History. That list included Corey Bradford, Will Fuller V, Kevin Walter, DeAndre Hopkins and, of course, Andre Johnson. Based on receiving yardage alone, Nico Collins is already the 3rd place WR all-time for the Texans with 4,347 yards heading into the 2026 season. For those doing the math at home, you’ll note that’s about half as many yards as #2 wideout, DeAndre Hopkins, who gained 8,602 while wearing the battle red. Where you can make an argument that Collins is better than Nuk is the yards-per-catch. D-Hop had 13.7, while Nico sits at 15.0. Give Collins 632 catches, the number Hopkins had as a Texan, and the current WR1’s total jumps from 4,347 to 9,480 yards – 878 more than D-Hop. Yes, that’s also more than the average NFL receiver gains in an entire season. For those paying attention this summer, we’ve looked at PFF’s ranking for quarterbacks, including the woefully low standing for C.J. Stroud. We’ve also side-eyed their take on running backs, with David Montgomery bringing up the rear of the pack. When it comes to Nico Collins, the stat crunching site has a far more positive outlook. PFF.com 8. Nico Collins , Houston Texans After two pedestrian seasons to begin his career, Collins has emerged as one of the NFL’s top receivers over the past three years. His 3,420 receiving yards during that span rank ninth in the NFL, while his 2.75 yards per route run rank second behind only Puka Nacua. Collins’ 93.0 PFF receiving grade since 2023 ranks third in the NFL behind Nacua and Amon-Ra St. Brown. Essentially, once you hit the Demeco Ryans era for the Texans, Collins is a Top 3 receiver in the NFL. And, you get no arguments from me. When Andre Johnson set about defining the prototype Houston Texans wide receiver, he carved an archetype out of quietly getting the job done in spectacular fashion. In an era where so many pass catchers have made more headlines with their mouths and over-the-top off-field antics, Johnson kept his head down, caught the ball 1,012 times and set the stage for the show-up-but-don’t-show-off character Houston is known for. Enter Nico Collins, who many might think is a modern day clone of Johnson. He doesn’t draw attention to himself in any manner other than catching passes, gaining yards and scoring touchdowns. All this has quietly led him to 3rd highest PFF grade for receivers since 2023. Every summer the NFL Channel drops its Top 100 players list. This year, Collins hit the charts at #58. Pretty easy to believe that this rank is a clear sign that Collins flies way, way under the radar. Nico Collins comes in at 58 in the #NFLTop100 CJ Stroud: “I think he’s top 5” Derek Stingley Jr.: “he’s top 3 in the league right now.” pic.twitter.com/9pv0KNfu9n — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) July 21, 2026 As mentioned in the Top QB and RB posts, if Houston can get the offensive line working right, and the run game gives Stroud a breather, the passing game should take a big step forward in 2026 – and that happens in large part due to Collins. Where do you put him, all-time, in Texans lore: What was your favorite Nico Collins moment? Where do you think he’ll shine the most in the 2026 Houston Texans schedule? Recent NFL polls according to Coaches, Execs and Scouts have Nico Collins as a top 10 WR. Why can’t he be top 5 this season? I think he already is. pic.twitter.com/bpBzwsDRAo — big ounce (@_bigounce) July 16, 2026

title: Unfortunately, ESPN analyst doesn’t see Colts re-finding 2025 first half form
summary: According to ESPN’s Ben Solak, the Indianapolis Colts won’t realistically regain their 2025 first half form, citing starting quarterback Daniel Jones’ uncertain health and the loss of a number of key veterans as the realistic reasons for the continued regression: First and foremost, Solak makes a valid point on Jones, who Indianapolis re-signed to a […]
full_text: Inglewood, CA - October 19: Quarterback Daniel Jones #17 talks with head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts during a time out against the Los Angeles Chargersin the first half of a NFL football game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on Sunday, October 19, 2025. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images According to ESPN’s Ben Solak, the Indianapolis Colts won’t realistically regain their 2025 first half form, citing starting quarterback Daniel Jones’ uncertain health and the loss of a number of key veterans as the realistic reasons for the continued regression : 2026 outlook: Repeat of early ’25 success seems unlikely It’s tough to expect anything close to a repeat performance from Jones in 2026, even before we consider the effect of the Achilles injury. It’s also worth noting that the Colts endured another offensive line departure (Braden Smith) and saw a key offensive weapon (Michael Pittman Jr.) leave the building to boot. Veteran defenders Nick Scott and Zaire Franklin both departed this offseason, leaving Day 2 rookies A.J. Haulcy and CJ Allen in line to fill their big shoes. The sheer number of departures, along with uncertain health for Jones, makes them a tough horse to back in 2026. — Ben Solak First and foremost, Solak makes a valid point on Jones, who Indianapolis re-signed to a 2-year contract extension worth up to a total of $100 million in earned incentives. Having suffered the season-ending torn Achilles late in Week 14 of last year, and for a quarterback who relies a lot on his mobility for playmaking, it will be realistically surprising if he’s able to make a fully recovery in such a short period of time. His ongoing Achilles rehab results are encouraging, but 2026 could be more of a redshirt year for him, and that may have been built into his recent contract in Indianapolis, considering it’s a two year pact for Indiana Jones. That being said, in my opinion, he’s overstating the loss of Colts veterans outside of longtime veteran wideout Michael Pittman Jr., who did a lot of the little things that help an offense be productive and move the sticks. Change was arguably needed at both starting linebacker by trading Zaire Franklin, as well as at right tackle by allowing veteran starter Braden Smith to depart in free agency without any reported resistance by Indianapolis. The Colts needed to get younger and more cost-controllable at both spots. Franklin didn’t seem to be as good of a natural fit in Lou Anarumo’s defensive scheme and his play had fallen off recently, while Smith’s durability remained a major concern going forward at his higher price tag. I’m appreciative of both of their prior tenures in Indianapolis, but I think each veteran player’s production had fallen off a bit in more recent seasons for the cost. The Colts shouldn’t lose much at all from Franklin to rookie CJ Allen and Smith to 2nd-year tackle Jalen Travis from a playing and production standpoint, although the dip in experience and veteran leadership may hurt a bit. Nick Scott? But yes, Nick Cross is a nicer young safety in this league, who excelled at times against the run and in-the-box, but was a bit of a wild card in coverage. Rookie safety AJ Haulcy should be more of a versatile, natural fit for Anarumo’s scheme, and the hope is that it comes with a lot more pass coverage consistency in time. Solak ultimately may land on the right conclusion, but I do disagree with a bit of his initial reasoning. The bigger issue to me is the failure to meaningfully upgrade at edge and wide receiver along with Jones’ continued questionable 2026 health. Fingers crossed it turns out differently for the Colts, and in a good way!
author: Luke Schultheis

title: ‘JT 4 MVP’? Colts RB Jonathan Taylor listed team’s non-QB ‘Most Valuable Player’ choice
summary: According to NFL.com’s Kevin Patra, Indianapolis Colts star workhorse Jonathan Taylor is the team’s best candidate among non-quarterbacks to win the NFL’s Most Valuable Player Award for the 2026 campaign: Indianapolis Colts: Jonathan Taylor, Running Back Daniel Jones is coming off an Achilles injury that could slow the passing game at least early in the season. I expect […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 26: Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates after the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 26, 2023 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL.com’s Kevin Patra, Indianapolis Colts star workhorse Jonathan Taylor is the team’s best candidate among non-quarterbacks to win the NFL’s Most Valuable Player Award for the 2026 campaign: Indianapolis Colts: Jonathan Taylor, Running Back Daniel Jones is coming off an Achilles injury that could slow the passing game at least early in the season. I expect head coach Shane Steichen to lean heavily on Taylor as his QB works through things. An every-down workhorse with explosive potential, the only question I have about Taylor is whether back-to-back seasons with 300-plus carries will sneak up on him or force the club to siphon off some of his totes as the season wears on. Regardless, if the Colts are to rebound from last year’s collapse, it’ll be on the strength of their Pro Bowl RB. It’s a pretty easy choice for the Colts. Last year, with the red hot Colts once sitting at an 8-2 overall record, featuring a historically elite offense and Taylor as unquestionably the unit’s best player and its focal point, Taylor was a bona fide NFL MVP candidate—not just NFL Offensive Player of the Year. He would’ve been the first running back to win the award since Adrian Peterson back in 2012, and it was a serious conversation among league media—albeit short-lived thereafter. Specifically, critical injuries to starting quarterback Daniel Jones, derailed not only the Colts, but Taylor’s MVP chances down the stretch. With Jones hobbled and eventually out of action with a season-ending Achilles injury, Taylor failed to eclipse 100 rushing yards in each of his final 7 starts, and not by coincidence, Indy lost all 7 games. That being said, Taylor still earned Pro Bowl honors, and had another monstrous season when it was all said and done, rushing for 1,585 total rushing yards and a league-leading 18 rushing touchdowns on his also league-leading 323 total carries during all 17 starts this past year. There’s no better choice here for Indianapolis. While it’s a longshot again, ‘JT 4 MVP’ still has a nice ring to it.

title: Legendary Colts kicker Adam Vinatieri chooses presenter for Hall of Fame enshrinement
summary: Former legendary Indianapolis Colts placekicker Adam Vinatieri has chosen his presenter for his upcoming summer enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026. It’s none other than Colts team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon, as a tap of Vinatieri’s golden right kicking foot to her father, late former franchise team owner Jim […]
full_text: Feb 5, 2026; San Franciso, CA, USA; Adam Vinatieri during a press conference introducing the NFL Hall of Fame Class of 2026 at Palace of Fine Arts. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Former legendary Indianapolis Colts placekicker Adam Vinatieri has chosen his presenter for his upcoming summer enshrinement into the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026. It’s none other than Colts team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon, as a tap of Vinatieri’s golden right kicking foot to her father, late former franchise team owner Jim Irsay, as well as her entire family. a special moment for @cirsay from future HOFer @adamvinatieri . pic.twitter.com/GXcpkOaG16 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) July 23, 2026 It was Irsay, who was one of the driving forces that brought the already Hall of Fame bound Vinatieri, then as a New England Patriots sudden surprising free agent, to the Colts in the 2006 offseason. The Colts were hoping that Vinatieri’s Super Bowl winning pedigree, leadership, kicking consistency, and clutchness would improve their odds of finally hoisting up an elusive Super Bowl trophy after a lot of recent playoff heartbreak. Vinatieri instantly became one of the best free agent signings the franchise ever made. The Colts won the Super Bowl that same season with the 34-year-old Vinatieri, who was a perfect 5 for 5 in field goal attempts—including a converted 51-yarder, in the Divisional Round against the Baltimore Ravens in hostile road and even tougher weather conditions. His 5 field goals were the Colts only points of the game, as they narrowly beat the Ravens, 15-6, and advanced to the AFC Title Game and continued their magical title run. One First-Team NFL All-Pro honor, One Pro Bowl, 336 made field goals, and 507 converted extra points later, en route to becoming the NFL’s all-time leading scorer (2,673), and Vinatieri would kick for 14 more seasons until the ripe old age of 47-years-old in Indianapolis—kicking well until the 2019 campaign. It’s obviously a tremendous honor for Irsay-Gordon, her sisters, and their whole family to help induct the greatest kicker all-time in NFL history. The Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2026 will be enshrined on August 8th at Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton, Ohio. The 2026 enshrinement ceremony is scheduled to start at noon.

title: Cam Newton points out clear disrespect of the Colts
summary: “I can’t get no respect.” Perhaps Rodney Dangerfield was a fan of the Indianapolis Colts because that is exactly how it feels around here sometimes. We see a lot of the same with the Pacers. A small market kills a team’s chances at nationally televised games, regardless of how good they may be. It’s worse […]
full_text: The team watches as Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle Colby Wooden (96) kicks at the end of practice during the team’s minicamp Thursday, June 11, 2026, at the Indiana Farm Bureau Football Center in Indianapolis. | Christine Tannous/IndyStar / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images “I can’t get no respect.” Perhaps Rodney Dangerfield was a fan of the Indianapolis Colts because that is exactly how it feels around here sometimes. We see a lot of the same with the Pacers. A small market kills a team’s chances at nationally televised games, regardless of how good they may be. It’s worse in the NBA, but the Colts are on the docket for only two primetime games. That is straight up disrespectful when compared to the rest of the league. The Downs brothers, Josh and Caleb, have a podcast on which Cam Newton was a recent guest. Caleb was drafted by the Cowboys, so you know they are going to get a disproportionate number of games under the lights no matter how good they are. With six games set for primetime, Newton quipped, “Caleb … you’re walking into a Netflix special. Josh over there went to a team that’s barely on Tubi.” It may sound rude on the surface, but it’s a joke that rings true. Even the 4:25 slot is barren for the Colts this year. Unless you live in the area or have NFL Sunday Ticket, the chances of seeing a Colts game are low. It’s hard to yell foul completely on this one for a few reasons. The Colts had a great start to the year, but a rough finish. They missed the playoffs. Should that type of team be rewarded? Additionally, the NFL cares about money and not much else. Wherever LeBron James goes, so goes the money. That is why Adam Silver can’t make the schedule. I have watched some horrible Christmas Day Lakers games while much better, small market teams sat at home. Exact same concept in the NFL. Just like a Thunder-Pacers Finals wasn’t as lucrative as a Knicks-Spurs Finals, the NFL prefers huge markets on its biggest stages. Indianapolis, as great as it is, just can’t compete in that arena. There aren’t many teams with fewer primetime games than the Colts. You’d have to scrape the bottom of the barrel of teams to find some with less. Here is the good news. With success, games can be flexed, and what time the Colts play doesn’t matter much. Winning is all that matters. The Colts, just like the Pacers, have to force their respective leagues to have no choice but to put them in the national spotlight. It isn’t easy, but if the Colts win and continue that in future seasons, expect more big time games in big time spots. They have to earn it first.
author: Jon Spradley

full_text: I guess we could start by eliminating those who would not be considered longshots. No starter from a year ago should be in that category. I would also eliminate our first two draft picks, as they are being penciled in as starters as well. As far as free agent acquisitions, Davis-Gaither has a pretty clear path to starting, as does Arden Key. Both should, and frankly need to be, to see the Colts defense improve enough to elevate the entire team. Maybe not every starter should be being counted on as major contributors? For me, if Travis emerged as a player that you start looking at wanting to lock up, that would mean he was making a pretty huge contribution. Fending off Farmer or Goncalves, would be setting the OL up for a couple of years of strong continuity. I would call Farmer a long-shot, but just barely. I don’t think many would be shocked if he won a role, but he does have a hill to climb as a rookie. Seeing Dulin, NWI, Gould, or Burks might be candidates, if one of them holds on to a role that many want to see a proven veteran be brought in to take. Either of our draft picks, Giddens or McGowan, would be logical choices, provided they win a role or see the field often enough to help. Seeing AR or Leonard become the starter for any stretch, would mean that something went wrong. But, should either get the opportunity and run with it, it certainly would change the narrative for 2027. There is a decent chance that Haulcey gets the first shot at Safety aside Bynum. There are some players who might push him, or push for time as a 3rd Safety/coverage LB. Wohler, Thomas, and Owens might get some opportunities, should Haulcey not take the role by the horns. If Ward or Sauce are not on the field, we have spent unwisely. If Walley is not on the field, we have assumed too much. It would, however, open up a chance to see if Taylor-Britt’s experience in the defense might play well. We have seen the other candidates at corner and a leap would have to be considered in the longshot range. Boettcher is interesting prospect. Although not truly hyped, he doesn’t have a proven player to rise above. I think if Carlies really had something, we would have seen it by now. Behind Grover, the most likely options are Wooden and Adebawore to have some impact. On the edge, JTT and Clemons are the “vets”, along with the rookies Gumbs and Curry. For a successful season, we probably really need 3 – 5 of these guys show some positive gains during the season. The depth lacks star power, but that is the case for all 32 in the NFL. Who is your choice as the long shot to make us forget the guy he is replacing? Obviously, the skill positions get the best opportunity to be seen as contributors. If one of the WRs or RBs happen to put together a nice season, it will get noticed more than if Adebawore continues to be a nice rotation piece. I expect Dulin to win that WR3 and to play well. Jones will find him often enough to lessen the focus on the rest of the receiving corps. If he simply catches the ball past the sticks with any sort of consistency, losing Pittman will not feel like as much of a hit. But, the guy I going to choose as my “longshot” contributor is JTT. He’s endured his period of not having Lou’s trust and he has the talent to be the best option opposite Latu. I think he will end up rising above Key, Clemons, and the rookies, to start being the best version of himself.

title: 2 All-Important Jaguars to Watch at 2026 Training Camp
summary: 2026 NFL training camps are about to kick off around the league, turning America’s attention back from fútbol to football. Travis and I will be out at the Miller Electric Center throughout the next few weeks to report back on your Jacksonville Jaguars. While he monitors several positional battles, I’ll be keeping an eye on […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - MAY 09: General manager James Gladstone talks with Nate Boerkircher #87 and Tanner Koziol #89 of the Jacksonville Jaguars walks off the field during rookie minicamp at Miller Electric Center on May 09, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images 2026 NFL training camps are about to kick off around the league, turning America’s attention back from fútbol to football. Travis and I will be out at the Miller Electric Center throughout the next few weeks to report back on your Jacksonville Jaguars. While he monitors several positional battles , I’ll be keeping an eye on two players in particular. TE Nate Boerkircher Jacksonville’s skill player lineup for 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WRs) looks impressive on paper. The starting receivers will be Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington, and Jakobi Meyers; the top tight end will be Brenton Strange; and the lead running back role will rotate between Bhayshul Tuten, Chris Rodriguez Jr., and LeQuint Allen Jr. The Jaguars are equipped for lighter packages as well. 10 personnel (1 RB, 0 TEs, 4 WRs) would allow Travis Hunter to play alongside those aforementioned wideouts, while 21 personnel (2 RBs, 1 TE, 2 WRs) — specifically, “pony” packages that field two receiving-capable backs as opposed to a tailback and a fullback — is another potential wrinkle to create schematic advantages. But what about when the offense wants to put heavier bodies on the field? Liam Coen could experiment with jumbo packages that add an extra offensive lineman to the equation, as he did on 108 snaps (sixth-most in the NFL) in his first year as Jaguars head coach. But that was more so a necessity than a luxury. About halfway through the 2025 season, Strange was placed on injured reserve, Hunter Long and Quintin Morris missed five combined games, and Johnny Mundt was at one point a healthy scratch. A lack of tight end availability gave way to more jumbo package opportunities. Plays with extra offensive linemen will still be part of Coen’s offense, but he’ll want to scale back those looks in favor of ones with multiple tight ends. The return of 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TEs, 2 WRs) and 13 personnel (1 RB, 3 TEs, 1 WR) to a league ruled by three-receiver sets is perhaps the top schematic story of this offseason. Jacksonville re-signed Morris before selecting two tight ends, Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol, in a draft that saw 22 tight ends in total go off the board (most since 2002). As a nearly-25-year-old prospect with just 38 career receptions, the selection of Boerkircher at No. 56 overall originally caught observers off guard. He’s an intriguing athlete, sure, but a near-top-50 selection? For someone who projects to be a No. 2 tight end? Really? Really. The Jags liked Morris enough to bring him back, and Long is still on the roster, but they’re hoping to see Boerkircher earn a Week 1 role as a complementary piece to Strange. During OTAs in June, Coen hinted toward a larger receiving workload for his top tight end so long as Boerkircher can hold up as a blocker. “As much as man, we love Brenton Strange blocking and he’s so tough, he wants to do it, he’s physical, he’ll bite you. He also missed some time last year … when you look at when he has production what our record looks like, it’s kind of interesting to see. And so, allowing Brenton to continue to do what he does well, but also to maybe take some of that wear and tear, some of the pounding that it takes when you’re blocking the Travon Walkers of the world and Josh Hines-Allens of the world, getting him matched up more on those linebackers and safeties and now he’s an advantage for us. Now we have an edge. So, we always feel good about Strange blocking at the point of attack, but we needed some help there. Being able to provide Strange an option to go maybe split out or go block other people that maybe keep him out of some of those one-on-one big situations, I think that’s going to help us tremendously.” I’m prepared to be underwhelmed by Boerkircher’s impact in the pass game for the duration of his rookie season. However, if he can hold his own in the trenches as early as training camp, I’ll feel much more comfortable about the flexibility of Coen’s offense entering the 2026 season. EDGE Travon Walker At the NFL’s annual league meetings back in March, Coen revealed a bold goal he set for Walker. “I had an almost two-hour meeting with him at the end of the season. Just what that looked like in terms of dominating. You know, I was with Aaron Donald in L.A., and we literally had to take him out of practice in order for us to gain yards on offense. And so, if you want to get where you want to go, and where we want you to go, and where you can go, I need to be taking you out of practice so that we can operate on offense. I want that kind of destruction and mindset and mentality. And he was on the same page about it.” “Not talent, not anything about their length and size and anything that way. It’s just habits. Elite habits, elite practice preparation, game preparation, that. Those habits. The way that you practice on a day-to-day basis. I’d better be taking you out of the practice for us to operate. You should disrupt the entire thing in order for us to operate. I want that.” Let’s see if we get it! Walker does have a lot of momentum entering this season, and not just because he’s $110 million richer . After ranking top-15 among all NFL defenders in sacks (2) and pressures (12) through the first three games of last season, he sustained the first of several injuries in Week 4, but continued to play relatively well nonetheless. The former Bulldog offers defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile the type of X’s and O’s advantage that Coen is hoping to get out of Boerkircher. On The Brent & Austen Show in April, Campanile said Walker’s versatility “is really what enables us to do a lot of the things that we do.” “A guy like Travon lets us play so many different fronts over the course of the game with the same personnel grouping that it makes it hard for the offense to ever get a gauge on what you’re going to be in in terms of the front. It’s one thing in the backend, you know, to be multiple and changing coverages and all that, but to be able to come out and be in over defense, be in under defense, be in bear, be in 6-1 defense, you know, be in loaded fronts. You really have to have a guy who’s versatile enough to do that.” The now-healthy and wealthy Walker started to flash those AD-like habits at OTAs, to the delight of his head coach. “Travon Walker showed up in a big way, especially when we got into some competitive situations, doing what I challenged him with, which was to dominate. Through the first two days of minicamp, he didn’t lose many reps.” Jacksonville’s roster is stocked with high-potential first-round picks. Walker, Anton Harrison, Brian Thomas Jr., and Travis Hunter are already significant contributors, but to take a leap in the NFL hierarchy, the Jaguars will need these players to take a leap individually. It starts with the guy who just got paid. Jaguars fans, let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

The team is hopeful Mahomes is cleared for training camp in the upcoming days, according to SI.com’s Albert Breer. But, like Daniel Jones, there’s a difference between being on the field and looking completely healthy. The Chiefs had a rough 2025 season and the only way they bounce back is if Mahomes is back to an MVP level. Jon Gruden and Ronde Barber will call Buccaneers-Chiefs preseason game | Pro Football Talk The Buccaneers announced that Gruden and Barber will be on the call for their August 22 home game against the Chiefs. Gruden has said he wants to be a play-by-play announcer, and now he will be, at least for one preseason game, for the franchise he coached to a Super Bowl XXXVII victory after the 2002 season. Barber was a Hall of Fame player on that team. Around the NFL Free-agent WR Tyreek Hill provides update after season-ending injury: ‘No power in my left leg’ | NFL.com “So it’s about 10 months after doing two surgeries,” Hill said. “My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg at all, so I’m trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it’s one day at a time.” The lack of a timetable for Hill to sign with a team falls in line with what his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said last month. Ravens waive rookie Diego Pavia to make room for Ethan Pocic | ESPN After throwing 29 touchdown passes and rushing for 10 more, Pavia was named first-team All-American and SEC Offensive Player of the Year and won the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award as the best upperclassman quarterback in college football.
