title: Can the Chiefs afford a ‘diet version’ of Patrick Mahomes in 2026?
summary: On Thursday morning, ESPN’s “Get Up” crew previewed the 2026 NFL season with a question about the Kansas City Chiefs: how good are the Chiefs if quarterback Patrick Mahomes can’t be 100% healthy this season? The question was first answered by former NFL wide receiver Andrew Hawkins, who doubted the team has enough “on the […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 23: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs attempts a pass while under pressure from Adetomiwa Adebawore #95 of the Indianapolis Colts in the third quarter of the game at Arrowhead Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday morning, ESPN’s “Get Up” crew previewed the 2026 NFL season with a question about the Kansas City Chiefs : how good are the Chiefs if quarterback Patrick Mahomes can’t be 100% healthy this season? The question was first answered by former NFL wide receiver Andrew Hawkins, who doubted the team has enough “on the outside” to succeed like the organization has in past years of the Mahomes era, before pointing out that the quarterback may need to tweak his game to make it work. “Does he need to change his style? He probably will need to,” Hawkins said. “He’s a little older, he’s obviously coming off injury, I don’t think that he can.” “They can’t afford a diet version of Patrick Mahomes and still expect to be as good as they’ve been in his career,” Hawkins concluded. NFL insider Adam Schefter responded to Hawkins with the context of the team’s actions this offseason, looking to strengthen the team around a recovering Mahomes. “This is why you break the bank and sign Kenneth Walker III,” Schefter said. “This is why you bring in Eric Bieniemy as your offensive coordinator. This is why you plan to have the ground game, the rushing attack as much a part of your offense as it has been in any recent season.” Former NFL general manager Mike Tannenbaum countered Schefter with the significance of the pass game in having an elite run game. “If [they] don’t have somebody on the outside, you’re going to load the box and say, ‘Hey, make somebody on the outside beat us, you’re going to load the box, we’re not going to let Walker be that guy,‘” Tannenbaum noted. Former NFL offensive lineman Damien Woody finished the segment with a definitive statement on where he believes the Chiefs are in the pecking order this season. “I don’t know if any Andy Reid team is going to go ground and pound,” Woody mentioned. “But this might be the first year in quite some time where they’re going to be forced to have an identity on offense because of the lack of explosiveness in the passing game.” “This team needs an identity,” Woody continued. “Too many times over the last few years, we saw the team ask Patrick Mahomes to basically throw on his cape and try to will this team to win, and I don’t think that’s going to be the case for this team moving forward this year. Couple that with all the change on the defensive side of the ball, I look at this Kansas City Chiefs team, quite honestly, as the third-best team in the AFC West.” Are the Chiefs doomed if Mahomes can’t play like himself this season, or can he make adjustments to his game and get back to winning as he moves closer to 100%? ESPN doubts it; what do you think?

title: 53 Days, only 53 touches for Xavier Worthy last season
summary: We are 53 days away from the Kansas City Chiefs‘ season-opening game against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. The No. 53 jersey will be worn by linebacker Kam Arnold this preseason. He was an undrafted free agent signed by the Washington Commanders following the 2025 draft, but the Chiefs scooped […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 28: Xavier Worthy #1 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs with the football in the first quarter during the NFL 2025 game between Baltimore Ravens and Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Kansas City, United States. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are 53 days away from the Kansas City Chiefs ‘ season-opening game against the Denver Broncos on “Monday Night Football” in Week 1. The No. 53 jersey will be worn by linebacker Kam Arnold this preseason. He was an undrafted free agent signed by the Washington Commanders following the 2025 draft, but the Chiefs scooped him up towards the end of the season for the practice squad when he was cut last year. In team history, the uniform seems to always be donned by a linebacker: The memorable No. 53s in franchise history Marvcus Patton (1999 – 2002) Anthony Hitchens (2018 – 2021) Whitney Paul (1976 – 1981, 1986) DeMorrio Williams (2008 – 2011) Ramik Wilson (2015 – 2017) It’s an interesting group of Chiefs linebackers who have made an impact with the No. 53 jersey in Kansas City. Hitchens was the middle linebacker at the beginning of the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, when the Chiefs won Super Bowl LIV, but Chiefs Kingdom was ready for Nick Bolton to take over in the middle of the defense. Patton filled up the box score during his four seasons as a starter in Kansas City. In 1999, after nine years playing elsewhere, he racked up 105 tackles, 16 tackles for loss, 6.5 sacks, four passes defended and three fumble recoveries. He was named team MVP that season. That level of production held steady through the 2002 season, his last in the NFL at the age of 35. 53: The number of times Xavier Worthy caught or rushed the ball last season Over the 14 games wide receiver Xavier Worthy played in 2025, he was given the ball 53 times, less than four touches per game. After the shoulder injury he suffered during Week 1, it was clear that Worthy’s usage was limited in the offense, and that has been reiterated by head coach Andy Reid this offseason. He was protected with his route tree, but that can’t continue to be the case in full health. He is too explosive in the open field, especially on quick-hitting plays like receiver screens and shallow crossing routes, to not have a higher volume of usage moving forward. Worthy has a lot to prove as an NFL player, but one of the biggest things will be his durability. He has shown toughness and flashes of play strength given his physique, but the team needs his full-go playmaking all season in 2026.

title: Chiefs News: KCK Mayor says Chiefs’ new stadium location still unknown
summary: The latest We have known about the Kansas City Chiefs’ future move across state lines to a brand-new, enclosed stadium in Wyandotte County for a little under a year now. On Wednesday, renderings of what the new home of the Chiefs will look like were released. There was plenty of positive and negative reaction to […]
full_text: Arrowhead Stadium at the Truman Sports Complex in Kansas City. (Tammy Ljungblad/Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The latest We have known about the Kansas City Chiefs ’ future move across state lines to a brand-new, enclosed stadium in Wyandotte County for a little under a year now. On Wednesday, renderings of what the new home of the Chiefs will look like were released. There was plenty of positive and negative reaction to the internal and external design, along with the number of parking spaces, but the exact location of this venue has not been revealed. KCK mayor reacts to Chiefs stadium renderings, says exact location still unknown | KCTV5 Kansas City, Kansas Mayor Christal Watson said she is excited by the six renderings the Kansas City Chiefs released Wednesday of their planned domed stadium — but acknowledged she has no answers yet on where exactly within the Star Bond District the facility will be built. “The renderings look wonderful,” Watson said. “There’s this old and new look to them, keeping the integrity of Arrowhead, but yet this new little twist, which is the dome.” Watson said the city has no role in determining the stadium’s precise location within the financing district. Kansas City Chiefs Select Manica To Design New Domed Stadium | Forbes Fully enclosed with a translucent ETFE roof, Manica hopes to improve on many of the team’s traditions. The more than 20,000 parking spaces in the lot will be designed to specifically enhance the tailgating experience. The stadium’s size, shape and roof geometry were determined after audio engineers studied the design to maximize crowd noise. The seating bowl design is reminiscent of the current Arrowhead Stadium with a Drum Deck for celebrations and a prominent placement of the Chiefs Ring of Honor above the bowl. Preview every WR on the KC Chiefs’ 90-man roster before training camp | Chiefs Wire The Chiefs gave Remigio playing time as a kick/punt returner last year, but the experiment largely failed. As a receiver, Remigio only managed to record one reception for 24 yards in 2025. His familiarity with Kansas City’s coaching staff may work in Remigio’s favor, but it will likely take Herculean performances in training camp and the preseason to get the Chiefs to take a mulligan on him. 2026 cap number: $1,075,000 Fantasy Football Sleepers, Busts & Predictions: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs | Yahoo! Sports Sleeper: Jalen Royals, WR Kansas City’s top pass catchers are (in some order) a tight end who turns 37 in October, a wide receiver who it seems is one off-field misstep away from being out of football, and a former first-rounder who only scored one touchdown and 532 yards last year despite playing as the team’s borderline WR1 much of the year. After those three (Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy, in order), the next options are guys like Tyquan Thornton, fifth-round rookie Cyrus Allen, backup tight end Noah Gray and Jalen Royals. In short, this team is not flush with pass-catching options, and if Patrick Mahomes can return healthy, someone’s going to have to step up, especially if Kelce really is over the age cliff and/or Rice can’t get his head on right. Royals did essentially nothing as a fourth-round rookie last year, not even seeing a target until he had 2 receptions for 4 yards on 3 targets in Week 18. 5 things that stand out to fans about renderings of new Chiefs stadium in Kansas | The Kansas City Star 5. A longshot hope for spiral walkways World Cup fans learned just how fun that can be after a game, and Chiefs fans think it’s a big part of their gameday experience. “Spiral walkways with unnecessary cladding we can bang on before and after the game or I’m out,” one wrote. Here is more of what was shared on X and Reddit … “As much as leaving ol’ Arrowhead pains me to my soul,” one person shared on Reddit, “if this is going to be the replacement, I feel pretty darn good about it.” Another wrote: “Use real grass, no turf! Looks sweet, I hope the real thing ends up looking similar to these renderings. Like that they’re keeping the general Arrowhead shape in this. Wish they were never leaving, but if we’re gonna leave might as well do it right.” Around the NFL Seahawks’ Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 | ESPN According to a source, the Seahawks knew that Emmanwori might eventually require surgery. He tried to manage his ankle over the offseason, but as he was ramping up for the start of training camp, he continued to experience soreness and opted to have an arthroscopic procedure that was performed earlier this month. After returning from his initial ankle injury, Emmanwori emerged as a versatile playmaker and a key part of Seattle’s top-ranked scoring defense. Serving as the Seahawks’ third safety, Emmanwori recorded 11 passes defended, 2.5 sacks and an interception in 14 regular-season games on his way to finishing second in voting for Associated Press Rookie of the Year. Jimmy Garoppolo open to playing after considering retirement | NFL.com After contemplating calling it a career earlier this offseason, Garoppolo has decided not to retire and would come back to play in the right situation, NFL Network Insider Mike Garafolo reported Wednesday. A 12-season NFL veteran with two Super Bowl rings won during his time with the New England Patriots, Garoppolo was with the Los Angeles Rams the last two seasons as Matthew Stafford’s backup. There is nothing imminent, per Garafolo, who added it might take an injury to a quarterback or the need for a veteran to get into the mix. Tyreek Hill says in rehab video he is trying to regain power in his left leg | Pro Football Talk “So it’s about 10 months after doing two surgeries,” Hill said. “My left leg is the one that I injured. I have no power in my left leg, so I’m trying to regain all the power back in my left leg. But it’s one day at a time.” In the 1-minute, 38-second social media post, titled Cheetah, Reborn, Hill runs and jumps outside on turf, on a basketball court and in a pool at what appears to be his Florida home. “I ain’t going to tell you what my timeline is, but timeline looking real good right now, man,” Hill said. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs with the highest career stakes this season: Felix Anudike-Uzomah Several veteran edge rushers remain unsigned and may simply plan to sign after some of the hot summer training camp practices have passed. The Chiefs could very well plan to add a veteran defensive end, similar to adding Carlos Dunlap early in 2022’s camp. Without such a move, Anudike-Uzomah by default appears set to blow past the 31% of defensive snaps he played in 2024. In a long awaited announcement, the Rams finally pulled back the curtain on their new threads to the NFL and Rams fans. As speculated, the two new uniforms are tribute to past teams. In the 1940s and 1950s, the Rams wore yellow uniforms and that was first alternate revealed. The other is all white and blue uniform to honor the 1960s and the Fearsome Foursome teams. The Los Angeles Rams have just dropped their two new uniforms. Classic Sol and Fearsome White. What’s your rank of the entire wardrobe, 1 – 5? pic.twitter.com/1xJD55uwKY — RAMS REPORT🗯 (@RamsNFLReport) July 24, 2026 The Rams are scheduled to wear the Classic Sol uniforms for Week 2 vs the New York Giants and Week 13 vs the Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams first “home” game will be in Week 2, so we will get to see those threads early on. The decision to wear them again in Week 13 against the Chiefs makes a lot of sense considering the Rams wore an all-yellow uniform in 2018 against the Chiefs in what went down as arguably the greatest regular season football game of all time. The Rams won 54-51 thanks to a Gerald Everett touchdown with less than 2 minutes remaining. The Chiefs-Rams game this year will also be on prime time television, Thursday Night Football presented by Amazon Prime. The Fearsome White uniforms will be worn against the Green Bay Packers in the first ever Thanksgiving Eve game on November 25. RATE THESE NEW LOS ANGELES #RAMS ALTERNATE WHITE UNIFORMS WITH THE SPECIAL BLUE HELMETS… FROM 1 TO 10 pic.twitter.com/gcbJlntT0X — MLFootball (@MLFootball) July 24, 2026 The Rams now have five uniform sets for the 2026 season. title: ESPN ranks the Rams last in under-25 talent
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were ranked last in having talent under the age of 25 by Aaron Schatz for ESPN, and when you look at the methodology he used, that’s fair. However, I’m not really sure what he’s trying to say with those rankings. But should the Rams fans be concerned by this apparent lack […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams were ranked last in having talent under the age of 25 by Aaron Schatz for ESPN , and when you look at the methodology he used, that’s fair. However, I’m not really sure what he’s trying to say with those rankings. But should the Rams fans be concerned by this apparent lack of young talent? Not really. Because Schatz starts by saying; “When we look at which NFL teams are set up for future success, a big part of that is considering how much young talent is on each roster.” What he fails to point out is how far in the future he’s looking. In the case of the Rams, the future is basically tomorrow. The Methodology The first two components of Schatz’s methodology virtually guarantee the Rams’ last-place ranking. Number of starts made by players under 25 years old Number of snaps played by players under 25 years old The Rams have two players who qualify : Kamren Kinchens and Terrance Ferguson. However, if we make our own list of Rams players under…let’s say 27 years old, it adds a few notables. Blake Corum Kyren Williams CJ Daniels Puka Nacua Jordan Whittington Steve Avila Warren McClendon Desjuan Johnson Omar Speights Emmanuel Forbes Trent McDuffie Josh Wallace Jaylen McCullough The point here is that the Rams have an abundance of very good young talent. Why the Rams may be lacking in ‘younger’ talent Over the last five years, the entry age of all drafted players is close to 24 . That drops to 22-ish for first-round picks and can probably be attributed to young, uber-talented guys declaring as soon as possible. They, or their agents, know the really big contracts are the second ones, or even the third ones. The non-first-rounders tend to stay in school longer because of the money available through NIL contracts and the fact that the transfer portal gives them more opportunities to grow as players and find a system that best displays their talents. Given that the Rams treat first-round picks as bargaining chips, they’ve used first-round picks three times in the last ten years, it’s no wonder they have fewer players than most under 25 given these averages. In addition, while many GMs tend to stay away from ‘older’ players coming out in the draft recently, Rams GM Les Snead seems to care less than most. Byron Young, for example, was 25 when the Rams drafted him in the third round of the 2023 draft and offers an example of age not being a detriment to a player’s development. While the Rams are absolutely set for this season , the picture gets a little blurry starting next year. With only four draft picks in the 2027 draft and a host of players eligible for free agency, Snead and head coach Sean McVay have a lot of decisions to make for the Rams’ next future.

title: Which broadcast team do you like calling Rams games?
summary: Before every Los Angeles Rams game, fans know they’ll hear a different voice depending on which network is carrying the broadcast. Some viewers enjoy deep X’s and O’s analysis, while others prefer energetic storytelling, humor, or the ability to explain complex plays in simple terms. The play-by-play announcer sets the pace, the analyst provides insight, […]
full_text: Before every Los Angeles Rams game, fans know they’ll hear a different voice depending on which network is carrying the broadcast. Some viewers enjoy deep X’s and O’s analysis, while others prefer energetic storytelling, humor, or the ability to explain complex plays in simple terms. The play-by-play announcer sets the pace, the analyst provides insight, and the sideline reporter delivers crucial injury updates, coaching interviews, and breaking news throughout the game. Every broadcast team has its own personality, making the viewing experience unique. Whether it’s a national Sunday afternoon matchup, a primetime showdown, or a postseason battle, the booth can influence how memorable a game becomes. Here are five of the NFL’s most recognizable broadcast teams that Rams fans regularly hear throughout the season. 1. FOX Play-by-Play: Kevin Burkhardt Analyst: Tom Brady Sideline Reporter: Erin Andrews FOX is the network Rams fans probably hear the most due to the NFC television package. Kevin Burkhardt keeps the broadcast moving with a steady, conversational style, while Tom Brady brings the perspective of arguably the greatest quarterback in NFL history. Erin Andrews remains one of the league’s most recognizable sideline reporters, providing updates on injuries, coaching decisions, and player interviews. The combination offers a balance of star power, technical analysis, and polished presentation that many fans have grown accustomed to during marquee NFC matchups. 2. CBS Play-by-Play: Jim Nantz Analyst: Tony Romo Sideline Reporter: Tracy Wolfson Although CBS primarily broadcasts AFC games, Rams fans occasionally hear this crew during interconference contests or nationally significant games. Jim Nantz’s smooth delivery has become synonymous with major sporting events, while Tony Romo is known for predicting offensive concepts before the snap and explaining quarterback decisions in real time. Tracy Wolfson rounds out the crew by delivering timely reports from the sidelines and providing valuable context throughout the game. 3. ESPN Monday Night Football Play-by-Play: Joe Buck Analyst: Troy Aikman Sideline Reporters: Lisa Salters and Laura Rutledge Monday Night Football continues to be one of the NFL’s premier television windows. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have spent decades calling some of football’s biggest moments together, giving viewers a familiar and polished presentation. Lisa Salters has become one of the most respected sideline reporters in sports television, while Laura Rutledge contributes additional reporting, interviews, and pregame coverage, creating one of the deepest broadcast teams in the NFL. 4. NBC Sunday Night Football Play-by-Play: Mike Tirico Analyst: Cris Collinsworth Sideline Reporter: Melissa Stark Many fans consider Sunday Night Football the NFL’s flagship weekly broadcast. Mike Tirico’s versatility and professionalism pair well with Cris Collinsworth’s detailed breakdowns of offensive and defensive strategy. Melissa Stark provides injury updates, coaching information, and player features from the sidelines. When the Rams appear in primetime on NBC, the production value and atmosphere often make the game feel like a playoff event. 5. Prime Video Thursday Night Football Play-by-Play: Al Michaels Analyst: Kirk Herbstreit Sideline Reporter: Kaylee Hartung Thursday Night Football has quickly developed its own identity. Legendary broadcaster Al Michaels continues to bring decades of experience to the booth, while Kirk Herbstreit successfully transitioned from college football into NFL analysis. Kaylee Hartung provides reports from field level, delivering injury updates and interviews while keeping viewers informed throughout the evening. Your Pick Every Rams fan values something different in a broadcast. Some enjoy analysts who dissect coverages and blitz packages. Others prefer personalities who tell stories and create excitement around big moments. Some viewers prioritize chemistry between the booth members, while others believe the sideline reporter plays an equally important role by delivering fast, accurate information during critical situations. So which broadcast team is your favorite when watching the Rams? Maybe, you like a lesser known crew. Make your feelings known Ram Nation!

title: Raiders and Fernando Mendoza reach deal, Rams and Ty Simpson next?
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders reached an agreement on a rookie deal with Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. The deal is reportedly a $57.27 million deal that is fully guaranteed with a fifth year option. Now that that domino has fallen, will Ty Simpon’s deal with the Los Angeles Rams […]
full_text: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 15: Fernando Mendoza accepts the Best College Athlete, Men's Sports award onstage during the 2026 ESPY Awards at David H. Koch Theater at Lincoln Center on July 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Mike Coppola/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders reached an agreement on a rookie deal with Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. The deal is reportedly a $57.27 million deal that is fully guaranteed with a fifth year option. Now that that domino has fallen, will Ty Simpon’s deal with the Los Angeles Rams be next? He’s the only player taken in the first round of the 2026 draft waiting to be signed. Though heavily debated as a good or bad move, Simpson was selected by the Rams with the 13th overall pick. That’s more than 10 picks after Mendoza, but still within the top-15 of the draft. How much will those picks in-between impact Simpson’s deal? For comparison’s sake, Bo Nix was taken in the 2024 NFL Draft with the 12th overall pick, and spotrac.com lists Nix’s deal as an $18,613,166 deal . The cap has gone up since 2024, so odds are Simpson will command a larger deal than Nix, but that’s not official, yet. If you use Google/AI (this is likely subject change), it’s expected that Simpson will fetch around a $25 million deal. That’s quite a bit more than Nix, but still well under Mendoza’s contract, which makes sense given that Mendoza was taken first overall as opposed to Simpson at pick 13. Unless something truly unprecedented happens, Simpson will be signing his deal with the Rams. It’s a matter of when and not if. With Mendoza’s contract now handled, that when (not if) may be sooner than it was prior to today. Stay tuned.

(Disney/Frank Micelotta) FERNANDO MENDOZA (Photo by Frank Micelotta/Disney via Getty Images) | Disney via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams don’t usually make first-round picks and maybe Ty Simpson’s prolonged waiting game to sign his rookie contract helps explain why, especially now that Fernando Mendoza is under contract. Mendoza and Simpson were the last two first-round picks who had not signed their rookie contracts, but that changed on Thursday as the Las Vegas Raiders officially locked down the first overall pick of the draft. Mendoza signed a four-year, $57 million deal, which we all knew would happen because of the rookie pay scale as per the CBA. We already know what Simpson is going to sign for, we already know it will be fully-guaranteed, but the Rams continue to work on “contract language” with the 13th overall pick. The only other two unsigned rookies in the NFL are quarterback Drew Allar and edge rusher Gabe Jacas. One finally is done: The Raiders and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza reached agreement today on a four-year, $57.2 million contract. With the Raiders rookies having reported to camp, Mendoza now can get to work. pic.twitter.com/5wBD7nP1UH — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) July 23, 2026 As per Blaine Grisak’s interview with Joel Corry of CBS Sports , the wait with Simpson is likely related to a signing bonus: “Simpson’s camp is probably insisting that the Rams extend the 2024 quarterback payment convention to him since he was drafted one slot lower than Nix,” said Corry. “Nearly every team besides the Jaguars and Rams requires offsets with salary guarantees for draft picks, including those selected in the top 10.” “Based on past practices, Simpson’s contract with the Rams shouldn’t contain offsets,” continued Corry. “The last time the Rams had a first-round pick, edge rusher Jared Verse in 2024, his contract did not contain offsets in the salary guarantees despite being the 19th overall selection.” The Rams report to camp on Saturday. Will Ty Simpson be there?

title: Rams-Bengals is the Super Bowl rematch we need
summary: Five seasons ago, the Los Angeles Rams hoisted the Lombardi Trophy on their home turf against the Cincinnati Bengals. With the Super Bowl returning to SoFi Stadium in February, Rams-Bengals for the NFL crown is the rematch we need this season. It’s not hard to imagine Los Angeles back in the big game, especially given […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 13: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams throws the ball during to the NFL Super Bowl LVI football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at SoFi Stadium on February 13, 2022 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Five seasons ago, the Los Angeles Rams hoisted the Lombardi Trophy on their home turf against the Cincinnati Bengals. With the Super Bowl returning to SoFi Stadium in February, Rams-Bengals for the NFL crown is the rematch we need this season. It’s not hard to imagine Los Angeles back in the big game, especially given their offseason, yet Cincy is much tougher to fathom. For starters, the Bengals have missed the playoffs three straight years after back-to-back AFC Championship appearances in 2021-22. They’ve been the definition of mediocrity, going 24-27 in that span, bottoming out at 6-11 in 2025. Former Rams assistant Zac Taylor has been on the hot seat for an eternity, it seems. The Bengals have an annoyingly patient front office, so Taylor coming close to winning a championship years ago has likely bought himself a lifetime appointment in Cincinnati. Joking aside, it’s truly a miracle that he’s the longest-tenured head coach in the AFC North, and tied for the fifth-longest in the league with the Packers’ Matt LaFleur. Much of the reason Cincy has missed the playoffs these last three seasons is their woeful defense. And woeful is putting it extremely kindly. The team finished dead last in most statistical categories in ‘25, and was especially a problem during Joe Burrow’s MVP-like campaign in 2024. This tweet pretty much sums up their defensive woes: Bengals 2024 Defense vs 2025 Defense pic.twitter.com/sYWhBnnOGH — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) January 5, 2026 Why should anyone be pining for a Rams-Bengals rematch? Burrow is the answer. When healthy — and that’s sadly a big ask anymore — he’s one of the best and most exciting quarterbacks in the league. He’s suffered through three injury-riddled seasons, including last year. The first two times, he won NFL Comeback Player of the Year, with the first en route to the Bengals’ Super Bowl berth. Plus, Burrow is just two seasons removed from the aforementioned MVP-like campaign. If Cincinnati fielded an average defense that season, he would’ve won the hardware handily, as MVP voters love eye-popping quarterback stats. Final 2024 regular season stats for #Bengals QB Joe Burrow • 460/652 • 4,918 passing yards • 43 passing TDs • 9 INTs pic.twitter.com/59mV68CvMq — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) January 5, 2025 The Bengals have also made plenty of investments on the defensive side of the ball this offseason. Cincy signed defensive end Boye Mafe, safeties Bryan Cook and Kyle Dugger, and defensive tackle Jonathan Allen in free agency, and traded for All-Pro Dexter Lawrence ahead of the NFL draft. On paper, the unit should be much improved, but given how terrible they’ve been lately, there’s a low bar for them to clear. Regardless of what the Bengals have done on the field in the last three seasons, they should not be slept on. The Athletic named them among the NFL’s underrated teams ahead of the 2026 season and praised the offseason overhaul that left them with “better depth.” FanDuel Sportsbook has Cincinnati at +2000 odds to win the Super Bowl and -198 odds to make the playoffs, eighth-best in the AFC. The Bengals came out of nowhere five years ago to make a surprise Super Bowl run against a powerhouse Rams squad. Fast-forward to now, and they have the chance to do the same against another elite L.A. team in the same stadium, this time with the Rams having former Cincy foe Myles Garrett in tow. A Super Bowl rematch is inevitable, as six such games have taken place since 2016, including Rams-Patriots in 2018. So, why not Rams-Bengals Part II? Aaron Donald might just make an appearance in the sequel as well, which is undoubtedly music to Burrow’s ears. Rams-Bengals was one of the most thrilling Super Bowls of the last decade, and the big game returns to Hollywood right as sequels continue drawing people in. Super Bowl rematches are typically hit or miss, yet this one could potentially break the box office this February if it were to happen.
author: Evan Craig

title: Myles Garrett predicted to break sacks record again
summary: Myles Garrett had an NFL record 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns last season, which is phenomenal, but his legacy could be even better if he improved on his mark in 2026 with the Los Angeles Rams. At least one NFL writer thinks that he will. It’s not that Garrett’s sack record is not legitimate, […]
full_text: Woodland Hills, - June 08:Rams Myles Garrett (95) at Rams practice on Monday, June 8, 2026. (Photo by David Crane/MediaNews Group/Los Angeles Daily News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Myles Garrett had an NFL record 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns last season, which is phenomenal, but his legacy could be even better if he improved on his mark in 2026 with the Los Angeles Rams. At least one NFL writer thinks that he will. It’s not that Garrett’s sack record is not legitimate, but imagine how much better his legacy would be if Garrett got to 23 sacks in 16 games instead of 17 games. Imagine if he did it with the Rams, for a good team, instead of with the Browns. And imagine if he didn’t just break the record, but that he shattered it. In making 61 predictions for the 2026 NFL season, SB Nation’s Jarrett Bailey went above and beyond when it came to predicting the type of first season that Garrett will have in L.A. : Myles Garrett breaks sack record for second straight year After recording 6.5 sacks in the first two weeks of the season, the Myles Garrett sack record watch becomes a focal point around the NFL for the second straight season. It doesn’t take him the full 17 games to achieve it this time around, though, as he gets to Baker Mayfield in Week 15 to get sack No. 24 on the year before finishing the season with 25.5 and winning his second consecutive Defensive Player of the Year award. In addition to breaking the sacks record, Bailey also predicted that Garrett would have 3.5 sacks against the Giants in Week 2. That’s the type of start that Garrett will need to get off to in order to break his own record. Playing along side Aaron Donald couldn’t hurt, if that’s what happens. Bailey also predicted that the Rams will blow out the 49ers in Week 1 and eventually earn the number one seed. “Nothing groundbreaking here. The Rams essentially built their own version of the MonSTARS by trading for both Trent McDuffie and Myles Garrett to add to a team that already featured Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, and reigning MVP Matthew Stafford. They’ll win 14 games and get the top seed in the NFC.” However, he has the Dallas Cowboys winning the Super Bowl. I guess you can’t win ‘em all.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams going all-in on tight ends
summary: In 2025, the Los Angeles Rams offense evolved from a team that was primarily based on one tight end to a unit that embraced three. L.A. coach Sean McVay didn’t use the three tight end formation until Week 6 of the regular season and from then on, according to Next Gen Stats, proceeded to employ […]
full_text: In 2025, the Los Angeles Rams offense evolved from a team that was primarily based on one tight end to a unit that embraced three. L.A. coach Sean McVay didn’t use the three tight end formation until Week 6 of the regular season and from then on, according to Next Gen Stats, proceeded to employ it on 43 percent of plays going forward. The Rams appear to be all-in on staying with the multiple tight end offense. They basically left the wide receiver corps alone, only adding a Round 6 draft pick (CJ Daniels) and instead drafted another receiver-first tight end, Max Klare, in Round 2. They also re-signed veteran Tyler Higbee. At eight-strong, the L.A. tight end room is a deep, solid mix of veterans and youngsters. All have good hands, are good route runners, and can attack/stretch defenses. How many will be on the Rams opening roster? A likelihood of five and the in-house competition should testing for them all. Rams 13 personnel in 3 play sequence. PA wheel route to Ferguson w/ great protection (including a double team by the TEs). A true naked w/ motion at the snap and routes working back (look at the 49ers LBs). Zone run against two-high (that formation vs. that front) for a TD. pic.twitter.com/R6ztQwBlkG — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 11, 2025 Incumbents Colby Parkinson – 6’7” 252 lb. After five seasons in the NFL as a rotational player, Parkinson put up career best numbers in starts, snaps, targets, receptions, yards, touchdowns, and catch percentage. Is he ready for a breakout? Or is this his ceiling as a pro? Came out of college as a receiver-first tight end. Drafted by Seattle and Pete Carroll, the Seahawks used a lot of two tight end formations, but didn’t really harness the unit as weapons. Parkinson never really broke through over four seasons in the Great Northwest, his first three seasons were as TE#3. However, his usage did go up each season and in 2023, he was on the field for nearly 50 percent of snaps as TE#2. He also improved his blocking chops with Seattle and is now visibly bigger than when he entered the league. At his best, Parkinson shows good hands and an ability to to box out smaller defenders. He runs crisp routes and can be dangerous at all depth’s. Tyler Higbee – 6’6” 249 lb. The Rams brought Higbee back for 2026 on a two-year deal worth up to $8 mil and only half guaranteed, well-below his previous contract. Now 33 and entering his 11th season as the Rams longest tenured player, it will be interesting to see how the season wears on his body. He should be at his par early in the early going, but after being dogged by injuries for most of his career, will the Rams need him to play through the pain now that they have a fully stocked tight end room? It is quite likely that Higbee will no longer man a feature role in the Rams offense. But his role is not just dependent on the continued development of Terrance Ferguson and incoming Round 2 pick Max Klare, it may also hinge on how the youngsters are used in the 2026 offense. If they are in games as a pseudo-WR#3, Higbee should have a fair share of the rotation. He’s a better blocker than both youngsters and Sean McVay/Matthew Stafford are comfortable targeting him, particularly on screen passes. Davis Allen – 6’6” 245 lb. Allen enters his fourth season in L.A. and is in the final year of his rookie contract. He’s coming off his best season as a pro, playing in all 20 games with six starts and logging 585 offensive reps, second amongst Rams tight ends, along with 211 on special teams. According to Next Gen stats, Allen was on the field for 100 percent of snaps when the Rams aligned with three tight ends (“13” formation). He caught 24 of 33 targets (three drops) for 208 yards, accounting for three touchdowns and 12 first downs. For coming into the league as a receiver-first tight end, Allen has really worked on upgrading his blocking. Known a a vacuum coming onto the league, he strangely has had some drops. Likely best suited to shorter routes and red zone work, his burst is adequate, but lumbers in space. Good explosiveness for contested catches and jump balls. Solid hand/eye coordination and body control as well. Long, lean build doesn’t look much bigger than when he got to L.A. As a blocker, his technique and hand work are much improved, he squares up and seals off, and has become much more of drive blocker. check out Davis Allen (#87) pic.twitter.com/TAlM4cRHVz — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) January 19, 2025 Pedigreed draftees Terrance Ferguson – 6’5” 247 lb. Battled injuries in his rookie year, a groin early and a hamstring late in the season, but still gave a sneak preview of what Rams fans can expect from him. Ferguson showed an ability to get behind defenders and make big plays on the way to averaging 21 yards per catch. Although there are still some issues to be worked out, catch percentage and showing physicality on contested catches, he was able to show that he’s got the hybrid chops to blur the lines of traditional “11”, “12”, and “13” personnel groupings. His rookie film shows crisp routes with sharp breaks that can create separation and long stride, build up speed to run past heavier-footed safeties and linebackers. Did not show a lot of yards after catch running with the ball in a small sample size, 11 catches on 25 targets. Ferguson’s blocking was not near as bad as draft pundits laid out. Yes there’s plenty of room for improvement, he’s certainly not a power player to drive defenders or land stunning strikes, but he did show the ability to get his long arms extended, stay in front, and lock out/screen off. Max Klare – 6’4” 246 lb. Another receiver-first hybrid from the same basic mold as Ferguson. While not an explosive athlete, Klare has natural fluidity with good arm length and loose hips. He was a high school quarterback, tight end, punter, and kicker as well as a top-tier baseball player that competed on the diamond in his first college season. Check out his film at Purdue and you see another TE prospect that can stretch defenses getting deep, or pressuring at the mid areas of the field. The Boilermakers lined him up all over the formation. Ohio State used him in a more traditional manner, but his best work was done out of the slot. Good route runner with a varied tree and shows a good feel for open areas in zones. More of a body catcher and his hands rate as good, not great. Transitions up field quickly and has good moves in open space for a big guy. But he’s not a finesse runner, he shows good contact balance, can break tackles, and finishes falling forward. Improved his blocking at Ohio State, but needs needs play strength work and hand placement to become an NFL blocker. He is however, willing and is agile when blocking in space. Undrafted roster battle Dan Villari – 6’4” 243 lb. Originally signed by Michigan to play quarterback, didn’t play much in two years (one redshirt). Transferred to Syracuse and moved to tight end for 2022. Slightly above average arm length (32 1/4”) and big, soft hands. On film, Villari looks like a fluid athlete. Used on simpler routes, primarily out of the slot. He quickly (1.66 10-yard split) gets to his spot and gives his quarterback a nice square target. Nice feel for open space. Plucks passes with his hands away from his body and tucks them away quickly. As an open-field runner, I’d use “competitive” as the descriptor, he gets north/south in a hurry and stays low, running through contact. Developmental prospect, but you can see his base traits. Villari has been on the receiving end of passes just three short years. Interesting versatility, ran the ball out of wildcat formation, can throw pretty well, and has very good hands. Needs route-running work, although his short area agility, natural athleticism, and football IQ hints that he can handle a bigger route tree. Additional strength work is also needed, but looks to have playmaking potential. Rohan Jones – 6’2” 238 lb. A hybrid tight end with the formational versatility to play…

title: Who is your favorite NFL analyst?
summary: Every football fan has that one analyst they refuse to miss. Some tune in for detailed X’s and O’s. Others want breaking news the moment it happens. Some enjoy behind-the-scenes stories from inside NFL locker rooms, while others simply want to be entertained. The truth is there isn’t one “correct” answer when it comes to […]
full_text: Every football fan has that one analyst they refuse to miss. Some tune in for detailed X’s and O’s. Others want breaking news the moment it happens. Some enjoy behind-the-scenes stories from inside NFL locker rooms, while others simply want to be entertained. The truth is there isn’t one “correct” answer when it comes to the best NFL analyst. The right choice depends entirely on what you’re looking for as a fan. When deciding who deserves the title of your favorite NFL analyst, several factors come into play. Reliability, football knowledge, access to sources, communication style, and even personality all shape the viewing experience. Here are several of the biggest names and what makes each one stand out. Dan Orlovsky If you’re someone who enjoys learning the game itself, Dan Orlovsky has become one of the premier film analysts on television. His breakdowns frequently explain why a quarterback made a certain read, how route concepts stress defenses, or why an offensive coordinator called a particular play. Rather than simply saying a quarterback made a mistake, Orlovsky often shows exactly what happened by slowing down the film and teaching viewers how NFL offenses operate. His ability to simplify complicated concepts has helped casual fans better understand the sport without talking down to them. Body language… #nfllive pic.twitter.com/YRnM1jPLhN — Dan Orlovsky (@danorlovsky7) November 21, 2022 Brian Baldinger Brian Baldinger has carved out his own niche through his famous “Baldy’s Breakdowns.” Instead of focusing primarily on quarterbacks, Baldinger highlights offensive linemen, defensive linemen, linebackers, and role players who often don’t receive national attention. His energetic voiceovers and genuine appreciation for trench play have earned him a loyal following. For fans who believe football games are won up front, Baldinger provides some of the most enjoyable film content available. . @RamsNFL @PoonaF_95 always a place in this league for players like Poona..Strong as an Ox; healthy as a horse; heart of a lion! #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/TdYGZXtpje — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) July 16, 2026 Peter Schrager Some analysts specialize less in diagrams and more in relationships. Peter Schrager has built a reputation for providing context that statistics and highlight reels simply can’t capture. His extensive relationships throughout the NFL allow him to share stories from locker rooms, coaching staffs, and front offices that help explain why teams make certain decisions. Whether it’s free agency, coaching hires, or draft season, Schrager frequently provides valuable perspective that goes beyond the box score. The case for Brock Purdy as OROY pic.twitter.com/z5FAVHAenG — Peter Schrager (@PSchrags) January 10, 2023 Pat McAfee Not every football fan wants a classroom. Pat McAfee has transformed sports coverage by blending NFL discussion with comedy, interviews, and personality-driven entertainment. His show regularly features current players, former coaches, and league insiders in conversations that often feel more authentic than traditional television interviews. While some viewers may prefer a more formal style, others appreciate the relaxed atmosphere and unpredictable nature of McAfee’s program. If entertainment matters just as much as analysis, he’s difficult to beat. "My understanding is that Aaron Donald is getting in football shape right now.. It's gonna be a while before we hear a final decision on when he's coming back.. He's in his own pre training camp routine" @AdamSchefter #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/sOoNtUmTgz — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) July 21, 2026 Ian Rapoport For many fans, the most valuable analyst isn’t breaking down tape—he’s breaking the news. Ian Rapoport has become one of the NFL’s most trusted insiders, consistently delivering updates on injuries, trades, contracts, coaching decisions, and roster moves before they become official. Reliability is everything in the news business, and fans who prioritize accurate, timely information often gravitate toward insiders like Rapoport. During free agency, the NFL Draft, and training camp, his updates become must-follow material. Ian Rapoport on complaints that Daniel Jones is currently set to make more money than Lamar Jackson: “They’re trying. … Believe me, if Lamar Jackson would take the deal the Ravens have offered, he would make *far more* than $40 million [per year].” pic.twitter.com/2e6NHLc49v — Sarah Ellison (@sgellison) March 8, 2023 What Makes an NFL Analyst Your Favorite? There isn’t a universal checklist, but several qualities usually separate the very best from the rest: Reliability: Can you trust the information being reported? Football Knowledge: Does the analyst genuinely teach you something new? Unique Perspective: Do they offer insights others don’t? Entertainment Value: Are they enjoyable enough to keep watching? Communication: Can they explain complex football concepts in a way everyone understands? Access: Do they have relationships throughout the league that provide meaningful context? Different fans prioritize different qualities. A fantasy football manager might value injury updates and insider information above everything else. A former player or coach may prefer technical film study. Casual fans may simply want a show that’s fun to watch on a Sunday morning. Or perhaps another voice like Rich Eisen, Kurt Warner, Kay Adams, Mina Kimes, or Louis Riddick has earned the top spot on your list. Cast your Vote Now it’s your turn. Who is your favorite NFL analyst?

title: Rams 53-man roster created by over 100 Rams fans
summary: What would the Los Angeles Rams final 53-man roster look like if the fans were able to create it? Now we don’t just have the question, we also have the answer: A 53-man roster entirely created by Rams fans. Over 100 of them. This week, I created a tool allowing fans to create their own […]
full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA - JUNE 2: Cam Lampkin #21 of the Los Angeles Rams kneels in prayer during organized team activities workout at Rams Village at the Warner Center on June 2, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Kevin Terrell/Getty Images) | Getty Images What would the Los Angeles Rams final 53-man roster look like if the fans were able to create it? Now we don’t just have the question, we also have the answer: A 53-man roster entirely created by Rams fans. Over 100 of them. This week, I created a tool allowing fans to create their own 53-man roster and immediately over 100 of you responded and submitted your own personal 53-man rosters. The results were fascinating, giving us 26 players on offense, 24 on defense, and showing us which players are entering training camp on the roster bubble, according to some of the more divisive selections from Rams fans. Here is your consensus 53-man roster created by you, followed by some fascinating notes. Consensus 53-man roster (percentage of 53-man rosters the player appeared on) Offense (26) QB (3) Matthew Stafford (100%) Ty Simpson (96.1%) Stetson Bennett IV (84.5%) RB (4) Kyren Williams (100%) Blake Corum (100%) Jarquez Hunter (92.2%) Ronnie Rivers (51.5%) WR (6) Davante Adams (100%) Puka Nacua (100%) Jordan Whittington (97.1%) CJ Daniels (98.1%) Konata Mumpfield (95.1%) Xavier Smith (86.4%) TE (5) Tyler Higbee (98.1%) Colby Parkinson (98.1%) Terrance Ferguson (97.1%) Max Klare (97.1%) Davis Allen (87.4%) OL (8) Alaric Jackson (99.0%) Steve Avila (100%) Coleman Shelton (99.0%) Kevin Dotson (98.1%) Warren McClendon Jr. (99.0%) Beaux Limmer (88.3%) Justin Dedich (75.7%) David Quessenberry (73.8%) Defense (24) DL (6) Braden Fiske (100%) Kobie Turner (100%) Poona Ford (99.0%) Tyler Davis (84.5%) Ty Hamilton (71.8%) Tim Keenan III (70.9%) EDGE (4) Myles Garrett (100%) Byron Young (100%) Josaiah Stewart (98.1%) Desjuan Johnson (68.9%) LB (4) Nate Landman (99.0%) Shaun Dolac (97.1%) Omar Speights (97.1%) Grant Stuard (67.0%) DB (10) Jaylen Watson (99.0%) Trent McDuffie (100%) Emmanuel Forbes Jr. (98.1%) Quentin Lake (100%) Kam Curl (98.1%) Kamren Kinchens (100%) Jaylen McCollough (91.3%) Josh Wallace (84.5%) Cam Lampkin (46.6%) Special Teams (3) Ethan Evans (100%) Harrison Mevis (100%) Joe Cardona (99.0%) Wow, there you have it: The only 53-man roster projection that actually matters heading into camp because it’s the only one that was created by over 100 Rams fans working together. Fascinating Findings Bubble Players Last In: CB Cam Lampkin Lampkin is the last player in, collecting 46 percent of the votes. Lampkin, a 2024 undrafted free agent, has only played in four games, all in 2024, and has zero career snaps on defense. Making it on the roster here is a fascinating bubble choice going into camp. Now if you feel like eight offensive linemen is not enough, that’s certainly a switch that you could try to make, although that gives the offense an even bigger numbers advantage over the defense. This is a gap quite obviously created by Sean McVay’s apparent insistence to load the tight end room. Will the Rams actually end up keeping three quarterbacks, four running backs, six receivers, and five tight ends? I think that’s where the problem really lies. Not that Lampkin was the last player in. Xavier Smith’s biggest asset to the team will be as the punt returner, although we can’t sleep on his deep threat ability as a receiver either because L.A. doesn’t have many other options there. Last Out: OT AJ Arcuri Given AJ Jackson’s situation, Arcuri not making it onto the roster sounds even more unlikely than it already does. But he only got on 45 percent of your rosters. So you may be wondering: Does a suspended player count against the 53? The answer is no . Therefore, we could probably sub out Jackson for Arcuri in that case, but the NFL hasn’t announced any discipline for Jackson yet. Next Last Out: LB Nikhai Hill-Green If the last out isn’t Arcuri, then it’s an undrafted free agent rookie linebacker. Obviously, Hill-Green already has some fans going into camp: 37.9 percent of you to be precise. Here were the top-10 vote-getters who didn’t make the cut: Would you pound the table to keep any of these players? Tell me in the comments below. The 100-percent club These players were on every roster—and yes, Ty Simpson not being on this list means that one or two people were either joking or don’t understand how the NFL works. Matthew Stafford Blake Corum Kyren Williams Davante Adams Puka Nacua Steve Avila Braden Fiske Kobie Turner Myles Garrett Byron Young Trent McDuffie Kamren Kinchens Quentin Lake Harrison Mevis Ethan Evans We can also add these players to the list because not being 100 percent is just not realistic: LS Jake Cardona, CB Jaylen Watson, LT AJ Jackson (but suspended maybe), RT Warren McClendon, C Coleman Shelton, NT Poona Ford, LB Nate Landman, G Kevin Dotson, S Kam Curl, TE Max Klare, G Keagen Trost, and also probably TE Colby Parkinson, TE Tyler Higbee, TE Terrance Ferguson, TE Davis Allen—although to be fair could one trade happen because of the numbers? It’s possible. Basically, over half of the roster is guaranteed to make the 53. Most of the other half is over 80 percent to make it. The actual “bubble” wouldn’t start until you get to the last five or six spots. Players who were on 3 rosters or fewer These players have fans, but not many: QB Matthew Caldwell, 1 roster DL Jaxson Moi, 1 roster DL Payton Zdroik, 2 rosters TE Mark Redman, 2 rosters TE Rohan Jones, 3 rosters DT Bill Norton, 3 rosters So fascinating that of all the positions to sneak someone on the roster…tight end. Rams keep 3 QBs Matthew Stafford and Ty Simpson are guaranteed to make it, but Stetson Bennett still appeared on 84.5 percent of your rosters. This indicates a belief that Bennett will win the backup job—and Simpson won’t. We can call this “all part of the plan” and that does seem to be the case, but we can’t deny how unusual it is for a 13th overall pick, or really any first round pick, to be slotted as QB3 for an entire season. Even Trey Lance was the backup for the 49ers in 2021, when the 49ers were vying for a Super Bowl with (coincidentally) Jimmy Garoppolo. And what if Bennett is good? What if Stafford misses four games and Bennett replaces him and is good? Do the Rams let Bennett leave as a free agent in 2027, with no compensation, or do they re-sign him and continue to put distance between Simpson and the field? I don’t think Bennett will be good, but if he wins the backup job, then the implication is that he’s good enough. In any case, the fans think the Rams will keep 3 quarterbacks. And I always listen to the fans.

title: Fernando Mendoza versus Purdue, Part XII of Las Vegas Raiders’ Mendoza Mania
summary: We’re wrapping up the regular season in Silver and Black Pride’s Mendoza Mania series, diving into film breakdowns for each of Fernando Mendoza’s games during his last College Football season, and looking at Indiana’s dominant 56-3 win over in-state rival Purdue. However, this was the Las Vegas Raiders’ new quarterback’s worst performance of a passer […]
full_text: WEST LAFAYETTE, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 28: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Indiana Hoosiers scores a touchdown while being chased by Charles Correa #5 of the Purdue Boilermakers at Ross-Ade Stadium on November 28, 2025 in West Lafayette, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re wrapping up the regular season in Silver and Black Pride’s Mendoza Mania series , diving into film breakdowns for each of Fernando Mendoza’s games during his last College Football season, and looking at Indiana’s dominant 56-3 win over in-state rival Purdue. However, this was the Las Vegas Raiders’ new quarterback’s worst performance of a passer from last year, going eight for 15 (53.3% completions) with 117 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions . The latter is misleading, though. Pro Football Focus had him on the hook for three “ turnover-worthy plays ” at a 17.6 percent rate, his most TWPs and highest rate (by over 12 percent) on the year. Also, the 2026 NFL draft No. 1 pick didn’t account for any “big-time throws” and posted his lowest PFF passing grade (28.3) of the season by more than 20 points against the Boilermakers. So, fair warning, this breakdown is going to be more negative than positive, as it looked like the Heisman Trophy winner was pressing and forced a handful of throws. Purdue was Fernando Mendoza's worst game last season, forcing a handful of throws He likes the 1on1 matchup with Sarratt here, but Sarratt is never open, and he misses on the back-shoulder throw pic.twitter.com/mDlbfu8APZ — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 15, 2026 This was Mendoza’s first pass of the game and, in a way, set a precursor for how the rest of the night went for him. Purdue is playing man coverage and makes no secret about it by showing and staying in Cover 1 pre- and post-snap while both corners are lined up in press coverage. With Indiana in a three-by-one formation, that sets up Elijah Sarratt with a one-on-one matchup that Mendoza clearly likes and wants to take advantage of. However, the cornerback plays soft-shoe press coverage instead of going for the jam at the line of scrimmage and stays in Sarratt’s hip throughout the route, meaning the receiver is never open. Ideally, the quarterback comes off the one-on-one matchup and works the other side of the progression, where the outside receiver and tight end are open. Instead, Mendoza tries to throw a back-shoulder pass to Sarratt and misses too far inside, forcing the receiver to be the defender and prevent the interception. Predetermining and being inaccurate with the throw is a bad combination, and he’s lucky this wasn’t a turnover. Tries to hit Cooper on the drag route, but the CB undercuts it and the pass is too flat. Lucky this wasn't an INT pic.twitter.com/pMpbjj6ImY — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 15, 2026 While the receiver and route are different here, this play is almost a carbon copy of the previous one. The Boilermakers have the same play call, running Cover 1 with a six-man pressure, while the Hoosiers come out in a three-by-one formation again. Granted, it doesn’t look like this is a predetermined throw/decision by Mendoza, but more of him trying to force the ball into someone who isn’t open. The matchup to watch here is in the slot, where the nickelback does a great job of covering Omar Cooper Jr. on the drag route. The defender knows he has safety help over the top with the single-high coverage. So, once Cooper releases off the line and starts to work across the field, the nickel can undercut the route to get into the passing lane since the free safety is protecting him from being beaten deep. As a result, the receiver isn’t open. But Mendoza throws it anyway and doesn’t get enough air on the ball to place it between the second and third levels of the defense. Instead, the pass goes right to the defender and should have been intercepted if the receiver didn’t play great defense to force the drop. What makes this play more frustrating is that if Mendoza had gotten to his next read, he would have seen the cornerback who was covering Sarratt slip to create an opportunity for a big play. While the pass-rush was coming, he had plenty of time to move on in the progression. Missed read on this one, picture changes post-snap and he doesn't see Sarratt open for the 3rd down conversion pic.twitter.com/mZXeuKe2MZ — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 15, 2026 This next one is a missed read more than anything. Purdue mixes up their coverage by showing the Cover 1 look they ran in the first two clips with the free safety in the middle of the field pre-snap. However, post-snap, they rotate into Cover 3 with pattern-matching principles in the secondary, where the nickelback in the boundary (bottom of the screen) rotates into the middle deep third and the safety slides over to take the hook-to-curl area. Also, they’re protecting against a deep or intermediate throw by having the middle linebacker drop well past the sticks in the other hook-to-curl zone, on top of the safety staying about five yards beyond the marker. That becomes the most significant aspect of the coverage because it leaves Sarratt wide open for an easy first down on the drag route. However, Mendoza doesn’t recognize it and appears to be looking for a big play despite it being third and seven, meaning it’s more important for the offense to convert and stay on the field. Additionally, he could hit the running back for a potential first down, especially since the defender closest to the back is a line of scrimmage player who dropped in coverage. With no one other than the checkdowns open, the quarterback has to hold onto the ball and the pass-rush starts to hit home. He eventually finds Charlie Becker (No. 80), who is working across the field on the dig route, and tries to layer the ball over the aforementioned linebacker in the middle of the field, but the pass falls incomplete. In fairness, Becker does get alligator arms with Riley Nowakowski (No. 37) working toward the middle of the field. So, maybe this pass could have been completed with a more courageous effort from the receiver. But that doesn’t change the fact that an easy completion that would have gotten the job done was there for the taking. Bootleg, late to find Becker and then misses the throw pic.twitter.com/gwVThCmbuL — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) July 15, 2026 Something was off with the Heisman Trophy winner in this game. He wasn’t seeing the field as clearly as he did in previous weeks, with the rep above serving as another example. Once again, the Boilermakers are playing Cover 1. Meanwhile, Indiana draws up a bootleg, where Mendoza could hit the running back in the flat to keep the offense on schedule. But there is an opportunity for a bigger play, so it’s understandable that he turns that down, especially since the receiver at the top of the screen wins on the corner route. However, Mendoza doesn’t see it or make that throw, either. Then, Becker comes from the other side of the field and is open on the drag route. Mendoza eventually finds Becker, but not until after he pivots toward the line of scrimmage, causing him to be late and miss the throw on the run. Maybe he was trying to get those two underneath defenders to come downhill, but he didn’t need to do that, and it’s more important to be on time and accurate with the throw than play games with the defense. Overall, this was definitely an off-night from the No. 1 pick. He had plenty of examples of going through the proper reads, making good decisions and good throws on the run throughout the season. However, Mendoza did tend to have one to two forced or predetermined throws that were dangerous per game; it was just more frequent against Purdue. So, that’s something he’ll want to be conscious of in the NFL because one or two bad decisions from a quarterback can be the difference between winning and losing a game. On a positive note, Mendoza did have a couple of good runs vs Purdue. Nice job working off the blocks for a…

title: Raiders news: Fernando Mendoza signing rookie contract
summary: The wait is over. The Las Vegas Raiders have now secured its entire rookie draft class by signing No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. It was a long process since the Raiders drafted the Heisman Trophy winner from Indiana on April 23. There was media speculation that he remained unsigned because of details with secondary […]
full_text: HENDERSON, NEVADA - JUNE 03: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders stretches during an OTA offseason workout at the Las Vegas Raiders Headquarters/Intermountain Health Performance Center on June 03, 2026 in Henderson, Nevada. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The wait is over. The Las Vegas Raiders have now secured its entire rookie draft class by signing No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. It was a long process since the Raiders drafted the Heisman Trophy winner from Indiana on April 23. There was media speculation that he remained unsigned because of details with secondary contract language such as guarantee payout scheduling, offset language and voiding rules. NFL Media reported he signed a four-year, $57.27 million fully guaranteed contract. The team hold a fifth-year option that will be determined in the spring of 2029. Mendoza’s signing comes on the day the Raiders’ rookies and select veterans report to training camp. The first full-squad practice is Wednesday. With Mendoza signed, the focus turns to when he will play. Recently, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media raised some eyebrows about the plan for Mendoza this season. According to Rapoport, the team’s ideal plan for the No. 1 overall draft pick is to keep him on the shelf for his entire rookie season. Rapoport said the team would like to see veteran Kirk Cousins, who was signed this offseason and who will turn 38 next month, play for the entire season. The Raiders have yet to publicly say what their plan is other than saying they do, indeed, have a quarterback plan. Both Las Vegas general manager John Spytek and head coach Klint Kubiak have said they would like to see rookie quarterbacks, in general, sit and learn in an ideal world. But an exact timeline for Mendoza hasn’t been announced. So, Rapoport’s report is interesting to suggest that Raiders would rather not insert Mendoza in the lineup at all in 2026. Time will what will happen, but the plan can proceed with Mendoza now officially in the fold.

summary: While this summer’s version of Netflix is streaming and getting strong reviews as the series usually does, there is already speculation on who will be the featured NFL played of ‘Quarterback’ in 2027, in a review of the 2026 season. There is already speculation there would be a major Las Vegas Raiders flavor to the […]
full_text: THE 2026 ESPYS PRESENTED BY CAPITAL ONE - Hosted by Marcello Hernández, who will bring his signature humor to the stage as he joins a star-studded roster of athletes and celebrities honoring the greatest achievements in the world of sports. "The ESPYS" will air live on Wednesday, July 15, 2026, at 8 p.m. EDT/7 p.m. CDT on ABC, ESPN+ and be available to stream next day on Hulu. (Disney/Frank Micelotta) FERNANDO MENDOZA (Photo by Frank Micelotta/Disney via Getty Images) | Disney via Getty Images While this summer’s version of Netflix is streaming and getting strong reviews as the series usually does, there is already speculation on who will be the featured NFL played of ‘Quarterback’ in 2027, in a review of the 2026 season. title: 3 major questions that must be answered for Miami Dolphins in 2026
summary: After enjoying the successes of a historically dominant offense for the first two years of former head coach Mike McDaniel’s tenure with the Miami Dolphins, the team took major steps back during the final two years of the coach’s four-year stint with the club. As a result, he was relieved of his duties, and the […]
full_text: Quarterback Malik Willis speaks after signing to play with the Miami Dolphins at Baptist Health Training Complex on Thursday, March 12, 2026, in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Amy Beth Bennett/South Florida Sun Sentinel/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) After enjoying the successes of a historically dominant offense for the first two years of former head coach Mike McDaniel’s tenure with the Miami Dolphins, the team took major steps back during the final two years of the coach’s four-year stint with the club. As a result, he was relieved of his duties, and the organization decided to hit the reset button — signalling the beginning of another roster reset in South Florida. After hiring new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and new head coach Jeff Hafley, the Dolphins took a machete to their roster — releasing or trading numerous high priced veteran players in an effort to get cheaper and younger. We now find ourselves heading into a 2026 NFL season that sees many questions for the Miami Dolphins needing answers if they hope to expedite the rebuilding process they currently find themselves in. Let’s take a look at the top-three concerns facing the team ahead of training camp which begins next week. Is Jeff Hafley the right man for the job? After moving on from the Mike McDaniel era, the Dolphins enter 2026 with first-year head coach Jeff Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan. The roster has been heavily reshaped, and expectations are centered less on immediate wins and more on establishing a new culture, identity, and longterm foundation. Personalities around the league widely view Miami as one of the NFL’s biggest rebuilds entering training camp. One of the most important aspects of Hafley’s first year is creating accountability and consistency. That includes: Defining leadership in the locker room. Developing players rather than simply acquiring them. Building a team that can withstand injuries. Creating systems that don’t depend on one or two star players. Can Malik Willis prove he’s the quarterback of the future? With Tua Tagovailoa now a member of the Atlanta Falcons, the Dolphins look to the newly signed Malik Willis to lead the offense. His athleticism is unquestioned, but consistency as a passer will determine whether Miami commits to him beyond 2026 or enters the 2027 draft looking for their next franchise quarterback. Willis doesn’t need to throw for 5,000 yards to succeed. If the Dolphins tailor the offense to his strengths, they could look to emphasize the following things: Play-action passing. Designed quarterback runs. Rollouts and moving pockets. Deep shots off run action. Quick, defined reads that allow him to play fast. Miami’s goal would be to create an offense that stresses defenses with both Willis’s arm and his legs while limiting situations that expose his current weaknesses. How quickly can Miami’s rookies develop? One of the more pressing questions for the Dolphins in 2026 is how quickly their rookie class can become meaningful contributors . For a team in the early stages of a rebuild, rookie development isn’t just a bonus, it’s essential to accelerating the franchise’s timeline for being competitive. Unlike veteran heavy contenders that can afford to ease first-year players into limited roles, Miami needs several members of its 2026 draft class to make an immediate impact. Every snap they play this season is an investment in what the organization hopes will become its next core. The Dolphins won’t judge their rookies solely by box-score production. Coaches will be watching for: Improvement from September to December. Increased confidence and consistency. Better understanding of the playbook. Fewer mental mistakes. ___ While expectations for the 2026 Miami Dolphins are low in regards to how many wins they can etch into the record books, it is still an extremely important season for a franchise desperate to get back to the glory days of long, long ago. Answering the questions posed above will go a long way towards achieving that goal, which gives all of us Dolphins fans incentives to watch our guys in aqua and orange compete all season long.

title: Jonah Savaiinaea under pressure to perform in second year
summary: Early on Wednesday morning, Miami Dolphins guard Jonah Savaiinaea was named by ESPN as a “bluechip” player under the age of 25 despite the fact that he struggled mightily during his rookie season. In fact, Miami’s second-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft was rated as the worst guard in the entire National Football League […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - OCTOBER 30: Jonah Savaiinaea #72 of the Miami Dolphins looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Baltimore Ravens at Hard Rock Stadium on October 30, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Early on Wednesday morning, Miami Dolphins guard Jonah Savaiinaea was named by ESPN as a “bluechip” player under the age of 25 despite the fact that he struggled mightily during his rookie season. In fact, Miami’s second-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft was rated as the worst guard in the entire National Football League last year by Pro Football Focus (PFF) — earning a dismal 28.4 grade. Earlier this month, PFF released their list of the top-10 second-year players in the NFL under the most pressure to perform in 2026 — and Savaiinaea was on that list. Here’s what they had to say about the young player: “The Dolphins’ 2025 season was a disaster by almost all accounts, and that included Savaiinaea at guard. The second-round pick was a consistent starter but had a difficult time acclimating to the pros. Last year, Savaiinaea’s 28.4 overall PFF grade was the worst among any qualified guard by almost nine grading points. In fact, that mark carries historical perspective: It’s easily the lowest in a season by any guard to play 950 or more snaps in the 20 years of PFF data. Not only did Savaiinaea permit eight sacks and 45 pressures, but he also played to a poor 37.3 PFF run-blocking grade. After Miami drafted Kadyn Proctor in the first round this April, Savaiinaea is projected to slide to right guard, where he played 985 snaps at Arizona . Although it projects as a transition year in South Beach, the Dolphins will need Savaiinaea to look far more comfortable as they try to protect new quarterback Malik Willis and open lanes for De’Von Achane .” So, despite ESPN’s seemingly misplaced praise for Savaiinaea earlier in the day, it is clear that there’s really nowhere the guard can go but up in terms of his play moving forward. Well… either that, or to the bench and eventually the unemployment line, which no Dolphins fan wants to see happen.
