title: Which 49ers player will be the biggest standout during training camp?
summary: We are a few days away from the San Francisco 49ers’ entire team reporting to training camp. We’ll see how often Kyle Shanahan gives veterans like Trent Williams and Christian McCaffrey days off. We know players like Nick Bosa, George Kittle, and Mykel Williams are recovering from season-ending injuries. That opens the door for some […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JANUARY 05: Jacob Cowing #19 of the San Francisco 49ers prepares for a game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on January 05, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are a few days away from the San Francisco 49ers’ entire team reporting to training camp. We’ll see how often Kyle Shanahan gives veterans like Trent Williams and Christian McCaffrey days off. We know players like Nick Bosa, George Kittle, and Mykel Williams are recovering from season-ending injuries. That opens the door for some other players on the roster to make a name for themselves and catch the eyes of the coaching staff. That’s especially true for the new faces on the roster. And there are plenty of those who will look to take advantage of potential openings. Whether that’s Christian Kirk at wide receiver, Robert Jones or Brett Toth at guard, Nate Hobbs in the secondary, or one of the undrafted free agent rookies added on defense, we can expect somebody to stand out. Last season, that was Demarcus Robinson. He was unguardable during training camp. You would have thought he was Brandon Aiyuk the way he was being talked about last August. Unfortunately, that summer success never came to fruition during the season. So, who will be the summer standout this year? Which 49ers player will be the biggest standout during training camp? My answer: Jacob Cowing In these practice settings, it tends to be the wide receiver, much like Robinson a year ago. I’ll go with the player who I think can carry over a strong training camp into the regular season. There will be veteran days off for Mike Evans during training camp and the preseason. That’ll open the door for other wideouts. So I’m going with Jacob Cowing, a guy who adds a speed dimension that the 49ers did not have a season ago. Ricky Pearsall tested extraordinarily well, but, to the eye test, Cowing plays faster than Pearsall. Cowing will be lined up in the slot and off the ball in advantageous matchups against a secondary that does not run well, at least compared to Cowing. Usage matters. Cowing will likely run deep crossing routes or routes with vertical stems. He may have a screen or two mixed in with an underneath route, but he’s a vertical threat. That’ll lead to big plays, splash plays, and “oohs and ahhs” from the crowd. That’ll show in preseason games, as will Cowing’s ability as a returner. He should get enough opportunities returning punts and kicks. It’s another area where Cowing can show off his speed and prove to the coaching staff that he can make an impact.

title: 49ers viewed among the worst teams in the NFL for talent under 25
summary: Each year, as we head into the regular season, teams are ranked by the talent they have on the current roster under the age of 25. Last year, the Niners ranked 30th in this exercise. The San Francisco 49ers improved this year, but that’s because there was really only one direction to go. Here is […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 04: San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Mykel Williams (98) looks on during San Francisco 49ers Training Camp on August 4, 2025 at the SAP Performance Facility in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Each year, as we head into the regular season, teams are ranked by the talent they have on the current roster under the age of 25. Last year, the Niners ranked 30th in this exercise . The San Francisco 49ers improved this year , but that’s because there was really only one direction to go. Here is a look at the methodology: Number of starts made by players under 25 years old Number of snaps played by players under 25 years old Quality of play by players under 25 years old, age-adjusted to capture the fact that a 21-year-old player of X ability will likely improve more than a 23-year-old player of X ability — and with extra consideration given to Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections Value and length of player contracts Relative importance of positions, with quarterbacks being more important and running backs, off-ball linebackers and specialists being less important than other positions Draft value added in the 2026 draft, particularly in the first three rounds Expected key starters and reserves under 25 years old for teams in 2026 Significant injuries or suspensions that will affect the 2026 availability of players under 25 years old The 49ers had one blue chip player: Last year’s rank: 30 Blue chips: Edge Mykel Williams Notable graduated players: CB Renardo Green , WR Ricky Pearsall Injuries led to playing time for a lot of the youth in San Francisco last season, as six different players currently under 25 started at least six games. We’ll begin on defense, with safeties Malik Mustapha and Marques Sigle . They are both 24 years old. Nickelback Upton Stout is also 24, as is defensive tackle Alfred Collins . Last year’s first-round pick, edge rusher Mykel Williams , turned 22 in June. On offense, 23-year-old Connor Colby and 24-year-old Carver Willis will battle for the starting left guard position in training camp. Second-round rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling is 23. Backup running backs Kaelon Black and Jordan James are 24 and 22, respectively. This year’s third-round pick, edge rusher Romello Height , is already 25 and does not qualify for our list. The issue for the Niners is that neither of their young talent has played long enough to show promise. Had Mustapha stayed healthy and continued the play from his rookie year, this conversation would be different. It also doesn’t help that the Niners have drafted on the older side — another reason to be intrigued by Jordan James. So if Romello Height rushes the passer or affects the pass rush like the team drafted him to, it wouldn’t reflect in rankings like this because of his age. That leaves Mykel Williams and De’Zhaun Stribling as the players with multiple years to show that they can be cornerstone players for the future. Both are walking into situations where they should have tremendous opportunities to do so. Williams gets to play alongside Nick Bosa and Osa Odighizuwa. Plus, there’s the thought that the 49ers would have the lead, thus more pass-rushing opportunities from the inside for Williams. As for Stribling, he gets to learn from Mike Evans and play on an offense that includes Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, and Ricky Pearsall, with Kyle Shanahan calling the plays. You’d be hard-pressed to find a better scenario for a rookie.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers News: All I want for my birthday is for the Niners to sign a lineman
summary: I don’t care which side of the ball. I don’t care if it’s interior or exterior. I don’t care if it’s a free agent or via trade. I don’t care if they’re better at pass rush, pass pro, run blocking, or run defense. We just need more DUDES!  Rant over. On to the links… Schefter […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: Enrique Cruz Jr. #69 and Carver Willis #74 of the San Francisco 49ers run a drill during a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I don’t care which side of the ball. I don’t care if it’s interior or exterior. I don’t care if it’s a free agent or via trade. I don’t care if they’re better at pass rush, pass pro, run blocking, or run defense. We just need more DUDES! Rant over. On to the links… Schefter on 49ers TE George Kittle’s Week 1 return: ‘I don’t think it’s a given’ “But the 49ers may be very careful, and let’s see if he makes it back. I don’t think it’s a given, just yet.” 49ers insider believes Deebo Samuel wanted a return to San Francisco “I do think Deebo had an interest in returning to the 49ers and was maybe even a little miffed that the 49ers so quickly signed Mike Evans as a free agent.” 49ers roster preview: Why Carver Willis needs a redshirt year “There are plenty of traits to like about Willis. His hand placement and punch timing are above average, even if his hands can occasionally get a little wide — likely Willis overcompensating. He does a great job on combo blocks, can easily redirect, and moves more like a second-rounder than a fourth-rounder. Best of all, Willis competes through the whistle and will look to finish whoever he is blocking. He stays engaged, which is a valuable trait to have. Some things happen to Willis that he cannot control. I saw one of the Ohio State players forklift him off the ground. Too often, his lack of length was problematic. And while changing directions isn’t an issue, the shorter arms allow defenders to close space on him, knowing that Willis won’t affect them….. When I watched him, Willis looked like a player who needed more sand in his pants to hold up in pass protection. Now, the 49ers could do different things upfront to hide him or minimize the number of 1-on-1s Willis gets. He was at his best when he was uncovered. When he could help somebody else out, or had help on combination blocks. That’s a center. Foerster is probably correct in viewing Willis as a starter, but that’s likely in 2027 to replace Brendel and become the 49ers’ center of the future. As a rookie, Willis should take advantage of a professional strength & conditioning program, as well as all of the nutrition that comes with being a pro. He’ll learn the ins and outs of playing a new position while going against NFL-quality linemen on the scout team.” One thought on Brock Purdy, Ricky Pearsall and every player on the 49ers offense (paywall) “Connor Colby: We’ll pencil in Colby as the team’s top left guard prospect, but we have to do it very lightly since several others are competing for that spot. Still, Colby logged 452 snaps at the position as a rookie last year and was in the top slot throughout spring drills. Robert Jones: The most likely candidate to nudge Colby from the starting spot? It’s probably Jones, who started 17 games in a similar Dolphins offense in 2024 and has logged more than 2,000 offensive snaps in his career. Jones is coming off a neck injury that cost him the entire 2025 season.” We gave 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch offseason advice. How well did they follow it? (Paywall) “The 49ers did more than study their substation issue. They also spent $9 million to upgrade their training facilities and hired three additional physical therapists. That was a response to dissatisfaction players had expressed in the most recent NFLPA survey in which they grade their team in 11 categories.”

title: Titans training camp preview: Cornerbacks and Safeties
summary: The Tennessee Titans will officially begin training camp on July 28th when the veterans report to Vanderbilt Health Football Camp in Nashville. We’re concluding our positional preview with the secondary, cornerbacks and safeties. The Titans have 17 defensive backs on the offseason roster. General manager Mike Borgonzi made various acquisitions across these positions. In camp (17): Alontae […]
full_text: Jun 16, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans cornerback Alontae Taylor (24) talks with the media post practice during day 1 of mini-camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans will officially begin training camp on July 28th when the veterans report to Vanderbilt Health Football Camp in Nashville. We’re concluding our positional preview with the secondary, cornerbacks and safeties. The Titans have 17 defensive backs on the offseason roster. General manager Mike Borgonzi made various acquisitions across these positions. In camp (1 7): Alontae Taylor, Cor’Dale Flott, Amani Hooker, Kevin Winston Jr., Marcus Harris, Tony Adams, Joshua Williams, Jerrick Reed II, Jalen McMurray, Latrell McCutchin, Jeadyn Lukus, Kendell Brooks, Sanoussi Kane, Erick Hallett II, Bishop Fitzgerald, Keydrain Calligan, Micah Robinson. Biggest storyline: The Titans totally revamped the cornerback room, signing Alontae Taylor and Cor’Dale Flott to very lucrative contracts in free agency. They’ll be tasked with being Robert Saleh’s starting boundary corners. This position needed a makeover after trading Jarvis Brownlee and Roger McCreary, and cutting L’Jarius Sneed. Expectations are high for Taylor and Flott. Most to prove: Both Kevin Winston Jr. and Marcus Harris are sophomores entering the year in starting roles. The Titans cut Xavier Woods during the offseason to make room for Winston in the starting lineup opposite Amani Hooker. Harris doesn’t appear to have any competition for the nickel role either. Breakout star: Winston Jr. is probably the correct choice. The former Penn State standout flashed an exciting skill set when he was healthy as a rookie. Winston is entering camp fully available and should make a massive impact next to Hooker in the lineup. He possesses every trait to be a breakout defender. Training camp competition: The Titans will only be having competition for back-end roles in the secondary. Is Joshua Williams the CB4 behind the three starters? That’s the expectation, given his experience. The fifth and presumably final cornerback spot will be decided by Micah Robinson, Keydrain Calligan, and three undrafted cornerbacks.

title: Washington Commanders 92-man 2026 pre-training camp roster/depth chart
summary: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this […]
full_text: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this IPP exemption, as they have again this season, so Washington’s offseason roster limit is once again 91 players. Washington’s 91st player via the IPP is currently edge rusher TJ Maguranyanga , who spent the 2025 season with the Commanders as well. An unanswered question As the Commanders head into training camp, with rookies reporting to camp Friday (July 24) and veterans reporting on Tuesday, there is at least one outstanding roster question to be resolved. It was recently and widely reported by sports media that Washington had signed veteran cornerback Rasul Douglas . This signing was also reported by the team , but the Commanders website hasn’t added the cornerback’s name to the roster page . Without Douglas’ name on the roster, Washington’s team site lists 91 players. Our Lads does have Douglas included on their depth chart, but it lists 92 players. The signing of Douglas appears on the official NFL transactions list on July 6, but there is no corresponding roster move to make space for him on the roster. Right now, without more information, it looks like the Commanders have 92 players, which is one player too many. It appears as if another transaction will need to happen (or be announced) soon to keep the Commanders in compliance with the 91-man training camp roster limit. That transaction could be the release of a player, but it could also result from a player being placed on the PUP (Physically Unable to Perform) list or other reserve list that removes him, usually temporarily, from being counted against the roster limit. I expect that roster transaction to be announced by Tuesday. In the meantime, since I don’t know what the team will do to create the roster opening, I’m presenting a 92-man depth chart here. So, before this article was even published, it was out of date — someone on the chart below will not be a full participant in next week’s training camp, and may not be on the roster this time next week. Changes since the last iteration of the depth chart Since the last time I published a depth chart article , there have been just a few changes: WR Ja’Corey Brooks was cut TE Anthony Firsker was signed Also, as mentioned above, CB Rasul Douglas has reportedly agreed to terms with the team, but no corresponding roster move to open a roster spot for him has been announced, nor does the NFL transaction wire list any such transaction. As a result, we should expect at least one more roster transaction in the coming days. Not your typical depth chart The chart below is only a depth chart insofar as it assigns players to positions and stacks them in an order. The primary purpose of the chart is to keep track of the 92 guys that currently comprise the training camp roster, not to predict gameday alignments. You will note, for example, that I have 12 offensive positions and 13 defensive positions on the chart, despite the fact that a team can only field 11 players at one time. You will also note that each player’s name appears only once regardless of the fact that he may play in multiple alignments or positions ( e.g., an interior offensive lineman who can play center and both guard spots will appear at only one of those positions, not all of them ). Again, this is by design since the goal is to provide handy visual reference of the 92 individual players while also offering an overall snapshot of team strength and depth. The bias, though, is to provide a visual list of the full roster, not so much to create a game-ready depth chart. Finally, you will also note that, where players are capable of playing more than one position (and likely to do so on game days), my decision on where to align them may be very different from your idea of where they belong. Here are comments on a couple of players who may seem misaligned to you: Antonio Williams I don’t think any informed fan will argue against the idea that this year’s third-round draft pick will play both inside (slot) and outside on offense. Because he played primarily in the slot in his final year at Clemson in 2025 , many people insist that he will be Washington’s primary slot receiver in 2026. I have repeatedly pointed to Adam Peters’ comments all offseason about Williams’ play outside in 2024 and his abilities as a wideout as one reason for my belief that the Clemson product is seen by the Commanders front office and coaching staff as a solution to the seeming need for a receiver to play opposite McLaurin. In addition, the team already has Luke McCaffrey and Jaylin Lane — a pair of recently drafted players with inside/outside skills — available for the slot. Further, we have heard multiple indications that the Commanders will play more 12 and 13 personnel this season, which would take one WR off the field. When that happens, I expect McLaurin and Williams to be the first choice to remain on the field in multiple tight end sets, most likely boosting the number of snaps Williams lines up on the outside. In my mind, all of this adds up to Williams aligning wide more than in the slot — which, by the way, would be consistent with the Lions’ use of Amon-Ra St. Brown, who is a frequent comp for Washington’s plans for AW: For all these reasons, I have listed Williams on the chart as the primary receiver opposite McLaurin. My chart would change in an instant if, for example, the team signed Stefon Diggs on Monday. Mike Sainristil I don’t think all the questions about the cornerback room are settled. I don’t think we know if Trey Amos is fully healthy. I don’t think we know whether Rasul Douglas was signed in the expectation of him starting or simply providing depth. I don’t think we know whether Mike Sainristil will end up as a starter or a backup, or whether he will align primarily as a wide corner or slot defender. In a manner similar to the increased use of tight ends on offense, the expected increase in three-safety looks on defense this season could lead to more alignments with only two 2 cornerbacks on the field instead of traditional nickel schemes. I have chosen, in the chart below, to assume that Amos will be healthy, that Douglas will be the primary CB on the opposite side, and that Sainristil will be the primary backup at both slot and out wide. I have listed him behind Amik Robertson on the chart. Of course, training camp and preseason could totally rewrite my ideas about how the secondary will be deployed. Consider these thoughts, published by A to Z Sports earlier this week: There are rumblings that the Commanders want to move Quan Martin into the primary nickel role, and honestly, that doesn’t make much sense to me. The majority of the safeties on the roster lack range, and Amik Robinson is a perfectly capable inside player. If Martin does slide to nickel, that leaves two cornerbacks under 5-foot-10 starting on the outside in both [Robertson] and Sainristill. And while both guys have shown they can play bigger than their body size, you don’t want your starting outside corners to both be under 5-foot-11. The Commanders could easily make a big mistake here and set themselves up in a bad spot by not only depriving themselves of their most capable centerfielder, but exposing the perimeter, as well. I have not included cap hits below $1.5m. The Commanders currently have 45 defensive players, 43 offensive players and 4 special teams players. Please note that assigned positions are my own personal opinions; they do not necessarily…

title: Washington Commanders Camp Battles: Treylon Burks vs. Antonio Williams
summary: Editor’s note: We’ll be running down some key roster battles in the the leadup to Washington Commanders training camp later this month. John Portis has taken the lead on this series that will look at rookies, veterans, and free agents who are fighting for playing time in July. The Washington Commanders have Terry McLaurin locked […]
full_text: Editor’s note: We’ll be running down some key roster battles in the the leadup to Washington Commanders training camp later this month. John Portis has taken the lead on this series that will look at rookies, veterans, and free agents who are fighting for playing time in July. The Washington Commanders have Terry McLaurin locked in as their No. 1 wide receiver for the 2026 season. He is healthy, ready to report to camp and in great shape. New offensive coordinator David Blough is on record saying he wants to get the Commanders’ wide receiver 10 targets a game. Blough is also expected to follow the growing trend of heavy 12 personnel usage, so with McLaurin locked in on the field, there will be just one other wide receiver on the field in many formations. Using Ben Johnson’s offense as a model, this player would need to bring a full route tree, versatility, run-blocking, and yards-after-catch ability. There are no less than four receivers in camp vying for the starting role opposite of Washington’s best wide receiver. Today, we focus on two specifically: one a veteran, the other a rookie. Treylon Burks was selected with the 18th overall pick of the 2022 NFL Draft by the Tennessee Titans. Drafted out of Arkansas, where he put up 1,104 yards and 11 touchdowns as a junior and was known for his YAC ability. His career in Tennessee was marred by injuries, and Burks was released by the Titans in Oct. 2025 with a total of 53 receptions for 699 yards and one touchdown in 27 games. Listed at 6-foot-2 and 225 pounds, Burks brings size and contested-catch ability to the Commanders. While not known as a refined route runner, Treylon has the versatility to play on the outside while also profiling as a big slot receiver. Posting an official 4.55 40-yard dash, Burks is not a speed threat, but after being signed to the Commanders practice squad and eventually the active roster, he was able to make an impact with last year’s team. Appearing in 10 games with three starts, Burks recorded 10 receptions for 130 yards with one touchdown. He had zero drops and a 100% catch rate in contested situations, including the NFL’s best catch of 2026 . The team liked what they saw from Burks and slowly increased his snap count over the season. Then they inked him to an extension just days before the start of free agency. Burks considers himself a fit for the Commanders new offense, citing Blough’s promotion to offensive coordinator as one of the reasons he decided to stay with Washington. At 5’11 1/2″ and 187 pounds, third-round NFL draft pick Antonio Williams is the antithesis of Burks in some ways. He is a polished and refined route runner that easily creates separation. Williams is not an imposing player like Burks, and while he can win in some contested catch situations, he is not physically dominant like the former Titan. Williams is not going to overpower defenders with his run-blocking, but has a good understanding of how to seal and wall off defenders in a zone scheme. A natural fit for the slot, there is debate among many about his ability to play on the outside. General manager Adam Peters has made it clear he believes Williams has the necessary versatility. In college, Williams created yards after the catch and has excellent vision with the ball in his hands. Burks was given multiple reps early in OTAs alongside McLaurin and responded by making a pair of tough catches along the sidelines and standing out in the early sessions. Williams also started to stake his own claim for the job, and Dan Quinn was quick to praise the rookie wide receiver. In fact, there has been early discussion of Williams as a potential offensive rookie of the year candidate. Commanders offensive assistant coach Wes Welker was quick to remind the media there is still a long way to go for the rookie, but Williams has looked the part early. Will he be able to win the starting role in camp, or will Burks’ pedigree, experience, and prototypical size be too much for the rookie to overcome? He possesses all the traits & talent to be a good WR, unfortunately has had bad luck with injuries. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/AMr6CNdjpm — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) June 12, 2026 Vs. Antonio Williams is my WR5 due to his coordinated, nuanced movement and ability to threaten the defense at all 3 levels Somewhere between Khalil Shakir and Tyler Lockett pic.twitter.com/AUNzycLb0N — NFL Draft Files (@NFL_DF) March 17, 2026

title: Commanders News: McCaffrey & Croskey-Merritt still have things to prove
summary: The Daily Slop – 23 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 02: Luke McCaffrey #11 of the Washington Commanders warms up before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Northwest Stadium on November 02, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 23 July 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room Where does WR Luke McCaffrey stand entering critical year 3? They say it takes three years for wide receivers to develop into reliable targets in the NFL. That trend has changed somewhat in recent years due to a number of very strong and deep wide receiver draft classes, but McCaffrey was considered a very raw prospect coming out. He entered college playing quarterback and switched positions, so he was very new to the position when the Commanders drafted him. That has caused him to take a little longer to develop, which makes this almost a make or break year for him. So where exactly does McCaffrey stand going into this important third year? With the current state of the receiver room, there should be opportunities for everyone to claim their spot in training camp. McLaurin is a lock as the top receiving option, but after him it’s a bit of a free for all. I don’t expect McCaffrey to establish himself as the second receiver or anything crazy like that, but I do think he can offer plenty as a fourth or fifth receiver on the depth chart and if everything goes well, could develop into the third receiver. Looking back at last season, the stats aren’t amazing. McCaffrey only played in nine games before breaking his collarbone and missing the rest of the year. As a result, he only had 11 catches, but he did pick up 203 yards and three touchdowns. 11 catches isn’t a huge sample size to go off, but when you watch McCaffrey you can see signs of development from him. The obvious place to start with McCaffrey last year was his 50-yard catch against the Chargers. It was his longest catch of the season and indeed his career to date, which showcased not only his speed to threaten down the field, but also his ball skills. WR Luke McCaffrey is entering a critical 3rd year with the Commanders. Given the state of the WR room, there will be opportunities for him to step up. So where does he stand after 2 years in Washington? I took a closer look: https://t.co/lueqaKmusP pic.twitter.com/Vf9l4YcHOZ — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) July 23, 2026 Heavy.com Commanders warned about trusting Jacory Croskey-Merritt Croskey-Merritt still looks like RB1, but the team has been warned about the risk of putting too much faith in the 25-year-old, as well as the dangers of not letting him develop crucial aspects of his game. The two-edged sword of how much to get Croskey-Merritt involved in this season’s running game was discussed by Danny Rouhier and Grant Paulsen on 106.7 The Fan’s “Grant & Danny Show.” Rouhier explained why the Commanders still have some doubts about JCM carrying the load as an every-down back: “I like him. It seems like they don’t as much. And here’s my evidence for that. It basically took Chris Rodriguez getting food poisoning or like a last-minute injury for them to finally give him double-digit carries. (In) nine of his 17 games, he averaged less than four yards a pop.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN 2026 Washington Commanders training camp preview Linebacker : Washington will use a 3-4 base look this season and signed/drafted five players for those roles — to pair with several holdovers. The Commanders will rotate players in, but there will be a question as to who will start, particularly on the inside. They have Luvu, free agent signee Leo Chenal and Sonny Styles. One won’t play as often — but do they use either Chenal or Styles in a nickel role at times to get all three on the field? And how will the outside rushers rotate? They have Dorance Armstrong, coming off a torn ACL, and free agent signees Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson as well as fifth-round pick Joshua Josephs. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Wire Will Commanders’ defensive overhaul be effective in 2026? Suffice it to say that between the departures and additions, the Commanders’ defense looks very different in 2026 than it did in 2025. But will what Peters did actually pan out this season? Under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, one of the biggest storylines is whether this defense can get all of its new faces on the same page, something that NFL.com’s Grant Gordon wrote about earlier this week. When you fall from being everyone’s NFC Championship Game darling to a 5-12 struggle bus, you can run out of fingers to point. The Commanders put a massive UNDER CONSTRUCTION sign in front of a defense that finished dead last in yards allowed. They used the No. 7 overall pick on Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles, an athletic marvel who will draw plenty of hype as a preseason Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate. General manager Adam Peters opened the check book before turning in the card to get Styles, too. Washington broke the bank to sign pass rusher Odafe Oweh, while adding plenty more veteran starters elsewhere: nickel Amik Robertson, safety Nick Cross, pass rusher K’Lavon Chaisson, linebacker Leo Chenal and defensive tackle Tim Settle. The Commanders added veteran depth, as well. Binging on free agents isn’t always a winning formula, of course. How quickly new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones and Washington’s cast of fresh faces get on the same page will be crucial in camp. The biggest problem the Commanders will have here is the number of new faces on the roster. It’s one thing if you bring in a handful of new players to join an otherwise stable unit, but it’s another beast altogether when you add a dozen or more new faces. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com Commanders 2026 opponent breakdown | Jaguars What will the offense look like without Etienne? It was widely expected for the Jaguars to not retain Etienne this past offseason, but there’s no doubt that he has been a key piece of their offense over the last four seasons with three 1,000-yard seasons. He had arguably his best campaign in 2025 with 1,107 yards and 13 total touchdowns. Now Etienne is with the New Orleans Saints, and the Jaguars have to find a way to replace him. For now, it seems like it’ll be a committee approach. They signed Rodriguez from Washington and seem eager to give him a shot at being their lead back after a solid season out of the former sixth-round pick. There’s also Bhayshul Tuten, who had limited opportunities in his rookie year but also had seven total touchdowns on 93 total touches. LeQuint Allen Jr., a seventh-round pick last season, was more of a special teams contributor, and Ameer Abdullah is an established veteran with 11 years of experience. Will one of these players emerge as a go-to option? Perhaps, but the Jaguars don’t seem to be in a hurry to figure that out. They like all their options, and each player will get their opportunities. How does the defense replace Devin Lloyd’s production on defense? Similar to Etienne, Lloyd was a key cog for the Jaguars’ success last season and has been an important fixture on their defense as a 2022 first-round pick. He didn’t hit 100 tackles like he did in the previous three seasons, but he made up for that with improvements in coverage and grabbed five interceptions, which helped him earn a Pro Bowl and Second Team All-Pro selection. However, also like Etienne, Lloyd left the team in free agency and signed with the Carolina Panthers. There are currently just six linebackers on the roster, most of which are young players with limited years of experience. title: Tyler’s Take – My two breakout players (offense and defense) for the 2026 Commanders
summary: The NFL draft is the lifeblood of your football team. Selecting and developing young talent is the number one job of an NFL general manager.  Adam Peters has been criticized a bit over his first two years in Washington for some of his higher draft picks. Some of those guys were expected to have a […]
full_text: The NFL draft is the lifeblood of your football team. Selecting and developing young talent is the number one job of an NFL general manager. Adam Peters has been criticized a bit over his first two years in Washington for some of his higher draft picks. Some of those guys were expected to have a MUCH bigger impact on the team than they have had to date. Conversely, some players who were picked a bit later shined early on. While we can make our voices heard in displeasure about some of Peter’s top 100 picks not preforming, we must be just as complementary of some guys who may have been overlooked in the draft, but came to Washington and did well. And, yes, I’m taking about BILL! Fans want to see players perform well. Some players take more time than others to develop, but the key to success is whether said player eventually gets to that “expected” level. With that said, below are my offensive and defensive breakout candidates for the upcoming season. Offense: TE Ben Sinnott Every time tight end Ben Sinnott touches the ball, good things seem to happen. The issue was that former offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury didn’t often get him the ball, instead relying on the savvy veteran Zach Ertz to help move the chains from the tight end position. Ben Sinnott with a huge 36yd gain! pic.twitter.com/ZlfXJAzuqz — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) December 14, 2025 This new David Blough offense seems tailor-made for a player like Sinnott. He can be moved around the formation, deployed as a blocker and pass catcher, and use his unique open-field abilities after the catch to move the offense up and down the field. He’s best with the ball in his hands with some space in front of him. This new system should scheme him to do just that. I view tight end Chig Okonkwo as a JUMBO wide receiver, so John Bates could be the true (more traditional) tight end of this offense. That leaves plenty of opportunity for Sinnott. Breakout Barometer: 40 receptions, 450 yards, 5 touchdowns Defense: DL Johnny Newtown Make no mistake about it — Johnny Newton was an absolute FORCE in Illinois’ one-gapping, attacking front in college. Because of that disruptive ability, he was selected early, in round two of the 2024 NFL draft. He was dealing with a lingering foot issue from college as a rookie and never quite got going. Newton was healthy entering Year 2, but a rash of injuries along the defensive front and a scheme that didn’t fit his talents thwarted his sophomore campaign. There were some quality flashes, but the consistency was missing. Year 3 could potentially paint an entirely different picture. The new up-field, attacking scheme that defensive coordinator Daronte Jones is expected to use should be much better for his skillset. Also, not having to two-gap in an EAGLE front should be to his liking. Quickness off the snap, plus an ability to get into the backfield and cause havoc are Newton’s best attributes. Putting him in a 3-technique and letting him use that quick-twitch ability against slower, more unathletic guards will be to his benefit. Breakout Barometer: 45 tackles, 9 TFL, 7 sacks, 1 FF Breakout Bonus: Mike Sainristil If you know me, you’ll know there can never be enough rainbows and unicorns. With that, I give you my bonus breakout player. As many of you already know, I’m a BIG Mike Sainristil fan. I thought he showed really well as a rookie, despite bouncing between the slot and boundary. Mike Sainristil with the nice play downfield here! pic.twitter.com/eCVSjsI3p0 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 10, 2024 Last year was a big step back, but how much of that was the system and lack of continuity around him? Sainristil has shown a propensity for taking the ball away during his first two seasons. In this new defensive scheme, where he’ll be able to play a lot more with his eyes on the quarterback, I expect him to continue to be the guy creating turnovers. Mike Sainristil with the MASSIVE INT right before the half!!! Huge play! pic.twitter.com/xGRKp94ht8 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) January 19, 2025 We’ve all seen that, despite his lack of size, Mikey is not afraid to come up and hit guys. I believe we see a nice blend of coverage and run support from the third-year corner, and we can watch Uncle Nick (Saban)’s praise about him being one of the best pound-for-pound players in the 2024 draft class come to reality in the league. I know one thing – Mike Sainristil is NOT afraid to tackle… pic.twitter.com/Kl6m3mvnnY — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 27, 2024 Breakout Barometer: 65 tackles, 1 FF, 1 sack, 5 INT, 15 PD *Sainristil had back-to-back seasons of 93 and 85 combined tackles respectively. However, you don’t want to see your cornerback making that many tackles, as that usually means your front seven is NOT doing their job. So, while I have Sainristil with less combined tackles, I just think that means Washington’s defensive line and linebackers are doing their jobs better. full_text: LANDOVER, MD - SEPTEMBER 11: Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin (17) catches a 49 yard touchdown pass during the NFL game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Washington Football Team on September 11, 2022 at Fed Ex Field in Landover, MD. (Photo by Mark Goldman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s 5 o’clock somewhere… The 5 O’Clock Club The 5 o’clock club is published from time to time during the season, and aims to provide a forum for reader-driven discussion at a time of day when there isn’t much NFL news being published. Feel free to introduce topics that interest you in the comments below. CLICK HERE to see the full 5 o’clock club archive 2026 opponent preview series: Wk 1 Eagles | Wk 2 Cowboys | Wk 3 Seahawks | Wk 4 Colts | Wk 5 Giants | Wk 6 49ers | Wk 9 Rams | Wk 11 Bengals | Wk 12 Cardinals | Wk 13 Titans | Wk 14 Texans | Wk 15 Falcons – Wk 16 Vikings Previewing Washington’s 14 opponents of the ‘26 season — one at a time In 2026, the Commanders will, like every other team in the NFL, play 17 games against 14 opponents. With the amount of roster change that NFL teams undergo annually along with the unusually large number of head coach and coordinator changes in 2026, it seems useful to spend some time to review each of Washington’s regular season opponents. JAGUARS The Week 17 road game in Jacksonville features the matchup of two relatively young NFL QBs, Trevor Lawrence and Jayden Daniels, each trying to enhance the trajectory of his career. Lawrence enters the late-season contest following a season in which he became an MVP finalist under coordinator Liam Coen. For the Commanders, Daniels will be hoping to be finishing a healthy season reminiscent of his rookie year, and leading a re-tooled and re-energized Washington offense under David Blough. This game could serve as a late-season benchmark for both quarterbacks as their teams will hopefully be fighting for playoff positioning. Week 17 Preview: Washington Commanders at Jacksonville Jaguars Date: Date & Time TBD Location: EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida The official NFL Commanders 2026 Season Preview ends with this projection of what the Commanders season could look like if Jayden Daniels stays healthy and returns to his 2024 ROTY form: While this projected start to the season (0-3; 2-4; 3-5) would lead to a lot of people having to be talked down from a lot of ledges in the months of September and October, given the team’s two new coordinators and the distribution of expected tougher/easier opponents, this 12-win projection doesn’t look very dissimilar to my own recent 10-win projection; in fact, I had the same W/L projections for all the games except for the Texans and this one against the Jaguars. My point here, if I have one, is that the Week 17 game in Jacksonville, if the season is unfolding along the lines of an optimistic preseason projection, could take place amidst a lot of winning and optimism for a Commanders team that could be living by the mantra that “it ain’t how you start; it’s how you finish” in this first weekend of NFL football in the 2027 calendar year ( For what it’s worth, I looked at the Jaguars’ season preview video from the NFL, and their best case outcome has them winning 13 games and winning this Week 17 game as well ). The Jaguars won 13 games last year en route to the AFC South championship, and I imagine that Jacksonville fans will be expecting a similarly strong 2026 season. The Jags season over/under win total is 9.5, so oddsmakers seem to be expecting a good season from Liam Coen’s team. One familiar face that the Commanders will know when they fly south for this winter battle is that of RB Chris Rodriguez, former 2023 6th-round draft pick of the Commanders. He signed with the Jaguars as a restricted free agent from the Commanders this offseason, and Rodriguez should be a focal point of Jacksonville’s short-yardage committee alongside second-year back Bhayshul Tuten. Jayden Daniels will see at least one friendly face from his college days. His former teammate at LSU, Brian Thomas Jr, is a star wide receiver for the Jaguars — or, at least, like JD5, Thomas looked like a star when he had 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 TDs as a rookie in 2024 before falling back to earth quite a bit in ‘25 (707 yards, 2 TDs). He was Jayden Daniels’ primary deep threat during their record-breaking 2023 college football season at LSU, where Thomas led the nation in touchdown receptions and helped propel Daniels to his Heisman Trophy win. Both players entered the NFL together as first-round picks in the 2024 NFL Draft, and there has been a lot of fan & media buzz in recent months about the concept of the Commanders front office trading for Thomas to set up an NFL reunion between quarterback and receiver. Of course, Daniels has another former college teammate on the roster with him at the moment — Rachaad White, signed by Washington in free agency back in March, and Daniels formed a productive offensive backfield together at Arizona State during the 2020 and 2021 college seasons before Daniels transferred to LSU. Under head coach Liam Coen in 2025, Jacksonville transformed into an offensive powerhouse, highlighted by an explosive post-bye-week stretch. If they mirror last year’s late-season surge in 2026, this game will likely be critical for securing the AFC South or a top seed. Washington, for its part, enters the ‘26 season determined to erase memories of a tough 2025 season and find its footing under new coordinators on offense & defense. Commanders fans are hoping that fresh leadership and a rejuvenated and healthy roster will see the team re-acquire the playoff form it demonstrated in 2024. This Week 17 battle represents either a statement game to clinch an NFC playoff seed or — in the pessimistic timeline — a spoiler opportunity against an AFC heavyweight. The All-Time Series Numbers The historical discrepancy between these two franchises is shockingly one-sided. Washington completely dominates the all-time series 7-1 , with Jacksonville’s solitary win against the franchise occurring all the way back in 2002. The only NFL team that has played Washington fewer times than the Jaguars is the Texans — the Commanders’ Week 14 opponent. No team has been more thoroughly dominated by Washington than the Jaguars based on the all-time series W-L record. Still, when the games are looked at individually, things have been much more even between the two teams than the series record would indicate; in the 5 straight Washington victories since 2006, 4 of them have been decided by a margin of 6 points or less, and two of them went into overtime. In other words, despite the dominance in series wins, the past two decades has been witness to a hard-fought bunch of games between these two teams. Undoubtedly, Jacksonville will be looking to partially balance the scales with a key win in this Week 17 game. The Commanders, on the other hand, will be keen to add to the most lopsided head-to-head series advantage they enjoy against any team in the league. Jaguars Coaching Staff While there were some limited staff changes, the Jaguars coaching staff returns for the 2026 season substantially the same as it was in 2025, with the same head coach and coordinators. Both OC Grant Udinski and DC Anthony Campanile had multiple interviews for head coaching positions, but both returned to Jacksonville on new contracts. That may, however, offer insight as to how the two are viewed around the NFL Head Coach : Liam Coen Offensive Coordinator : Grant Udinski Defensive Coordinator : Anthony Campanile Special Teams Coordinator : Heath Farwell The team did hire a new Defensive Pass Game Coordinator and a new Offensive Run Game Coordinator; they also promoted Shane Waldron to Assistant Head Coach and elevated Heath Farwell to Associate Head Coach.
